P2000.title: NOx Adsorber Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P2000.plain: The lean NOx trap (LNT) on bank 1 is no longer storing or releasing NOx within the required efficiency window. Detected by the downstream NOx sensor or model-based monitor — typically caused by sulphur poisoning, thermal aging, or a failed regeneration strategy.
causes: Sulphur poisoning from high-sulphur fuel — desulphation regeneration not running
Thermal aging of washcoat after high-temperature exposure

P2001.title: NOx Adsorber Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P2001.plain: The lean NOx trap (LNT) on bank 2 is no longer storing or releasing NOx within the required efficiency window. Detected by the downstream NOx sensor or model-based monitor — typically caused by sulphur poisoning, thermal aging, or a failed regeneration strategy.

P2002.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P2002.plain: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1): the control module has detected this fault condition.
causes: DPF heavily loaded — repeated short trips prevent regeneration
Filter substrate cracked or melted from runaway regeneration

P2003.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P2003.plain: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.
causes: DPF heavily loaded — repeated short trips prevent regeneration

P2004.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2004.plain: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flap on bank 1 is stuck in the open position. The IMRC swirls or tumbles intake charge at low rpm by closing one runner per cylinder; when stuck open, low-end torque drops and the engine may misfire on cold starts.
causes: IMRC actuator or vacuum motor failed

P2005.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 2)
P2005.plain: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flap on bank 2 is stuck in the open position. The IMRC swirls or tumbles intake charge at low rpm by closing one runner per cylinder; when stuck open, low-end torque drops and the engine may misfire on cold starts.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2006.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2006.plain: The IMRC flap on bank 1 is stuck in the closed position and cannot open at higher rpm. Top-end power suffers because the runner is restricted, and the engine may breathe poorly above mid-range.
causes: Actuator stuck or vacuum line collapsed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2007.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Closed (Bank 2)
P2007.plain: Bank 2 counterpart to P2006. The IMRC flap on bank 2 cannot return to the open position and chokes intake flow at higher rpm.
causes: Carbon deposits seize flap closed on bank 2
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2008.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit Open (Bank 1)
P2008.plain: The ECU detects an open circuit on the IMRC solenoid for bank 1. No control current flows when the runner is commanded to switch, leaving the flap in its default position.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2009.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2009.plain: The IMRC solenoid drive line for bank 1 reads below the lower threshold — short to ground or a failed driver stage. The runner cannot be switched on demand.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P200A.title: Intake Manifold Runner Performance (Bank 1)
P200A.plain: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) on bank 1 reports that flap movement does not match the commanded position within the allowed time window — either too slow, too short a stroke, or position feedback off-target.
causes: Actuator weak or vacuum supply low
Linkage worn — play between actuator and flap

P200B.title: Intake Manifold Runner Performance (Bank 2)
P200B.plain: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) on bank 2 reports that flap movement does not match the commanded position within the allowed time window — either too slow, too short a stroke, or position feedback off-target.

P200C.title: Particulate Filter Over Temperature (Bank 1)
P200C.plain: A temperature sensor at the diesel particulate filter (DPF) on bank 1 has exceeded the safe limit — typically during a runaway regeneration. Continued operation can melt or crack the substrate.
causes: Excessive soot load triggers runaway regeneration
DPF temperature sensor reading drifts high

P200D.title: Particulate Filter Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P200D.plain: A temperature sensor at the diesel particulate filter (DPF) on bank 2 has exceeded the safe limit — typically during a runaway regeneration. Continued operation can melt or crack the substrate.

P200E.title: Catalyst System Over Temperature (Bank 1)
P200E.plain: A temperature sensor in the exhaust catalyst on bank 1 reports a value above the safe operating limit. Sustained over-temperature can sinter the precious-metal washcoat and destroy conversion efficiency.
causes: Persistent misfire dumps unburned fuel into the cat
Sustained rich mixture from leaking injector or fuel pressure regulator

P200F.title: Catalyst System Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P200F.plain: A temperature sensor in the exhaust catalyst on bank 2 reports a value above the safe operating limit. Sustained over-temperature can sinter the precious-metal washcoat and destroy conversion efficiency.

P2010.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit High (Bank 1)
P2010.plain: Drive voltage at the IMRC solenoid on bank 1 is above the upper limit — short to supply or an open ground side. The solenoid is energised constantly or the driver protection trips.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2011.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit/Open (Bank 2)
P2011.plain: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 2 is open or has lost continuity — control module no longer detects a closing path through the actuator winding.
causes: Open wiring or chafed conductor in IMRC harness

P2012.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P2012.plain: The IMRC actuator drive line on bank 2 reads below the expected voltage threshold — typically a short to ground or a stuck-low driver inside the control module.
causes: Short to ground in driver line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2013.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2013.plain: The IMRC actuator drive line on bank 2 reads above the expected voltage threshold — typically a short to battery voltage or an open ground side.
causes: Short to B+ in driver line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2014.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit (Bank 1)
P2014.plain: The position feedback signal of the IMRC flap on bank 1 is missing or implausible. Without feedback, the ECU cannot verify that the commanded runner position has been reached.

P2015.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P2015.plain: The IMRC position sensor on bank 1 reports a value, but it does not match the commanded flap state — for example, the flap is commanded closed yet the sensor still reads open. Common on engines where the connector pin clip wears out and the sensor reads erratic positions.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2016.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2016.plain: The IMRC position sensor signal on bank 1 reads below the lower limit. Usually a short to ground on the signal wire or a failed sensor.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2017.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 1)
P2017.plain: The IMRC position sensor signal on bank 1 reads above the upper limit. Typically a short to supply, an open ground reference, or a sensor that failed high.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2018.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Open (Bank 2)
P2018.plain: The ECU detects an open circuit on the IMRC position sensor on bank 2. Without position feedback the ECU cannot confirm runner switching and falls back to a default mode.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2019.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P2019.plain: The IMRC position sensor on bank 2 produces an electrically valid signal that does not match the commanded runner state — typically a sensor drift or sticking flap.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P201A.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P201A.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Unit 1): the signal is implausible or outside the valid range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: DEF crystallisation clogs the dosing nozzle

P201B.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Actuator Supply Voltage Low (Bank 1)
P201B.plain: The supply voltage feeding the IMRC actuator on bank 1 is below the lower limit — typically a fuse, relay, or harness fault on the supply rail.

P201C.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Actuator Supply Voltage Low (Bank 2)
P201C.plain: The supply voltage feeding the IMRC actuator on bank 2 is below the lower limit — typically a fuse, relay, or harness fault on the supply rail.

P201D.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Actuator Internal Performance (Bank 1)
P201D.plain: Internal self-diagnostics of the IMRC actuator on bank 1 report an off-spec condition — driver stage, position-feedback or thermal limit no longer matches the calibrated profile.
causes: Actuator internal driver or sensor fault

P201E.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Actuator Internal Performance (Bank 2)
P201E.plain: Internal self-diagnostics of the IMRC actuator on bank 2 report an off-spec condition — driver stage, position-feedback or thermal limit no longer matches the calibrated profile.

P201F.title: Reductant Pump A Stuck On
P201F.plain: Reductant Pump A Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position.
causes: Pump driver line shorted to B+
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2020.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P2020.plain: The IMRC position sensor on bank 2 reports a voltage below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or a sensor with very low resistance.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2021.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2021.plain: The IMRC position sensor on bank 2 reports a voltage above the upper threshold — usually a short to positive or an open ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2022.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2022.plain: The IMRC position sensor on bank 2 reports a signal above the upper plausibility limit — typically an open signal line, broken sensor, or short to B+.
causes: Open signal line at IMRC position sensor

P2023.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
P2023.plain: The IMRC position sensor signal on bank 2 jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a loose pin, partially-broken conductor, or moisture in the connector.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2024.title: EVAP Fuel Vapor Temperature Sensor Circuit
P2024.plain: A general fault is reported on the EVAP fuel-vapor temperature sensor circuit — open, shorted, or out of plausible range. The sensor is part of the evaporative-emission system used to monitor canister loading.
causes: Harness fault between sensor and PCM

P2025.title: EVAP Fuel Vapor Temperature Sensor Performance
P2025.plain: The EVAP fuel-vapor temperature sensor reading is plausible but does not match expected behaviour over time or temperature — slow response, incorrect offset, or stuck reading.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P2026.title: EVAP Fuel Vapor Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Voltage
P2026.plain: The EVAP fuel-vapor temperature sensor signal sits below the lower plausibility limit — short to ground or short between signal and ground inside the sensor.
causes: Short to ground on signal line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2027.title: EVAP Fuel Vapor Temperature Sensor Circuit High Voltage
P2027.plain: The EVAP fuel-vapor temperature sensor signal sits above the upper plausibility limit — open signal line, broken sensor, or short to B+.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2028.title: EVAP Fuel Vapor Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P2028.plain: The EVAP fuel-vapor temperature sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a connector or chafed wire.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2029.title: Fuel Fired Heater Disabled
P2029.plain: The fuel-fired auxiliary heater (used to warm coolant or DEF on cold start) has been disabled by the control module — typically because of repeated start failures, low-voltage supply, or a self-protection condition.
causes: Fuel supply starved — empty tank or pump weak

P202A.title: Reductant Tank Heater Control Circuit/Open
P202A.plain: The DEF tank heater control circuit is open or has lost continuity — the PCM cannot drive the resistive heater that prevents the DEF (urea) tank from freezing in winter.
causes: Open wire between PCM and heater
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P202B.title: Reductant Tank Heater Control Circuit Low
P202B.plain: The DEF tank heater control line reads below the expected voltage — short to ground or stuck-low driver.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P202C.title: Reductant Tank Heater Control Circuit High
P202C.plain: The DEF tank heater control line reads above the expected voltage — short to B+ or open ground. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P202D.title: Reductant Leakage
P202D.plain: A leak has been detected in the DEF (urea) supply system — usually by a pressure-decay test after pump shutdown, or by visible crystallisation around fittings.

P202E.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P202E.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Unit 1): the signal is implausible or outside the valid range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P202F.title: Reductant/Regeneration Supply Control Circuit Range/Performance
P202F.plain: The control line that gates the DEF supply pump or the regeneration heating circuit does not respond as commanded — duty cycle, current draw, or response time off-spec.
causes: Supply relay aged or pitted contacts
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2030.title: Fuel Fired Heater Performance
P2030.plain: The fuel-fired auxiliary heater is operating but not delivering the expected heat output within the calibrated time — flame sensor reports weak combustion, exhaust temperature does not rise, or coolant heating rate is below threshold.
causes: Combustion chamber sooted from short cycles

P2031.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P2031.plain: The exhaust gas temperature (EGT) sensor at position 2 on bank 1 — typically downstream of the catalyst or before the DPF — reports an implausible signal. EGT sensors protect the turbocharger and DPF from over-temperature and time the regeneration cycle.

P2032.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P2032.plain: The EGT sensor at bank 1 position 2 reads below the lower limit. Common when the signal is shorted to ground or the sensor element is open.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2033.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P2033.plain: The EGT sensor at bank 1 position 2 reads above the upper limit. Usually a short to supply, an open ground or a sensor that drifted high — risk of false DPF over-temperature limp.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2034.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P2034.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on the exhaust gas temperature (EGT) sensor at bank 2 sensor 2 — open, short, or out of plausibility. EGT sensors monitor catalyst, DPF, and turbocharger inlet/outlet temperatures.

P2035.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P2035.plain: The EGT sensor on bank 2 sensor 2 reads below the lower plausibility limit — short to ground or shorted sensor element.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2036.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P2036.plain: The EGT sensor on bank 2 sensor 2 reads above the upper plausibility limit — open signal or short to B+.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2037.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P2037.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on reductant injection air-pressure sensor A — used on air-assisted DEF dosing systems to monitor the atomisation air pressure delivered to the injector.
causes: Harness fault between sensor and PCM

P2038.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P2038.plain: The reductant injection air-pressure sensor A reads inside the electrical range but does not match expected behaviour over time or load — slow response or wrong offset.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2039.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P2039.plain: The reductant injection air-pressure sensor A reads below its lower plausibility limit — short to ground or sensor internal short.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P203A.title: Reductant Level Sensor A Circuit
P203A.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on DEF level sensor A — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. Some tanks use multiple level senders to cover irregular tank shapes; this is the primary one.
causes: Sender failed — float, swing arm, or rheostat

P203B.title: Reductant Level Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P203B.plain: DEF level sensor A reading is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — value sticks, jumps, or does not match consumption.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P203C.title: Reductant Level Sensor A Circuit Low
P203C.plain: DEF level sensor A reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P203D.title: Reductant Level Sensor A Circuit High
P203D.plain: DEF level sensor A reads above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P203E.title: Reductant Level Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P203E.plain: Reductant Level Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic: the signal is intermittent or erratic. Often a loose connector or chafed wiring; a wiggle test often locates it.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P203F.title: Reductant Level Too Low
P203F.plain: The DEF tank level has dropped below the warning threshold — driver action required to refill before the inducement strategy escalates to limp mode or no-restart.
causes: DEF tank simply empty — refill needed

P2040.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P2040.plain: The reductant injection air-pressure sensor A reads above its upper plausibility limit — open signal line or short to B+.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2041.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P2041.plain: The reductant injection air-pressure sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or harness issue.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2042.title: Reductant Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P2042.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on reductant (DEF) temperature sensor A — used to compensate dosing for fluid viscosity and to enable tank heating in winter.

P2043.title: Reductant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P2043.plain: Reductant temperature sensor A reading is within electrical range but plausibility check fails — slow response or sticks at one value through a tank-warming cycle.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2044.title: Reductant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P2044.plain: Reductant temperature sensor A reads below its lower plausibility limit — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2045.title: Reductant Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P2045.plain: Reductant temperature sensor A reads above its upper plausibility limit — open signal or short to B+.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2046.title: Reductant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P2046.plain: Reductant temperature sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or harness fault.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2047.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P2047.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Unit 1): the circuit is open. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Open wire between PCM and valve

P2048.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P2048.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 1 Unit 1): the signal voltage is below the expected range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2049.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit High (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P2049.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit High (Bank 1 Unit 1): the signal voltage is above the expected range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P204A.title: Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit
P204A.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on the DEF system pressure sensor — used to verify pump priming, line pressure, and to detect leaks via pressure-decay tests.

P204B.title: Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P204B.plain: DEF pressure sensor reads within electrical range but plausibility fails — does not rise during prime, drift over a drive cycle, or stuck at a constant value.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P204C.title: Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P204C.plain: DEF pressure sensor reads below the lower plausibility limit — short to ground or sensor element shorted.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P204D.title: Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P204D.plain: DEF pressure sensor reads above the upper plausibility limit — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P204E.title: Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P204E.plain: DEF pressure sensor signal is unstable or jumps — usually a connector or chafed wire. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P204F.title: Reductant System Performance
P204F.plain: The SCR (selective catalytic reduction) system using AdBlue/DEF is not delivering the expected NOx conversion. Causes range from poor reductant quality, dosing module faults, heater failure on the AdBlue tank in cold weather, or a degraded SCR catalyst.
causes: Dosing module clogged with urea crystals

P2050.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P2050.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Unit 1): the circuit is open. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2051.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P2051.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 2 Unit 1): the signal voltage is below the expected range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2052.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit High (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P2052.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit High (Bank 2 Unit 1): the signal voltage is above the expected range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2053.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Unit 2)
P2053.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Unit 2): the circuit is open. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2054.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 1 Unit 2)
P2054.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 1 Unit 2): the signal voltage is below the expected range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2055.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit High (Bank 1 Unit 2)
P2055.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit High (Bank 1 Unit 2): the signal voltage is above the expected range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2056.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Unit 2)
P2056.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Unit 2): the circuit is open. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2057.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 2 Unit 2)
P2057.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 2 Unit 2): the signal voltage is below the expected range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2058.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit High (Bank 2 Unit 2)
P2058.plain: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit High (Bank 2 Unit 2): the signal voltage is above the expected range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2059.title: Reductant Injection Air Pump Control Circuit/Open
P2059.plain: Reductant Injection Air Pump Control Circuit/Open: the control circuit is open. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P205A.title: Reductant Tank Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P205A.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on DEF tank temperature sensor A — separate from the metering-unit temperature sensor and used to gate tank-heating.

P205B.title: Reductant Tank Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P205B.plain: DEF tank temperature sensor A reads within electrical range but plausibility fails — sensor sticks during a heating cycle.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P205C.title: Reductant Tank Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P205C.plain: DEF tank temperature sensor A reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P205D.title: Reductant Tank Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P205D.plain: DEF tank temperature sensor A reads above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P205E.title: Reductant Tank Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P205E.plain: DEF tank temperature sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or harness issue.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P205F.title: Reductant System Performance (Bank 2)
P205F.plain: The DEF system as a whole on bank 2 is not delivering the required NOx reduction — NOx-out remains too high relative to commanded dosing across a drive cycle. Causes range from poor DEF quality, restricted dosing line, weak pump, to a degraded SCR catalyst.
causes: Poor DEF quality — diluted or contaminated

P2060.title: Reductant Injection Air Pump Control Circuit Low
P2060.plain: Reductant Injection Air Pump Control Circuit Low: the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2061.title: Reductant Injection Air Pump Control Circuit High
P2061.plain: Reductant Injection Air Pump Control Circuit High: the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2062.title: Reductant/Regeneration Supply Control Circuit/Open
P2062.plain: The control line that energises the DEF supply pump or regeneration heating circuit is open — no continuity through the load or harness.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2063.title: Reductant/Regeneration Supply Control Circuit Low
P2063.plain: Reductant/regeneration supply control line stuck low — short to ground or stuck-low driver. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2064.title: Reductant/Regeneration Supply Control Circuit High
P2064.plain: Reductant/regeneration supply control line stuck high — short to B+ or open ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2065.title: Fuel Level Sensor B Circuit
P2065.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on the secondary fuel-level sensor (B) — vehicles with saddle tanks or auxiliary tanks use a second sender to cover the full tank volume.
causes: Sender failed — float, swing arm, or rheostat

P2066.title: Fuel Level Sensor B Performance
P2066.plain: Secondary fuel-level sensor B reads within range but plausibility check fails — value sticks, jumps, or does not match consumption.

P2067.title: Fuel Level Sensor B Circuit Low
P2067.plain: Fuel-level sensor B reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2068.title: Fuel Level Sensor B Circuit High
P2068.plain: Fuel-level sensor B reads above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2069.title: Fuel Level Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P2069.plain: Fuel-level sensor B signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a corroded sender or wiring. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P206A.title: Reductant Quality Sensor Circuit
P206A.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on the DEF (urea) quality sensor — measures urea concentration via ultrasonic or refractive method to detect water dilution or wrong fluid.

P206B.title: Reductant Quality Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P206B.plain: DEF quality sensor reads in range but reports an off-spec urea concentration — typically diluted DEF or non-DEF fluid in the tank.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P206C.title: Reductant Quality Sensor Circuit Low
P206C.plain: DEF quality sensor reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P206D.title: Reductant Quality Sensor Circuit High
P206D.plain: DEF quality sensor reads above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P206E.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2)
P206E.plain: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P206F.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 2)
P206F.plain: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2070.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2070.plain: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1): the control module has detected this fault condition.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2071.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2071.plain: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 1): the control module has detected this fault condition.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2072.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Ice Blockage (Bank 1)
P2072.plain: The electronic throttle on bank 1 is jammed by ice — typical at very low ambient temperatures with high humidity, after a short trip that did not warm the throttle housing. The strategy attempts a self-clearing motion before setting the code.
causes: Throttle housing coolant warming circuit blocked

P2073.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure / Mass Air Flow - Throttle Position Correlation at Idle
P2073.plain: At idle, the relationship between MAP/MAF and throttle position does not match the calibrated map — typically a vacuum leak, dirty MAF, sticking throttle plate, or sensor drift.
causes: Vacuum leak — cracked hose, gasket, or PCV

P2074.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure / Mass Air Flow - Throttle Position Correlation at Higher Load
P2074.plain: At higher load, the relationship between MAP/MAF and throttle position does not match the calibrated map — typically a charge-air leak, restricted intake, or wide-open MAF underread.

P2075.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit (Bank 1)
P2075.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on the IMT valve position sensor at bank 1 — open, short, or out of plausibility.

P2076.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P2076.plain: IMT valve position sensor at bank 1 reads in range but plausibility check fails — value sticks or does not match commanded position.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2077.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2077.plain: IMT position sensor at bank 1 reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2078.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 1)
P2078.plain: IMT position sensor at bank 1 reads above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2079.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1)
P2079.plain: IMT position sensor at bank 1 signal is unstable — connector or harness issue. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P207A.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit (Bank 2)
P207A.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on the IMT valve position sensor at bank 2 — open, short, or out of plausibility.

P207B.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P207B.plain: IMT valve position sensor at bank 2 reads in range but plausibility check fails — value sticks or does not match commanded position.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P207C.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P207C.plain: IMT position sensor at bank 2 reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P207D.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 2)
P207D.plain: IMT position sensor at bank 2 reads above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P207E.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
P207E.plain: IMT position sensor at bank 2 signal is unstable — connector or harness issue. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P207F.title: Reductant Quality Performance
P207F.plain: The ECU has concluded that the AdBlue/DEF in the tank does not meet specification. Diagnosed by comparing expected NOx reduction against the dosed reductant volume — too much dosing for too little NOx drop indicates diluted or wrong fluid.
causes: AdBlue diluted with water or wrong fluid filled
NOx sensor drift gives false reductant-quality verdict

P2080.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2080.plain: The pre-catalyst EGT sensor on bank 1 returns a value that does not match the expected temperature curve under load. Often slow response time after long service life or a contaminated tip.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2081.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2081.plain: The EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 signal jumps or drops out intermittently — typically a connector or chafed wire near the exhaust manifold heat zone.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2082.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2082.plain: The EGT sensor at bank 2 sensor 1 reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response, stuck reading, or value does not track other EGT sensors during a regeneration.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2083.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2083.plain: The EGT sensor at bank 2 sensor 1 signal jumps or drops out intermittently — typically a connector or chafed wire near the exhaust manifold heat zone.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2084.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P2084.plain: The bank 1 sensor 2 EGT reading deviates from the expected ratio against the upstream EGT sensor or modeled exhaust temperature. Confuses DPF regeneration control and may force a forced regen.
causes: DPF heavily loaded — non-physical temperature gradient
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2085.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P2085.plain: The EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 2 signal jumps or drops out intermittently — typically a connector or chafed wire near the exhaust manifold heat zone.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2086.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P2086.plain: The EGT sensor at bank 2 sensor 2 reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response, stuck reading, or value does not track other EGT sensors during a regeneration.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2087.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P2087.plain: The EGT sensor at bank 2 sensor 2 signal jumps or drops out intermittently — typically a connector or chafed wire near the exhaust manifold heat zone.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2088.title: Camshaft Position A Actuator Control Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2088.plain: Drive voltage to the intake VVT oil control valve on bank 1 reads below the lower limit. Usually a short to ground or a coil shorted internally.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2089.title: Camshaft Position A Actuator Control Circuit High (Bank 1)
P2089.plain: Drive voltage to the intake VVT oil control valve on bank 1 is above the upper limit — short to supply or open ground side. The solenoid is energised constantly or the driver protection trips.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P208A.title: Reductant Pump A Control Circuit/Open
P208A.plain: The control line driving DEF pump A is open — no continuity through the motor or harness, dosing pressure cannot be built.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P208B.title: Reductant Pump A Control Performance/Stuck Off
P208B.plain: DEF pump A receives a run command but does not start, or shuts off prematurely — pump performance is below threshold.
causes: Pump motor seized — DEF crystallised inside pump head
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P208C.title: Reductant Pump A Control Circuit Low
P208C.plain: DEF pump A control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P208D.title: Reductant Pump A Control Circuit High
P208D.plain: DEF pump A control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P208E.title: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P208E.plain: The DEF injection valve at bank 1 unit 1 does not open when commanded — typically crystallised DEF blocks the nozzle, no flow into the SCR.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P208F.title: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P208F.plain: The DEF injection valve at bank 2 unit 1 does not open when commanded — typically crystallised DEF blocks the nozzle, no flow into the SCR.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2090.title: Camshaft Position B Actuator Control Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2090.plain: Drive voltage to the exhaust VVT oil control valve on bank 1 is below the lower limit. Same failure pattern as P2088 but for the exhaust cam phaser.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2091.title: Camshaft Position B Actuator Control Circuit High (Bank 1)
P2091.plain: Drive voltage to the exhaust VVT oil control valve on bank 1 is above the upper limit. Mirror image of P2089 on the exhaust cam side.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2092.title: A Camshaft Position Actuator Control Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P2092.plain: The intake (A) camshaft phaser solenoid drive line on bank 2 is stuck low — short to ground or stuck-low driver. Variable-valve timing on intake bank 2 cannot be modulated.
causes: Short to ground in solenoid drive line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2093.title: A Camshaft Position Actuator Control Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2093.plain: The intake (A) camshaft phaser solenoid drive line on bank 2 is stuck high — short to B+ or open ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2094.title: B Camshaft Position Actuator Control Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P2094.plain: The exhaust (B) camshaft phaser solenoid drive line on bank 2 is stuck low — short to ground or stuck-low driver.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2095.title: B Camshaft Position Actuator Control Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2095.plain: The exhaust (B) camshaft phaser solenoid drive line on bank 2 is stuck high — short to B+ or open ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2096.title: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Lean (Bank 1)
P2096.plain: Long-term fuel trim derived from the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 has reached the lean limit. The downstream-trim correction is a fine adjustment that runs after the main trim from the upstream sensor; persistent excursion suggests a degraded catalyst, an exhaust leak after the catalyst, or a drifting downstream sensor.
causes: Exhaust leak after catalyst (post-cat sensor sees ambient air)

P2097.title: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Rich (Bank 1)
P2097.plain: Long-term post-catalyst fuel trim on bank 1 has reached its rich limit. The downstream sensor sees more reductant than expected, often pointing to a degraded catalyst that no longer stores oxygen, or a failing downstream sensor biased rich.

P2098.title: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Lean (Bank 2)
P2098.plain: Bank 2 counterpart of P2096. The post-catalyst fuel trim correction on bank 2 has reached its lean limit, suggesting an exhaust leak after the bank 2 catalyst, a drifting downstream sensor, or a degraded catalyst.

P2099.title: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Rich (Bank 2)
P2099.plain: Bank 2 counterpart of P2097. Post-catalyst trim on bank 2 has reached the rich limit — usually a depleted catalyst or a downstream sensor biased rich on the bank 2 side.

P209A.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P209A.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on reductant injection air-pressure sensor B — the second air-assist pressure sensor on dual-bank or dual-injector DEF systems.

P209B.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P209B.plain: The reductant injection air-pressure sensor B reads inside the electrical range but does not match expected behaviour over time or load — slow response or wrong offset.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P209C.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P209C.plain: The reductant injection air-pressure sensor B reads below its lower plausibility limit — short to ground or sensor internal short.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P209D.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P209D.plain: The reductant injection air-pressure sensor B reads above its upper plausibility limit — open signal line or short to B+.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P209E.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor A/B Correlation
P209E.plain: The two reductant injection air-pressure sensors A and B disagree by more than the allowed tolerance — one is reading off, or there is a real pressure imbalance between the two air-assist branches.
causes: One sensor drifts relative to the other

P209F.title: Reductant Tank Heater Control Circuit Performance
P209F.plain: DEF tank heater is electrically OK but does not warm the tank within the expected time — element is partially open, fluid level too low for proper heat transfer, or the heater is undersized for the ambient temperature.
causes: DEF level too low for heat transfer

P20A0.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve A Circuit/Open
P20A0.plain: The reductant purge control valve A drive circuit is open — used to evacuate DEF lines back to the tank when the engine is shut down to prevent freezing damage.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P20A1.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve A Performance
P20A1.plain: Reductant purge control valve A is electrically OK but does not vent the line within the expected time — partial blockage or weakened solenoid.

P20A2.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve A Circuit Low
P20A2.plain: Reductant purge control valve A drive line stuck low — short to ground. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20A3.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve A Circuit High
P20A3.plain: Reductant purge control valve A drive line stuck high — short to B+. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20A4.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve A Stuck Open
P20A4.plain: Reductant purge control valve A is mechanically stuck open — system cannot maintain dosing pressure because the line is constantly vented to the tank.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20A5.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve A Stuck Closed
P20A5.plain: Reductant purge control valve A is mechanically stuck closed — DEF lines cannot be vented at shutdown, increasing risk of freeze damage in winter.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20A6.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Control Valve Circuit/Open
P20A6.plain: The drive circuit for the air-assist pressure-control valve in the DEF system is open — atomisation pressure cannot be regulated, dosing accuracy degrades.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P20A7.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Control Valve Performance
P20A7.plain: Reductant air-pressure control valve is electrically OK but cannot hold or modulate pressure within calibration — partial blockage or weak solenoid.

P20A8.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Control Valve Circuit Low
P20A8.plain: Reductant air-pressure control valve drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20A9.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Control Valve Circuit High
P20A9.plain: Reductant air-pressure control valve drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20AA.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Control Valve Stuck Open
P20AA.plain: Reductant air-pressure control valve mechanically stuck open — air pressure cannot be reduced, dosing atomisation off-spec.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20AB.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Control Valve Stuck Closed
P20AB.plain: Reductant air-pressure control valve mechanically stuck closed — air supply blocked, dosing fails.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20AC.title: Reductant Metering Unit Temperature Sensor Circuit
P20AC.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on the temperature sensor inside the DEF metering unit — used to protect the unit from over-temperature and to compensate for fluid viscosity.

P20AD.title: Reductant Metering Unit Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P20AD.plain: Metering unit temperature sensor in range but fails plausibility — slow response or stuck reading. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P20AE.title: Reductant Metering Unit Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P20AE.plain: Metering unit temperature sensor below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20AF.title: Reductant Metering Unit Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P20AF.plain: Metering unit temperature sensor above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20B0.title: Reductant Metering Unit Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P20B0.plain: Metering unit temperature sensor signal jumps or drops out — connector or harness issue. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P20B1.title: Reductant Heater Coolant Control Valve Circuit/Open
P20B1.plain: The drive circuit for the engine-coolant control valve that warms the DEF tank/lines is open — coolant cannot be routed to the heating loop.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P20B2.title: Reductant Heater Coolant Control Valve Performance/Stuck Open
P20B2.plain: Reductant coolant control valve is electrically OK but stuck open or does not modulate as commanded — DEF heating loop loses control authority.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20B3.title: Reductant Heater Coolant Control Valve Circuit Low
P20B3.plain: Reductant coolant control valve drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20B4.title: Reductant Heater Coolant Control Valve Circuit High
P20B4.plain: Reductant coolant control valve drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20B5.title: Reductant Metering Unit Heater Control Circuit/Open
P20B5.plain: The control circuit for the heater inside the DEF metering unit is open — winter operation cannot keep the dosing block above freezing.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P20B6.title: Reductant Metering Unit Heater Control Circuit Performance
P20B6.plain: Metering unit heater is electrically OK but does not warm the block within the expected time — partial winding fault or excessive heat loss.

P20B7.title: Reductant Metering Unit Heater Control Circuit Low
P20B7.plain: Metering unit heater control line stuck low — short to ground. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20B8.title: Reductant Metering Unit Heater Control Circuit High
P20B8.plain: Metering unit heater control line stuck high — short to B+. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20B9.title: Reductant Heater A Control Circuit/Open
P20B9.plain: Reductant heater A (typically the supply line heater nearest the tank) control circuit is open — that segment of DEF line will not be kept above freezing in winter.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P20BA.title: Reductant Heater A Control Performance
P20BA.plain: The reductant (AdBlue/DEF) tank or line heater A does not reach the expected temperature within the calibrated time window. In cold weather frozen DEF blocks the SCR dosing system and the engine enters a no-restart state after ignored warnings.

P20BB.title: Reductant Heater A Control Circuit Low
P20BB.plain: Reductant heater A control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20BC.title: Reductant Heater A Control Circuit High
P20BC.plain: Reductant heater A control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20BD.title: Reductant Heater B Control Circuit/Open
P20BD.plain: Reductant heater B (next supply-line segment) control circuit open — that line segment will not be kept above freezing.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P20BE.title: Reductant Heater B Control Circuit Performance
P20BE.plain: Reductant heater B is electrically OK but does not warm the line in time — partial winding fault or excessive heat loss.

P20BF.title: Reductant Heater B Control Circuit Low
P20BF.plain: Reductant heater B control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20C0.title: Reductant Heater B Control Circuit High
P20C0.plain: Reductant heater B control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20C1.title: Reductant Heater C Control Circuit/Open
P20C1.plain: Reductant heater C control circuit open.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P20C2.title: Reductant Heater C Control Circuit Performance
P20C2.plain: Reductant heater C does not warm in time — partial fault.

P20C3.title: Reductant Heater C Control Circuit Low
P20C3.plain: Reductant heater C control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20C4.title: Reductant Heater C Control Circuit High
P20C4.plain: Reductant heater C control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20C5.title: Reductant Heater D Control Circuit/Open
P20C5.plain: Reductant heater D control circuit open.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P20C6.title: Reductant Heater D Control Circuit Performance
P20C6.plain: Reductant heater D does not warm in time.

P20C7.title: Reductant Heater D Control Circuit Low
P20C7.plain: Reductant heater D control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20C8.title: Reductant Heater D Control Circuit High
P20C8.plain: Reductant heater D control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20C9.title: Reductant Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P20C9.plain: The dedicated reductant/SCR control module has requested that the master PCM illuminate the malfunction indicator lamp — a generic forward of an internal SCR fault. Read the SCR module subcodes for the actual cause.
causes: Internal SCR module fault — read subcodes

P20CA.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Leakage
P20CA.plain: A leak has been detected in the air-assist branch of the DEF system — pressure decays faster than allowed when the air pump shuts off.
causes: Air pressure control valve seat leaks

P20CB.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Control Circuit/Open
P20CB.plain: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Control Circuit/Open: the control circuit is open. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P20CC.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Control Performance
P20CC.plain: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Control Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.

P20CD.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Control Circuit Low
P20CD.plain: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Control Circuit Low: the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20CE.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Control Circuit High
P20CE.plain: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Control Circuit High: the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20CF.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Stuck Open
P20CF.plain: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Stuck Open: the control module has detected this fault condition. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20D0.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Stuck Closed
P20D0.plain: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Stuck Closed: the control module has detected this fault condition. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20D1.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit/Open
P20D1.plain: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit/Open: the control circuit is open. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P20D2.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Performance
P20D2.plain: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.

P20D3.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit Low
P20D3.plain: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit Low: the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20D4.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit High
P20D4.plain: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit High: the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20D5.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Open
P20D5.plain: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Open: the control module has detected this fault condition. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20D6.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Closed
P20D6.plain: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Closed: the control module has detected this fault condition. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20D7.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit/Open
P20D7.plain: The control circuit for the dedicated aftertreatment fuel supply pump or solenoid is open — HC dosing into the exhaust will fail.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P20D8.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Performance
P20D8.plain: Aftertreatment fuel supply is electrically OK but does not deliver the commanded pressure or flow during regeneration — weak pump or partial blockage.
causes: Pump weak — flow or pressure below threshold

P20D9.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit Low
P20D9.plain: Aftertreatment fuel supply control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20DA.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit High
P20DA.plain: Aftertreatment fuel supply control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20DB.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Stuck Open
P20DB.plain: Aftertreatment fuel supply solenoid stuck open mechanically — fuel pressure cannot be cut off, risk of over-fueling exhaust.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20DC.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Stuck Closed
P20DC.plain: Aftertreatment fuel supply solenoid stuck closed — HC dosing into exhaust fails, regeneration cannot raise temperature.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20DD.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit
P20DD.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on the aftertreatment fuel-pressure sensor — used to verify the dedicated HC-dosing rail is primed.

P20DE.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P20DE.plain: Aftertreatment fuel-pressure sensor reads in range but plausibility fails — pressure does not rise during prime, drift across a regeneration.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P20DF.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P20DF.plain: Aftertreatment fuel-pressure sensor below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20E0.title: Reductant Pressure Too Low
P20E0.plain: The pressure in the SCR reductant (AdBlue/DEF) line is below the calibrated minimum. Without sufficient pressure the dosing module cannot atomise reagent properly, leading to NOx exceedence.

P20E1.title: Reductant Pressure Too Low
P20E1.plain: The reductant (AdBlue/DEF) line pressure stays below the demanded value during dosing. The dosing system needs a stable supply pressure to inject metered amounts; without it the system cannot meet NOx targets.

P20E2.title: Reductant Pressure Too High
P20E2.plain: The reductant line pressure exceeds the upper limit. A blocked return path, a stuck pump or a faulty pressure sensor are common causes; over-pressure can damage the dosing valve and the pump head.

P20E3.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/3 Correlation (Bank 1)
P20E3.plain: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/3 Correlation (Bank 1): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.
causes: Exhaust leak between the two sensor positions

P20E4.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 2/3 Correlation (Bank 1)
P20E4.plain: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 2/3 Correlation (Bank 1): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

P20E5.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 2)
P20E5.plain: EGT sensors 1 and 3 on bank 2 disagree by more than the allowed tolerance — one is reading off, or there is a real temperature gradient that exceeds the calibrated map (e.g. from a leaking exhaust joint between the two locations).

P20E6.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Too Low
P20E6.plain: The DEF system air-assist pressure is below the required threshold — pump weak, line leak, or pressure-control valve stuck open.

P20E7.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Too High
P20E7.plain: The DEF system air-assist pressure exceeds the upper threshold — pressure-control valve stuck closed or air pump runaway.

P20E8.title: Reductant Pressure Too Low
P20E8.plain: Pressure in the AdBlue/DEF supply line is below the target. Usually a failing reductant pump, a clogged filter, frozen lines, or a leak in the pressurised circuit.

P20E9.title: Reductant Pressure Too High
P20E9.plain: Manufacturer-specific variant of the reductant over-pressure condition. The pressure exceeds the upper threshold during a defined operating window; on some platforms used in addition to P20E2 to flag a different test path.

P20EA.title: Reductant Pump Control Circuit Open
P20EA.plain: The control circuit to the reductant (DEF) dosing pump is open — no current flow detected. Without pump pressure no AdBlue reaches the SCR catalyst and NOx reduction stops.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P20EB.title: Reductant Reservoir Heater "A" Control Circuit
P20EB.plain: A general electrical fault on the reductant tank heater "A" control circuit. AdBlue freezes at -11 C, so the tank heater must work for cold-start dosing.

P20EC.title: Reductant Heater "A" Control Stuck Off
P20EC.plain: The reductant tank heater "A" does not heat when commanded on. Either a failed element or a stuck-off driver in the dosing module.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P20ED.title: Reductant Heater "A" Control Stuck On
P20ED.plain: The reductant tank heater "A" stays energised even when not commanded — usually a shorted driver stage. Continuous heating wastes current and can overheat the heater element.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P20EE.title: NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P20EE.plain: The SCR catalyst on bank 1 is no longer reducing NOx to the level the ECU expects, even with proper reductant dosing and quality. Often the result of catalyst poisoning by sulphur or hydrocarbons, thermal aging, or a leak between the upstream and downstream NOx sensors.
causes: Exhaust leak between upstream and downstream NOx sensors

P20EF.title: Reductant Injection Valve Performance
P20EF.plain: The SCR reductant injection valve does not deliver the commanded amount of reagent. Causes include clogging by urea crystals, electrical faults or incorrect spray pattern.

P20F0.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P20F0.plain: SCR NOx Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2): the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.

P20F1.title: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P20F1.plain: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2): the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.

P20F2.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P20F2.plain: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.
causes: Catalyst poisoning from sulphur or oil ash

P20F3.title: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P20F3.plain: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.

P20F4.title: Reductant Consumption Too Low
P20F4.plain: The DEF consumption observed over the dosing window is below the model expectation — typically a clogged dosing nozzle, weak pump, or leak between pump and injector that recirculates DEF back to the tank.
causes: Dosing nozzle clogged with crystallised DEF

P20F5.title: Reductant Consumption Too High
P20F5.plain: The DEF consumption observed over the dosing window is above the model expectation — typically a leaking injector seat, leaking line fitting, or a pressure-control valve that vents constantly to the tank.
causes: Injector seat leaks DEF into exhaust

P20F6.title: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P20F6.plain: The DEF injection valve at bank 1 unit 1 does not close when commanded — DEF flows continuously into the SCR. Risk of crystallisation in the catalyst and over-dosing.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P20F7.title: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2 Unit 1)
