P20F7.plain: The DEF injection valve at bank 2 unit 1 does not close when commanded — DEF flows continuously into the SCR. Risk of crystallisation in the catalyst and over-dosing.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20F8.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 1)
P20F8.plain: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 1 is electrically OK but its current draw or duty-cycle response is outside the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or a partially shorted driver.

P20F9.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 2)
P20F9.plain: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 2 is electrically OK but its current draw or duty-cycle response is outside the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or a partially shorted driver.

P20FA.title: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit/Open
P20FA.plain: The control line driving DEF pump B is open. On large engines or dual-tank systems a second pump (B) supplements pump A; with B offline the system loses redundancy.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P20FB.title: Reductant Pump B Control Performance/Stuck Off
P20FB.plain: DEF pump B receives a run command but does not start, or shuts off prematurely.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20FC.title: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P20FC.plain: DEF pump B control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20FD.title: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit High
P20FD.plain: DEF pump B control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20FE.title: Reductant Metering Unit 1 Performance
P20FE.plain: The first DEF metering unit (the integrated module that combines pump, filter, level sensor, and dosing valve) is electrically OK but does not deliver the expected pressure or flow during operation.
causes: Metering unit aged or partially clogged

P20FF.title: Reductant Control Module Performance
P20FF.plain: The dedicated SCR/reductant control module reports an internal performance fault — failed self-tests, watchdog resets, or calibration mismatch. Frequently a forerunner of total module failure.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P2100.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Open
P2100.plain: The drive-by-wire throttle motor circuit is open — no current flow detected. The ECU loses authority over the throttle plate and forces a limp-home with reduced power.

P2101.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P2101.plain: The throttle motor responds, but its actual position does not track the commanded position within tolerance. Often a dirty throttle bore where the plate sticks, or a worn motor.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2102.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Low
P2102.plain: Drive voltage to the throttle motor is below the lower limit. Typically a short to ground or a failed driver stage in the ECU.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2103.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit High
P2103.plain: Drive voltage to the throttle motor is above the upper limit. Usually a short to supply or an open ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2104.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Idle
P2104.plain: The ECU has detected a fault severe enough that it forces the throttle actuator to the idle stop. The driver loses pedal authority — only idle is available until the underlying TAC fault clears.

P2105.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Engine Shutdown
P2105.plain: The TAC monitor commanded an engine shutdown because throttle authority can no longer be guaranteed safely. The most aggressive TAC limp mode — used when both throttle position sensors disagree or the motor is uncontrollable.
causes: TPS1 and TPS2 disagree beyond limit

P2106.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Limited Power
P2106.plain: The TAC monitor restricts maximum throttle opening as a safety response to a TAC fault. The vehicle can still be driven, but accelerator pedal travel is capped.

P2107.title: Throttle Actuator Control Module Internal Processor
P2107.plain: The internal processor or watchdog of the throttle actuator control module reports an internal fault. Communication between the TAC monitor core and the main ECU core has failed plausibility — typical for a defective ECU.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P2108.title: Throttle Actuator Control Module Performance
P2108.plain: Self-tests within the TAC module fail their performance criteria — for example RAM/ROM checks or analog reference voltages drift. Indicates an aging ECU rather than a wiring fault.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P2109.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Minimum Stop Performance
P2109.plain: The ECU detects that the throttle position sensor A signal at the closed-throttle stop does not match the learned minimum value. The mechanical or electrical zero reference of the throttle has drifted out of the expected range, often after cleaning, replacement or wear.

P210A.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit/Open
P210A.plain: The drive circuit of throttle actuator motor B is open. Throttle B is the secondary throttle on engines with two throttle bodies — typically used for tumble flap or charge-motion control.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P210B.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P210B.plain: Throttle actuator B motor responds electrically but does not move the throttle plate as commanded — typically high-resistance brushes, partial winding fault, or a sticky throttle bore.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P210C.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Low
P210C.plain: Throttle actuator B motor drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P210D.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit High
P210D.plain: Throttle actuator B motor drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P210E.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C/F Voltage Correlation
P210E.plain: The redundant throttle or accelerator pedal position channels C and F disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. Drive-by-wire systems compare two or three independent channels to detect a faulty potentiometer track.
causes: One potentiometer track worn — voltage drift

P210F.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Forced Limited RPM
P210F.plain: Throttle B control has detected an unsafe condition and forced an RPM limit. Common protective response when motor current, throttle position feedback, or supply voltage on the B path is out of spec.
causes: Protection mode triggered by paired throttle-B fault

P2110.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Limited RPM
P2110.plain: The TAC monitor caps engine speed at a fixed limp-home rpm because it can no longer trust the throttle response. Driver may notice a hard rev limit well below redline.
causes: Underlying TAC fault triggers rpm cap
Throttle response time out of spec

P2111.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Stuck Open
P2111.plain: The throttle plate cannot be commanded back to the closed/idle position. Idle speed runs high or the engine cannot decelerate properly — safety-critical fault that usually triggers immediate limp mode.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2112.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Stuck Closed
P2112.plain: The throttle plate cannot be commanded open. The engine stays at idle or stalls under load. Often caused by a seized motor, broken gear, or heavy carbon coking inside the throttle bore.
causes: Throttle motor seized or gear broken
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2113.title: Throttle Actuator Control System Forced Limited RPM
P2113.plain: The throttle actuator control has detected a fault and limits engine speed to a defined emergency value. The vehicle stays drivable but with severely reduced power until the underlying fault is cleared.

P2114.title: Throttle Actuator Control System Forced Below Limit RPM
P2114.plain: The throttle actuator system has dropped engine speed below the normal limp limit because of a more serious fault. The engine may run only at idle or stall.

P2115.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Minimum Stop Performance
P2115.plain: The minimum stop calibration of throttle position sensor A is outside the expected range during the ECU self-check. The signal at fully closed throttle does not match the stored reference, indicating a mechanical or sensor issue.
causes: Throttle plate sticking due to carbon

P2116.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Minimum Stop Performance
P2116.plain: The minimum stop calibration of throttle position sensor B does not match the learned reference during ECU self-test. Sensor B is the redundant channel used to cross-check sensor A.

P2117.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Minimum Stop Performance
P2117.plain: The minimum stop signal from throttle/pedal position sensor C is out of specification during initialization. Used on systems with three redundant sensor channels for safety-critical drive-by-wire control.

P2118.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P2118.plain: The current draw of the throttle motor lies outside the expected range — either much higher (binding plate) or much lower (worn brushes, open winding) than calibrated.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2119.title: Throttle Closed Position Performance
P2119.plain: When commanded to idle, the throttle plate does not reach the calibrated closed position. Often a coked throttle bore preventing the plate from seating fully.
causes: Throttle bore coked at closed-position stop
Plate or stop misadjusted after service

P211A.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Open
P211A.plain: Throttle B is mechanically stuck open — typically carbon buildup or a broken return spring on the secondary throttle plate.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P211B.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Closed
P211B.plain: Throttle B is mechanically stuck closed — carbon buildup or a seized bearing on the secondary throttle.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P211C.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P211C.plain: Throttle B motor current draw does not match the calibrated map for the commanded position — high friction, partial short, or stiction.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P211D.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Throttle Body Range/Performance
P211D.plain: The throttle B body itself does not respond as commanded — position feedback is plausible but does not track the setpoint within the calibrated time window.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P211E.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Processor
P211E.plain: The processor monitoring throttle B inside the throttle/PCM has reported a self-test failure — RAM check, ROM check, or watchdog timeout.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P211F.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Performance
P211F.plain: The throttle control module on the B path reports general performance issues — internal fault, communication mismatch, or calibration drift.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P2120.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Circuit
P2120.plain: A general electrical fault on the "C" channel of the throttle or pedal position sensor. Drive-by-wire pedals carry two or three redundant tracks; "C" is the third channel.

P2121.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Range/Performance
P2121.plain: The "C" channel of the throttle or pedal sensor produces an electrically valid signal that does not match the other channels or the operating point.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2122.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit Low
P2122.plain: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2123.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit High
P2123.plain: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2124.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Circuit Low
P2124.plain: The "C" channel signal is below the lower threshold — usually a short to ground or an open signal wire.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2125.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Circuit High
P2125.plain: The "C" channel signal is above the upper threshold — typically a short to positive or an open ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2126.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Circuit Intermittent
P2126.plain: The "C" channel produces an intermittent signal — usually a marginal connector or a worn track inside the pedal sensor.
causes: Track C worn at common pedal angle

P2127.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit Low
P2127.plain: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2128.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit High
P2128.plain: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2129.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit Intermittent
P2129.plain: The "D" channel of the throttle or pedal sensor produces an intermittent signal — typically marginal connector contacts.

P212A.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit
P212A.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on throttle position sensor G — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. Sensor G is part of a multi-channel redundancy on dual-throttle systems.

P212B.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Range/Performance
P212B.plain: TPS G reads in range but plausibility check fails — value sticks, lags, or does not match the commanded throttle position.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P212C.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Low
P212C.plain: TPS G below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P212D.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit High
P212D.plain: TPS G above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P212E.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Intermittent
P212E.plain: TPS G signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or harness issue. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P212F.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F/G Voltage Correlation
P212F.plain: Channels F and G of the throttle/pedal position sensor disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. Drive-by-wire system has lost redundancy and may force limp mode.

P2130.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F Circuit
P2130.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on throttle/pedal position sensor F — open, shorted, or out of plausibility.

P2131.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Range/Performance
P2131.plain: The "E" channel of the pedal/throttle sensor produces electrically valid values that do not match other channels or the operating window.
causes: Track E worn at common angle
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2132.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit Low
P2132.plain: The "E" channel signal is below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or an open signal wire.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2133.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit High
P2133.plain: The "E" channel signal is above the upper threshold — usually a short to positive or an open ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2134.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F Circuit Intermittent
P2134.plain: TPS/APP sensor F signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2135.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A"/"B" Voltage Correlation
P2135.plain: The two redundant throttle position sensors on the throttle body disagree by more than allowed. Distinct from P2138 which monitors the pedal pair — P2135 monitors the throttle-body pair on drive-by-wire systems.

P2136.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A/C Voltage Correlation
P2136.plain: The "A" and "C" channels of the throttle or pedal sensor disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. The ECU cannot trust either reading and forces limp-home with reduced torque.

P2137.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B/C Voltage Correlation
P2137.plain: The "B" and "C" channels of the throttle or pedal sensor disagree beyond tolerance — the ECU cannot trust either signal and reverts to limp-home.

P2138.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D"/"E" Voltage Correlation
P2138.plain: The two redundant accelerator pedal position sensors disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. The ECU cannot trust either signal and switches to limp-home with very limited torque. Often appears intermittently with a worn pedal sensor before failing outright.
causes: Pedal position sensor worn or contaminated

P2139.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D/F Voltage Correlation
P2139.plain: Channels D and F of the throttle/pedal position sensor disagree by more than the allowed tolerance.

P213A.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B/Open
P213A.plain: The drive circuit of EGR throttle B is open. EGR throttles partially close intake to increase exhaust gas recirculation flow at low loads.

P213B.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B Range/Performance
P213B.plain: EGR throttle B is electrically OK but does not move as commanded — typically carbon buildup or a sticking actuator.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P213C.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B Low
P213C.plain: EGR throttle B drive line stuck low — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P213D.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B High
P213D.plain: EGR throttle B drive line stuck high — short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P213E.title: Fuel Injection System Fault - Forced Engine Shutdown
P213E.plain: A safety-critical fuel-injection fault has been detected and the PCM has shut down the engine to prevent damage. Examples are common-rail pressure runaway, multiple stuck-open injectors, or HPFP failure.

P213F.title: Fuel Pump System Fault - Forced Engine Shutdown
P213F.plain: A safety-critical fuel-pump fault has been detected and the engine has been shut down. Typical for HPFP runaway or low-pressure pump that loses control authority.

P2140.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E/F Voltage Correlation
P2140.plain: Channels E and F of the throttle/pedal position sensor disagree by more than the allowed tolerance.

P2141.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A Low
P2141.plain: EGR throttle A drive line stuck low — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P2142.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A High
P2142.plain: EGR throttle A drive line stuck high — short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P2143.title: EGR Vent Control Circuit/Open
P2143.plain: The drive circuit of the EGR vent solenoid is open — the solenoid releases vacuum from the EGR actuator. Open circuit means the EGR cannot reset its position.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2144.title: EGR Vent Control Circuit Low
P2144.plain: EGR vent solenoid drive line stuck low — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2145.title: EGR Vent Control Circuit High
P2145.plain: EGR vent solenoid drive line stuck high — short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2146.title: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2146.plain: The ECU detects an open or missing supply voltage on injector group A. The injectors of this bank cannot be energized; the affected cylinders may not fire and the engine runs rough or stalls.

P2147.title: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2147.plain: The supply voltage measured at injector group A is below the calibrated threshold. Either the supply is shorted to ground or the source voltage has collapsed during cranking or load.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2148.title: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2148.plain: The injector group A supply voltage exceeds the calibrated upper limit. Often a sign of a short to battery voltage on the supply line, an over-charging alternator or an internal driver failure.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2149.title: Fuel Injector Group B Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2149.plain: The ECU detects an open or missing supply voltage on injector group B. The injectors on this bank cannot be energized, leading to misfire on the affected cylinders.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P214A.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High
P214A.plain: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.

P214B.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High During Particulate Filter Regeneration
P214B.plain: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High During Particulate Filter Regeneration: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.

P214C.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Outlet Temperature Too High
P214C.plain: SCR NOx Catalyst Outlet Temperature Too High: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.

P214D.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Outlet Temperature Too High During Particulate Filter Regeneration
P214D.plain: SCR NOx Catalyst Outlet Temperature Too High During Particulate Filter Regeneration: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.

P214E.title: Reductant Pump A Current Too High
P214E.plain: DEF pump A current draw exceeds the upper threshold — typically a seized pump head or partial winding short.

P214F.title: Reductant Heater A Current Too High
P214F.plain: DEF heater A current draw exceeds the upper threshold — typically a partial short in the heating element.

P2150.title: Fuel Injector Group B Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2150.plain: The supply voltage feeding injector group B has dropped below the lower limit. The injectors in this group lose drive voltage and may stop firing, so the cylinders they serve run lean or cut out. Causes: a blown fuse, a failed injector supply relay, a voltage drop in the supply harness, or a poor ground or connector on the group-B supply.
causes: Fuse, relay, or wiring fault on supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2151.title: Fuel Injector Group B Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2151.plain: The supply voltage on injector group B is above the upper limit. Overvoltage on the group-B supply can mis-time or damage the injectors. Causes: charging-system overvoltage, a stuck supply relay or regulator, or a wiring fault shorting the group-B supply to a higher voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2152.title: Fuel Injector Group C Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2152.plain: The supply rail to injector group C is open, so none of the injectors in this group can fire. The affected cylinders produce no power and the engine runs rough or on reduced cylinders. Causes: a broken supply wire, an open relay or fuse, or a disconnected group-C supply connector.
causes: Open supply wire or blown fuse
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2153.title: Fuel Injector Group C Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2153.plain: The supply voltage feeding injector group C has dropped below the lower limit. The injectors in this group lose drive voltage and may stop firing, so the cylinders they serve run lean or cut out. Causes: a blown fuse, a failed injector supply relay, a voltage drop in the supply harness, or a poor ground or connector on the group-C supply.
causes: Fuse, relay, or wiring fault on supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2154.title: Fuel Injector Group C Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2154.plain: The supply voltage on injector group C is above the upper limit. Overvoltage on the group-C supply can mis-time or damage the injectors. Causes: charging-system overvoltage, a stuck supply relay or regulator, or a wiring fault shorting the group-C supply to a higher voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2155.title: Fuel Injector Group D Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2155.plain: The supply rail to injector group D is open, so none of the injectors in this group can fire. The affected cylinders produce no power and the engine runs rough or on reduced cylinders. Causes: a broken supply wire, an open relay or fuse, or a disconnected group-D supply connector.
causes: Open supply wire or blown fuse
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2156.title: Fuel Injector Group D Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2156.plain: The supply voltage feeding injector group D has dropped below the lower limit. The injectors in this group lose drive voltage and may stop firing, so the cylinders they serve run lean or cut out. Causes: a blown fuse, a failed injector supply relay, a voltage drop in the supply harness, or a poor ground or connector on the group-D supply.
causes: Fuse, relay, or wiring fault on supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2157.title: Fuel Injector Group D Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2157.plain: The supply voltage on injector group D is above the upper limit. Overvoltage on the group-D supply can mis-time or damage the injectors. Causes: charging-system overvoltage, a stuck supply relay or regulator, or a wiring fault shorting the group-D supply to a higher voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2158.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Circuit
P2158.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on vehicle speed sensor B — second VSS used either at the transmission output or as redundancy. Open, short, or implausible signal.

P2159.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Range/Performance
P2159.plain: The signal of the secondary vehicle speed sensor is implausible compared to other sensors. The ECU cannot use the value for fuel and ignition control or transmission shifting.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P215A.title: Vehicle Speed - Wheel Speed Correlation
P215A.plain: The vehicle speed signal computed from VSS does not match the wheel-speed signal from ABS within tolerance. One of the two sources is wrong, or there is a tyre-size mismatch.

P215B.title: Vehicle Speed - Output Shaft Speed Correlation
P215B.plain: VSS does not match transmission output-shaft speed within tolerance. Possible transmission slip, sensor fault, or harness issue.

P215C.title: Output Shaft Speed - Wheel Speed Correlation
P215C.plain: Transmission output-shaft speed does not match ABS wheel speed within tolerance — typically transmission slip, driveline fault, or one sensor drift.

P215D.title: Reductant Pump B Stuck On
P215D.plain: Reductant Pump B Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P215E.title: Reductant Heater D Current Too Low
P215E.plain: DEF heater D current draw is below threshold — typically a partially-open winding.

P215F.title: Reductant Heater D Current Too High
P215F.plain: DEF heater D current draw exceeds threshold — element partially shorted.

P2160.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Circuit Low
P2160.plain: VSS B reads below lower plausibility — short to ground or sensor not signalling. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2161.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic/High
P2161.plain: VSS B signal jumps, drops out, or reads above plausibility — connector or harness issue, or magnetic ring damaged.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2162.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A/B Correlation
P2162.plain: VSS A and VSS B disagree by more than the allowed tolerance.

P2163.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Maximum Stop Performance
P2163.plain: Throttle/pedal position sensor A does not reach the calibrated maximum-stop value during the wide-open self-test. Sensor wear, mechanical stop misalignment, or a stuck pedal.

P2164.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Maximum Stop Performance
P2164.plain: Throttle/pedal position sensor B does not reach the calibrated maximum-stop value during the wide-open self-test. Sensor wear, mechanical stop misalignment, or a stuck pedal.

P2165.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Maximum Stop Performance
P2165.plain: Throttle/pedal position sensor C does not reach the calibrated maximum-stop value during the wide-open self-test. Sensor wear, mechanical stop misalignment, or a stuck pedal.

P2166.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor D Maximum Stop Performance
P2166.plain: Throttle/pedal position sensor D does not reach the calibrated maximum-stop value during the wide-open self-test. Sensor wear, mechanical stop misalignment, or a stuck pedal.

P2167.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor E Maximum Stop Performance
P2167.plain: Throttle/pedal position sensor E does not reach the calibrated maximum-stop value during the wide-open self-test. Sensor wear, mechanical stop misalignment, or a stuck pedal.

P2168.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor F Maximum Stop Performance
P2168.plain: Throttle/pedal position sensor F does not reach the calibrated maximum-stop value during the wide-open self-test. Sensor wear, mechanical stop misalignment, or a stuck pedal.

P2169.title: Exhaust Pressure Regulator Vent Solenoid Control Circuit/Open
P2169.plain: The drive circuit of the exhaust pressure regulator vent solenoid is open. The solenoid releases pressure from the exhaust backpressure regulator, which is part of the exhaust brake system on diesel trucks.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P216A.title: Fuel Injector Group E Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P216A.plain: The supply rail to injector group E is open, so none of the injectors in this group can fire. The affected cylinders produce no power and the engine runs rough or on reduced cylinders. Causes: a broken supply wire, an open relay or fuse, or a disconnected group-E supply connector.
causes: Open supply wire or blown fuse
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P216B.title: Fuel Injector Group E Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P216B.plain: The supply voltage feeding injector group E has dropped below the lower limit. The injectors in this group lose drive voltage and may stop firing, so the cylinders they serve run lean or cut out. Causes: a blown fuse, a failed injector supply relay, a voltage drop in the supply harness, or a poor ground or connector on the group-E supply.
causes: Fuse, relay, or wiring fault on supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P216C.title: Fuel Injector Group E Supply Voltage Circuit High
P216C.plain: The supply voltage on injector group E is above the upper limit. Overvoltage on the group-E supply can mis-time or damage the injectors. Causes: charging-system overvoltage, a stuck supply relay or regulator, or a wiring fault shorting the group-E supply to a higher voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P216D.title: Fuel Injector Group F Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P216D.plain: The supply rail to injector group F is open, so none of the injectors in this group can fire. The affected cylinders produce no power and the engine runs rough or on reduced cylinders. Causes: a broken supply wire, an open relay or fuse, or a disconnected group-F supply connector.
causes: Open supply wire or blown fuse
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P216E.title: Fuel Injector Group F Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P216E.plain: The supply voltage feeding injector group F has dropped below the lower limit. The injectors in this group lose drive voltage and may stop firing, so the cylinders they serve run lean or cut out. Causes: a blown fuse, a failed injector supply relay, a voltage drop in the supply harness, or a poor ground or connector on the group-F supply.
causes: Fuse, relay, or wiring fault on supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P216F.title: Fuel Injector Group F Supply Voltage Circuit High

causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2170.title: Exhaust Pressure Regulator Vent Solenoid Control Circuit Low
P2170.plain: EPR vent solenoid drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2171.title: Exhaust Pressure Regulator Vent Solenoid Control Circuit High
P2171.plain: EPR vent solenoid drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2172.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Sudden High Air Flow Detected
P2172.plain: A sudden, large jump in MAF/MAP signal not matched by a corresponding pedal change has been detected — typically a torn intake boot, dropped MAF sensor, or actively-stuck-open throttle plate.

P2173.title: High Airflow/Vacuum Leak Detected (Slow Accumulation)
P2173.plain: Long-term fuel and air adaptation values indicate a slow but continuous excess of air entering the engine. The ECU concludes that an unmetered air leak is gradually growing in the intake system.
causes: Cracked vacuum hose or intake gasket

P2174.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Sudden Low Air Flow Detected
P2174.plain: A sudden, large drop in MAF/MAP signal not matched by a pedal change — typically intake restriction, MAF failure, or actively-stuck-closed throttle plate.

P2175.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Low Air Flow Detected
P2175.plain: Sustained low air-flow condition detected — slower than P2174 but persistent. Restricted air filter, dirty MAF, or partially-stuck throttle.

P2176.title: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Idle Position Not Learned
P2176.plain: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Idle Position Not Learned: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P2177.title: System Too Lean Off Idle Bank 1
P2177.plain: Fuel trim values on bank 1 indicate a lean condition during off-idle operation. The ECU has to add significant fuel correction to maintain stoichiometric mixture above idle.

P2178.title: System Too Rich Off Idle Bank 1
P2178.plain: Bank 1 fuel trim shows a strong rich correction during off-idle operation. The ECU is forced to subtract fuel to keep the mixture near stoichiometric.

P2179.title: System Too Lean Off Idle Bank 2
P2179.plain: Fuel trims on bank 2 show a lean deviation during off-idle operating conditions. Causes are similar to bank 1 but isolated to the second cylinder bank.

P217A.title: Fuel Injector Group G Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P217A.plain: The supply rail to injector group G is open, so none of the injectors in this group can fire. The affected cylinders produce no power and the engine runs rough or on reduced cylinders. Causes: a broken supply wire, an open relay or fuse, or a disconnected group-G supply connector.
causes: Open supply wire or blown fuse
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

Causes: a blown fuse, a failed injector supply relay, a voltage drop in the supply harness, or a poor ground or connector on the group-G supply.
causes: Fuse, relay, or wiring fault on supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

causes: Open supply wire or blown fuse
Pin pushed back out of connector body

Causes: a blown fuse, a failed injector supply relay, a voltage drop in the supply harness, or a poor ground or connector on the group-H supply.
causes: Fuse, relay, or wiring fault on supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P217F.title: Fuel Injector Group H Supply Voltage Circuit High
P217F.plain: The supply voltage on injector group H is above the upper limit. Overvoltage on the group-H supply can mis-time or damage the injectors. Causes: charging-system overvoltage, a stuck supply relay or regulator, or a wiring fault shorting the group-H supply to a higher voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2180.title: System Too Rich Off Idle Bank 2
P2180.plain: Bank 2 fuel trim shows a rich shift during off-idle conditions. The ECU subtracts fuel to maintain proper combustion. Common causes are stuck injectors or excess fuel pressure.

P2181.title: Cooling System Performance
P2181.plain: The engine cooling system does not reach or maintain the expected temperature within the diagnostic window — usually a stuck-open thermostat, but also a low coolant level or a stuck cooling fan that overcools the engine.

P2182.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit
P2182.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on engine coolant temperature sensor 2 — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. Sensor 2 is typically at the radiator outlet or as redundancy on the second cylinder bank.

P2183.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance
P2183.plain: ECT sensor 2 reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response, stuck reading, or value does not track ECT 1 across a warm-up.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2184.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P2184.plain: ECT sensor 2 reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2185.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit High
P2185.plain: The second coolant temperature sensor (often radiator-outlet or cylinder-head bank) reports a voltage above the upper threshold — typically an open signal wire or a sensor with infinite resistance.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2186.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P2186.plain: The second coolant temperature sensor reports a voltage below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or a sensor with very low resistance.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2187.title: System Too Lean at Idle (Bank 1)
P2187.plain: Fuel trim on bank 1 hits the lean limit only at idle, while trim returns to normal at higher load. This pattern strongly indicates a vacuum leak — leaks become a larger fraction of total airflow at idle and so dominate the trim, but disappear into background noise above idle.
causes: Vacuum leak (intake gasket, brake booster, hoses)

P2188.title: System Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1)
P2188.plain: Fuel trim on bank 1 hits the rich limit only at idle. Often a leaking injector dribbling fuel at low load, a sticky purge valve dumping fuel vapour, or fuel pressure regulator that fails to relieve pressure when intake vacuum is high.

P2189.title: System Too Lean at Idle (Bank 2)
P2189.plain: Fuel trim on bank 2 hits the lean limit only at idle, while trim returns to normal at higher load. This pattern strongly indicates a vacuum leak — leaks become a larger fraction of total airflow at idle and so dominate the trim, but disappear into background noise above idle.

P218A.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Idle Position Not Learned
P218A.plain: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Idle Position Not Learned: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P218B.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit
P218B.plain: A general electrical fault on the throttle/fuel inhibit signal B — used by anti-theft, immobiliser, or transmission to forbid throttle/fuel until released.

P218C.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit Range/Performance
P218C.plain: Throttle/fuel inhibit B signal reads in range but plausibility fails — does not assert/release as expected.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P218D.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit Low
P218D.plain: Throttle/fuel inhibit B line stuck low. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P218E.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit High
P218E.plain: Throttle/fuel inhibit B line stuck high. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P218F.title: Reductant No Flow Detected
P218F.plain: The DEF dosing system commands flow but the pressure or flow sensor reports no actual delivery — typically a fully blocked dosing nozzle, a frozen line, or a dead pump.
causes: Dosing line or nozzle fully blocked
Line frozen at very low ambient temperature

P2190.title: System Too Rich at Idle (Bank 2)
P2190.plain: Fuel trim on bank 2 hits the rich limit only at idle. Often a leaking injector dribbling fuel at low load, a sticky purge valve dumping fuel vapour, or fuel pressure regulator that fails to relieve pressure when intake vacuum is high.
causes: Leaking injector at idle on bank 2

P2191.title: System Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P2191.plain: Bank 1 fuel trim hits the lean limit only at higher engine load. Pattern points to a fuel-supply restriction — failing fuel pump, blocked filter, or weak injectors — rather than a vacuum leak (which would dominate at idle).
causes: MAF reads low at high airflow

P2192.title: System Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P2192.plain: Bank 1 fuel trim hits the rich limit only at higher load. Often excessive fuel pressure, a stuck-closed MAF reading low, or coolant temperature signal stuck cold causing over-fuelling.

P2193.title: System Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P2193.plain: Bank 2 fuel trim hits the lean limit only at higher engine load. Pattern points to a fuel-supply restriction — failing fuel pump, blocked filter, or weak injectors — rather than a vacuum leak (which would dominate at idle).

P2194.title: System Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P2194.plain: Bank 2 fuel trim hits the rich limit only at higher load. Often excessive fuel pressure, a stuck-closed MAF reading low, or coolant temperature signal stuck cold causing over-fuelling.

P2195.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P2195.plain: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 returns a constant lean signal during conditions where rich content is expected (for example after a deceleration fuel cut-off recovery). Usually a sensor that has lost its rich-side response or a slow heater warm-up.
causes: Sensor heater slow to warm up

P2196.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P2196.plain: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 returns a constant rich signal under deceleration fuel cut-off where lean is expected. Often a contaminated sensor (silicone, oil, coolant) or short to ground that pulls the signal high in some sensor types.

P2197.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P2197.plain: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 returns a constant lean signal during conditions where rich content is expected (for example after a deceleration fuel cut-off recovery). Usually a sensor that has lost its rich-side response or a slow heater warm-up.

P2198.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P2198.plain: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 returns a constant rich signal under deceleration fuel cut-off where lean is expected. Often a contaminated sensor (silicone, oil, coolant) or short to ground that pulls the signal high in some sensor types.

P2199.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation
P2199.plain: The two intake air temperature sensors disagree by more than the calibrated correlation threshold during stable conditions. The ECU cannot determine which value is correct.

P219A.title: Bank 1 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P219A.plain: The fuel-trim values across cylinders on bank 1 differ enough that the bank-average air-fuel ratio is biased — a single cylinder is significantly leaner or richer than the rest. Detected by short-term-fuel-trim variance or by the wide-band O2 sensor harmonic monitor.
causes: Vacuum leak at one intake runner

P219B.title: Bank 2 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P219B.plain: The fuel-trim values across cylinders on bank 2 differ enough that the bank-average air-fuel ratio is biased — a single cylinder is significantly leaner or richer than the rest. Detected by short-term-fuel-trim variance or by the wide-band O2 sensor harmonic monitor.

P219C.title: Cylinder 1 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P219C.plain: Cylinder 1 fuel trim deviates significantly from the bank average — a single-cylinder injector or intake fault.

P21A8.title: Reductant Level Sensor B Circuit
P21A8.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on DEF level sensor B — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. Some tanks use multiple level senders to cover irregular tank shapes; this is the primary one.

P21A9.title: Reductant Level Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P21A9.plain: DEF level sensor B reading is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — value sticks, jumps, or does not match consumption.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P21B2.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop NOx Adsorber Control
P21B2.plain: The NOx adsorber control did not enter closed-loop operation within the calibrated time after engine start — typically a slow-warming NOx sensor or pre-heat heater fault.

P21B3.title: Closed Loop NOx Adsorber Control At Limit - Too High
P21B3.plain: NOx adsorber closed-loop trim has reached the upper authority limit — the controller cannot correct further. Typically a degraded LNT or stuck-rich engine condition.

P21B4.title: NOx Adsorber Over Temperature (Bank 1)
P21B4.plain: A temperature sensor at the NOx adsorber on bank 1 reports a value above the safe limit. Sustained over-temperature destroys the storage washcoat.

P21B5.title: NOx Adsorber Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P21B5.plain: A temperature sensor at the NOx adsorber on bank 2 reports a value above the safe limit. Sustained over-temperature destroys the storage washcoat.

P21B6.title: Cold Start Cylinder 1 Injection Timing
P21B6.plain: Cylinder 1 cold-start injection timing is outside the calibrated window. Diesel cold-start uses adapted injection timing per cylinder to limit white smoke and noise; deviation typically points at a worn injector or faulty crank/cam correlation.

causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P21C5.title: Reductant Level Sensor A Stuck
P21C5.plain: DEF level sensor A reading does not change over a refill or consumption window — float arm jammed or sender wiper stuck. Distinct from a circuit fault because the electrical signal stays plausible.
causes: Float arm jammed by debris or crystallisation

P21C6.title: Reductant Level Sensor B Stuck
P21C6.plain: DEF level sensor B reading does not change over a refill or consumption window — float arm jammed or sender wiper stuck. Distinct from a circuit fault because the electrical signal stays plausible.

Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P21CB.title: Reductant Control Module Supply Voltage Low
P21CB.plain: SCR control module supply voltage measured at the module pin is below the lower threshold.

P21CC.title: Reductant Control Module Supply Voltage High
P21CC.plain: SCR control module supply voltage above the upper threshold — overvoltage.

P21CD.title: Reductant Quality Module Supply Voltage Low
P21CD.plain: Supply voltage at the dedicated DEF quality sensor module is below the lower threshold.

P21CE.title: Reductant Quality Module Performance
P21CE.plain: DEF quality module reports an internal performance fault — self-test failed or measurement loop unable to converge. The module may need replacement.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve
