P21F2.title: Cylinder 12 Injector B Circuit Low
P21F2.plain: Cylinder 12 second-injector (B) drive line stuck low — short to ground. A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P21F3.title: Cylinder 12 Injector B Circuit High
P21F3.plain: Cylinder 12 second-injector (B) drive line stuck high — short to B+. A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P21F4.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean Off Idle (Bank 1)
P21F4.plain: The secondary fuel control loop B on bank 1 reports a lean condition outside idle. On dual-injection systems (port + direct) the secondary loop trims port injection independently from the main loop.

P21F5.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 1)
P21F5.plain: Fuel Control System B Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 1): the fuel-trim control is correcting for an over-rich mixture in this operating range.

P21F6.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean Off Idle (Bank 2)
P21F6.plain: The secondary fuel control loop B on bank 2 reports a lean condition outside idle. On dual-injection systems (port + direct) the secondary loop trims port injection independently from the main loop.

P21F7.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 2)
P21F7.plain: The secondary fuel control loop B on bank 2 reports a rich condition outside idle.

P21F8.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Idle (Bank 1)
P21F8.plain: Secondary fuel control loop B reports a lean condition at idle on bank 1. Idle is sensitive to vacuum leaks since manifold flow is low.
causes: Vacuum leak — most visible at idle

P21F9.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1)
P21F9.plain: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1): the fuel-trim control is correcting for an over-rich mixture in this operating range.
causes: Injectors leak at low duty cycle

P21FA.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Idle (Bank 2)
P21FA.plain: Secondary fuel control loop B reports a lean condition at idle on bank 2. Idle is sensitive to vacuum leaks since manifold flow is low.

P21FB.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Idle (Bank 2)
P21FB.plain: The secondary fuel control loop B reports a rich condition at idle on bank 2. Idle rich often means injectors that leak at low duty cycle.

P21FC.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P21FC.plain: Secondary fuel control loop B on bank 1 reports a lean condition at higher load. Lean at high load typically points at fuel pressure shortfall, restricted injectors, or charge-air leak.

P21FD.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P21FD.plain: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 1): the fuel-trim control is correcting for an over-rich mixture in this operating range.

P21FE.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P21FE.plain: Secondary fuel control loop B on bank 2 reports a lean condition at higher load. Lean at high load typically points at fuel pressure shortfall, restricted injectors, or charge-air leak.
causes: Fuel or charge-air problem on bank 2

P21FF.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P21FF.plain: The secondary fuel control loop B reports a rich condition at higher load on bank 2. Rich at high load typically points to a stuck-closed return on the fuel pressure regulator or over-delivering injectors.

P2200.title: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 1)
P2200.plain: The NOx sensor on bank 1 — typically upstream of the SCR catalyst — does not communicate or sends an invalid signal. NOx sensors are smart sensors with their own controller on the CAN bus; faults often involve heater failure or bus dropout.
causes: Sensor wiring or CAN harness open

P2201.title: NOx Sensor Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P2201.plain: The bank 1 NOx sensor reports values outside the plausibility window against modeled NOx and the downstream sensor. Often slow response from contamination by oil ash or coolant.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2202.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2202.plain: The NOx sensor signal on bank 1 is below the lower limit. Either short to ground on the analog return, sensor failed at low end, or pump cell stuck.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2203.title: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1)
P2203.plain: The NOx sensor signal on bank 1 is above the upper limit — short to supply, open ground, or a sensor that failed high. SCR control runs in default mode.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2204.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1)
P2204.plain: The bank 1 NOx sensor signal drops out intermittently. Typical cause is a marginal connector, harness chafing near hot exhaust components, or thermal-cycling solder joints inside the smart sensor.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2205.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1)
P2205.plain: The heater inside the bank 1 NOx sensor cannot be controlled — open, short, or failed driver. Without proper heater operation the sensor never reaches its operating temperature and reports invalid data.
causes: Heater short to supply or ground

P2206.title: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 2)
P2206.plain: A general electrical fault on the bank 2 NOx sensor circuit. NOx sensors are smart sensors with a CAN/LIN interface; this code typically indicates that the sensor module no longer responds.

P2207.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P2207.plain: The bank 2 NOx sensor returns values outside the expected range for the operating point — for example a non-zero reading at engine off or unchanged values during load changes.
causes: Sensor contaminated with soot or condensate
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2208.title: NOx Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 2)
P2208.plain: A general electrical fault on the heater of the bank 2 NOx sensor. NOx sensors must reach roughly 800 C to measure correctly; without heater current the sensor never enters its operating range.
causes: Heater wiring open or connector loose

P2209.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P2209.plain: The heater feedback (sense) line on the bank 2 NOx sensor reports values outside the expected window — heating is happening but the temperature does not match the model.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P220A.title: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P220A.plain: The supply voltage rail to the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 is faulty — typically a fuse, harness break, or short. NOx sensors need a clean stable supply for the heater and the wide-band measurement cell.

P220B.title: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P220B.plain: The supply voltage rail to the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 is faulty — typically a fuse, harness break, or short. NOx sensors need a clean stable supply for the heater and the wide-band measurement cell.

P220C.title: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P220C.plain: The supply voltage rail to the NOx sensor on bank 2 sensor 1 is faulty — typically a fuse, harness break, or short. NOx sensors need a clean stable supply for the heater and the wide-band measurement cell.

P220D.title: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P220D.plain: The supply voltage rail to the NOx sensor on bank 2 sensor 2 is faulty — typically a fuse, harness break, or short. NOx sensors need a clean stable supply for the heater and the wide-band measurement cell.

P220E.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P220E.plain: The heater control loop for the NOx sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 reports off-spec behaviour — heater current draw or response time outside the calibrated range. NOx sensors only operate above ~600 °C, so heater control is critical.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P220F.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P220F.plain: The heater control loop for the NOx sensor at bank 1 sensor 2 reports off-spec behaviour — heater current draw or response time outside the calibrated range. NOx sensors only operate above ~600 °C, so heater control is critical.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2210.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
P2210.plain: The bank 2 NOx sensor reports correctly some of the time but intermittently drops out. Often a marginal connector, a wiring chafe or a sensor that fails when warm.

P2211.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
P2211.plain: The heater sense line on the bank 2 NOx sensor produces intermittent readings. Often a thermal fault inside the sensor or a connector under temperature cycling.

P2212.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2212.plain: The feedback line that monitors the NOx sensor heater current draw on bank 1 sensor 1 jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or harness issue.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2213.title: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 2)
P2213.plain: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 2): an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P2214.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P2214.plain: NOx sensor on bank 2 reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response, drift, or value does not match the model expectation.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2215.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P2215.plain: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 2): the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2216.title: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2216.plain: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 2): the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2217.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
P2217.plain: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2): the signal is intermittent or erratic. Often a loose connector or chafed wiring; a wiggle test often locates it.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2218.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit/Open (Bank 2)
P2218.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit/Open (Bank 2): the control circuit is open. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2219.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P2219.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2): the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P221A.title: NOx Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 1)
P221A.plain: NOx sensors 1 and 2 on bank 1 disagree by more than the allowed tolerance over a drive cycle. One sensor drifts, or there is a real NOx gradient that exceeds the calibrated map.

P221B.title: NOx Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 2)
P221B.plain: NOx sensors 1 and 2 on bank 2 disagree by more than the allowed tolerance over a drive cycle. One sensor drifts, or there is a real NOx gradient that exceeds the calibrated map.

P221C.title: Reductant Heater B Current Too Low
P221C.plain: Reductant Heater B Current Too Low: the control module has detected this fault condition. The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) heater keeps the urea fluid from freezing; a fault can impair SCR dosing in cold conditions.

P221D.title: Reductant Heater B Current Too High
P221D.plain: Reductant Heater B Current Too High: the control module has detected this fault condition. The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) heater keeps the urea fluid from freezing; a fault can impair SCR dosing in cold conditions.

P221E.title: Reductant Heater C Current Too Low
P221E.plain: Reductant Heater C Current Too Low: the control module has detected this fault condition. The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) heater keeps the urea fluid from freezing; a fault can impair SCR dosing in cold conditions.

P221F.title: Reductant Heater C Current Too High
P221F.plain: Reductant Heater C Current Too High: the control module has detected this fault condition. The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) heater keeps the urea fluid from freezing; a fault can impair SCR dosing in cold conditions.

P2220.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2220.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2): the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2221.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit (Bank 2)
P2221.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit (Bank 2): an electrical fault is present in the circuit. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.

P2222.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P2222.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2): the signal is implausible or outside the valid range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2223.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P2223.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Low (Bank 2): the signal voltage is below the expected range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2224.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2224.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit High (Bank 2): the signal voltage is above the expected range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2225.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
P2225.plain: The feedback line that monitors the NOx sensor heater current draw on bank 2 sensor 1 jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or harness issue.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2226.title: Barometric Pressure Circuit
P2226.plain: The ECU detects a general fault in the barometric pressure sensor circuit. The atmospheric pressure value used for altitude compensation and fuel/air calculation is not available or implausible.

P2227.title: Barometric Pressure Circuit Range/Performance
P2227.plain: The barometric pressure sensor delivers an electrically valid signal that does not match the operating point — for example pressure jumps that do not match altitude changes, or values stuck near full scale.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2228.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2228.plain: The barometric (ambient) pressure sensor reports a voltage below the valid window. The ECU uses this signal to compensate fuel and boost calculations for altitude — a stuck-low value tricks the ECU into thinking the car is at high altitude.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2229.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P2229.plain: The barometric pressure sensor reports a voltage above the valid window. Usually a short to supply or an open ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P222A.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P222A.plain: A general electrical fault on barometric pressure sensor B — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. The sensor measures atmospheric pressure for altitude compensation; sensor B is a redundant or secondary unit.

P222B.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P222B.plain: Barometric sensor B reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P222C.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P222C.plain: Barometric sensor B below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P222D.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P222D.plain: Barometric sensor B above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P222E.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P222E.plain: Barometric sensor B signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P222F.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor A/B Correlation
P222F.plain: Barometric pressure sensors A and B disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. Used for redundancy on hybrid and emission-critical systems.

P2230.title: Barometric Pressure Circuit Low
P2230.plain: Voltage from the barometric pressure sensor is below the calibrated minimum. The signal is too low for any plausible atmospheric pressure, suggesting a short to ground or sensor fault.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2231.title: Barometric Pressure Circuit High
P2231.plain: The barometric pressure sensor reports a voltage above the upper limit. The signal cannot represent any realistic atmospheric pressure, indicating an open circuit or short to supply voltage.
causes: Open in signal or ground wire
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2232.title: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P2232.plain: The O2 sensor signal wire on bank 1 sensor 2 has shorted to the heater wire. This pulls the signal away from a measurement of exhaust composition and produces erratic fuel-trim behaviour.
causes: Short between signal and heater wires

P2233.title: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P2233.plain: The O2 sensor signal wire on bank 1 sensor 3 has shorted to the heater wire. This pulls the signal away from a measurement of exhaust composition and produces erratic fuel-trim behaviour.
causes: Short between signal and heater wires

P2234.title: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2234.plain: The O2 sensor signal wire on bank 2 sensor 1 has shorted to the heater wire. This pulls the signal away from a measurement of exhaust composition and produces erratic fuel-trim behaviour.
causes: Short between signal and heater wires

P2235.title: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P2235.plain: The O2 sensor signal wire on bank 2 sensor 2 has shorted to the heater wire. This pulls the signal away from a measurement of exhaust composition and produces erratic fuel-trim behaviour.
causes: Short between signal and heater wires

P2236.title: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P2236.plain: The O2 sensor signal wire on bank 2 sensor 3 has shorted to the heater wire. This pulls the signal away from a measurement of exhaust composition and produces erratic fuel-trim behaviour.
causes: Short between signal and heater wires

P2237.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2237.plain: The pumping current line of the wide-band lambda sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 is unable to operate. Wide-band sensors regulate exhaust oxygen to a reference cell via this pumping current — without it, AFR cannot be measured.

P2238.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2238.plain: Pumping current at the bank 1 sensor 1 wide-band lambda probe is below the lower limit — short to ground or sensor at end of life.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2239.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2239.plain: Pumping current at the bank 1 sensor 1 wide-band lambda probe is above the upper limit — short to supply or open return path.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P223A.title: Reductant Heater E Control Circuit
P223A.plain: Reductant Heater E Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault. The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) heater keeps the urea fluid from freezing; a fault can impair SCR dosing in cold conditions.

P223B.title: Reductant Heater F Control Circuit
P223B.plain: Reductant Heater F Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault. The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) heater keeps the urea fluid from freezing; a fault can impair SCR dosing in cold conditions.

P223C.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P223C.plain: The pumping current of the wide-band O2 sensor on bank 1 is in electrical range but plausibility check fails. Wide-band sensors use a pumping cell that adjusts oxygen concentration in a reference chamber; the current required is proportional to lambda.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P223D.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P223D.plain: The pumping current of the wide-band O2 sensor on bank 2 is in electrical range but plausibility check fails. Wide-band sensors use a pumping cell that adjusts oxygen concentration in a reference chamber; the current required is proportional to lambda.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P223E.title: O2 Sensor Reference Resistance Out Of Range (Bank 1)
P223E.plain: The reference resistance of the wide-band O2 sensor on bank 1 is outside the calibrated range — used by the controller to set the operating point of the pumping cell. Drift here indicates sensor element ageing or contamination.

P223F.title: O2 Sensor Reference Resistance Out Of Range (Bank 2)
P223F.plain: The reference resistance of the wide-band O2 sensor on bank 2 is outside the calibrated range — used by the controller to set the operating point of the pumping cell. Drift here indicates sensor element ageing or contamination.

P2240.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2240.plain: Bank 2 counterpart of P2237. The wide-band lambda sensor on bank 2 sensor 1 cannot operate its pumping current circuit.
causes: Pumping current line open on bank 2

P2241.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2241.plain: The pumping-current line of the wide-band oxygen sensor on bank 2, sensor 1 is below the lower threshold. Wide-band sensors use a small pumping current to keep their measuring cell at lambda 1; a low value usually means an open or shorted pump cell.
causes: Pump cell open or sensor failed
Pumping current line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2242.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2242.plain: The pumping-current line of the bank 2, sensor 1 wide-band oxygen sensor reads above the upper threshold. Common with a short to a positive supply or a damaged sensor amplifier in the ECU.
causes: Pumping current line shorted to positive
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2243.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2243.plain: The reference voltage line that powers the wide-band sensor cell on bank 1 sensor 1 is missing or out of tolerance. Without correct reference, the AFR calculation is invalid.

P2244.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2244.plain: The reference voltage that the ECU supplies to the wide-band oxygen sensor on bank 1, sensor 1 drifts outside the expected range. The reference is the baseline against which the cell voltages are measured; a drift falsifies every lambda calculation.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2245.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2245.plain: The reference voltage feeding the bank 1, sensor 1 wide-band oxygen sensor is below the lower threshold. Often a short to ground in the wiring or a failed reference output stage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2246.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2246.plain: The reference voltage on the bank 1, sensor 1 wide-band oxygen sensor reads above the upper threshold. Common with a short to a positive supply or a corroded connector with leakage current.
causes: Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2247.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2247.plain: Bank 2 counterpart of P2243. Reference voltage on the bank 2 sensor 1 wide-band probe is missing or out of tolerance.
causes: Reference voltage line open on bank 2

P2248.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2248.plain: Bank 2 counterpart to P2244. The reference voltage at the wide-band oxygen sensor on bank 2, sensor 1 is outside its expected range and falsifies the lambda calculation.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2249.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2249.plain: Bank 2 counterpart to P2245. The reference voltage on bank 2, sensor 1 is below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or failed ECU output.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P224A.title: NOx Sensor Heater Resistance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P224A.plain: The measured heater element resistance of the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 is outside the calibrated range. Used as a sensor-element health check.

P224B.title: NOx Sensor Heater Resistance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P224B.plain: The measured heater element resistance of the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 is outside the calibrated range. Used as a sensor-element health check.

P224C.title: Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit/Open
P224C.plain: The drive circuit for the shutoff valve at the alternative-fuel tank A is open. Bi-fuel vehicles (CNG, LPG, hydrogen) use a high-pressure shutoff valve at the tank for safety; with this fault the alternative fuel cannot be drawn from the tank.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P224D.title: Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P224D.plain: Alternative-fuel shutoff valve A is electrically OK but does not open when commanded. Vehicle remains on petrol/diesel only.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P224E.title: Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Low
P224E.plain: Shutoff valve A drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P224F.title: Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit High
P224F.plain: Shutoff valve A drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2250.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2250.plain: Bank 2 counterpart to P2246. The reference voltage at bank 2, sensor 1 is above the upper threshold, usually due to a short to positive or connector leakage.
causes: Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2251.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2251.plain: The negative current control line (Vs−) of the wide-band lambda sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 is open or out of range. Used as the virtual ground reference for the Nernst cell.

P2252.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2252.plain: The negative-current (Vs negative) line on the bank 1, sensor 1 wide-band oxygen sensor is below the lower threshold. This line is the return path for the Nernst cell; loss of the signal blocks the lambda calculation.
causes: Vs negative line shorted to ground
Nernst cell return open inside sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2253.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2253.plain: The Vs negative line on bank 1, sensor 1 reads above the upper threshold. Often a short to positive or a damaged ECU sensor amplifier.
causes: Vs negative line shorted to positive
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2254.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2254.plain: Bank 2 counterpart to P2252. The Vs negative line on the wide-band oxygen sensor at bank 2, sensor 1 is below the lower threshold.
causes: Vs negative line shorted to ground
Nernst cell return open inside sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2255.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2255.plain: Bank 2 counterpart to P2253. The Vs negative line on bank 2, sensor 1 reads above the upper threshold.
causes: Vs negative line shorted to positive
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2256.title: O2 Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 2
P2256.plain: The ECU detects a low-side voltage below threshold on the heater control of the rear oxygen sensor on bank 1. The heater driver may be stuck on or shorted to ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2257.title: Secondary Air Injection System Control A Circuit Low
P2257.plain: The control circuit of the secondary air injection system A reads a voltage below specification. Either the relay output is shorted to ground or the wiring/load is faulty.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2258.title: Secondary Air Injection System Control A Circuit High
P2258.plain: The control circuit A of the secondary air injection system shows a voltage above the calibrated upper threshold. Likely a short to battery voltage or an open in the relay coil/output.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2259.title: Secondary Air Injection System Control B Circuit Low
P2259.plain: The drive line for secondary air injection (AIR) control circuit B is stuck low. Secondary air is pumped into the exhaust manifold during cold start to speed up catalyst light-off.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P225A.title: NOx Sensor Calibration Memory (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P225A.plain: The factory calibration memory of the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 cannot be read or contains a checksum error. Each NOx sensor ships with a unique calibration table programmed at the factory.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P225B.title: NOx Sensor Calibration Memory (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P225B.plain: The factory calibration memory of the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 cannot be read or contains a checksum error. Each NOx sensor ships with a unique calibration table programmed at the factory.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P225C.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P225C.plain: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck High (Bank 1 Sensor 1): the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.
causes: Sensor poisoned by silicon, sulphur, or oil ash
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P225D.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P225D.plain: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1): the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P225E.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P225E.plain: The NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 reads suspiciously high for too long — biased upward or stuck. Common after sensor poisoning by silicon, sulphur, or oil ash.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P225F.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P225F.plain: The NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 reads suspiciously low for too long — biased downward or stuck. Common after sensor element ageing, condensate damage from cold start, or wiring fault that pulls the signal down.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P2260.title: Secondary Air Injection System Control B Circuit High
P2260.plain: AIR system control B drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2261.title: Turbo/Super Charger Bypass Valve Mechanical
P2261.plain: The ECU detects a mechanical fault in the turbocharger or supercharger bypass valve. The valve does not open or close as commanded, causing boost-pressure errors and reduced engine response.

P2262.title: Turbo Boost Pressure Not Detected - Mechanical
P2262.plain: The ECU does not detect any meaningful boost pressure increase under load even though the turbocharger is commanded. Likely a mechanical defect in the turbo, charge-air piping or wastegate.

P2263.title: Turbo/Super Charger Boost System Performance
P2263.plain: Boost pressure does not match the requested target during normal operation. The deviation between commanded and measured boost exceeds the calibrated tolerance, often due to leaks, sticking actuators or sensor errors.

P2264.title: Water in Fuel Sensor Circuit
P2264.plain: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the diesel water-in-fuel sensor circuit. Until repaired, water contamination in the fuel filter cannot be detected, risking damage to the high-pressure pump and injectors.

P2265.title: Water in Fuel Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2265.plain: The ECU detects that the water-in-fuel sensor signal is implausible compared to operating conditions. The reading does not change as expected during fuel filter purge or warm-up.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2266.title: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit Low
P2266.plain: The water-in-fuel sensor at the diesel fuel filter reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. The sensor warns the driver to drain the filter when condensate accumulates.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2267.title: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit High
P2267.plain: Water-in-fuel sensor reads above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2268.title: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P2268.plain: Water-in-fuel sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2269.title: Water in Fuel Condition - Sensor A
P2269.plain: The water-in-fuel sensor at fuel filter A has detected water above the warning threshold. The fuel filter must be drained; running the engine on water-contaminated diesel can damage the high-pressure pump and injectors.
causes: Condensate accumulated in filter — drain required

P226A.title: Water in Fuel Lamp Control Circuit
P226A.plain: A general electrical fault on the drive line for the dashboard water-in-fuel warning lamp.

P226B.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger A Boost Pressure Too High - Mechanical
P226B.plain: Boost pressure on turbo A exceeds the upper threshold and the cause is mechanical (wastegate stuck closed, VGT vanes stuck closed) rather than electrical drive fault.

P226C.title: Turbocharger Boost Control A Slow Response
P226C.plain: Turbocharger Boost Control A Slow Response: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.

P226D.title: Particulate Filter Deteriorated/Missing Substrate (Bank 1)
P226D.plain: The DPF substrate on bank 1 has been detected as cracked, melted, or removed. Differential pressure across the filter is too low for the measured exhaust flow — the soot trap no longer works.
causes: Substrate cracked or melted from runaway regen

P226E.title: Particulate Filter Deteriorated/Missing Substrate (Bank 2)
P226E.plain: The DPF substrate on bank 2 has been detected as cracked, melted, or removed. Differential pressure across the filter is too low for the measured exhaust flow — the soot trap no longer works.

P226F.title: Turbocharger Boost Control B Slow Response
P226F.plain: Turbocharger Boost Control B Slow Response: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.

P2270.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P2270.plain: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports a constant lean signal during a forced-rich command from the ECU. Suggests either a sensor that has lost its rich-side response, or a catalyst that is so degraded that no rich exhaust reaches the downstream sensor (cross-check P0420).

P2271.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P2271.plain: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports a constant rich signal during a forced-lean command. Suggests a failed downstream sensor or a sensor contaminated by oil/coolant from upstream engine wear.

P2272.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
P2272.plain: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 reports a constant lean signal during a forced-rich command from the ECU. Suggests either a sensor that has lost its rich-side response, or a catalyst that is so degraded that no rich exhaust reaches the downstream sensor (cross-check P0420).

P2273.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
P2273.plain: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 reports a constant rich signal during a forced-lean command. Suggests a failed downstream sensor or a sensor contaminated by oil/coolant from upstream engine wear.

P2274.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P2274.plain: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 3): the control module has detected this fault condition.

P2275.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P2275.plain: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 3): the control module has detected this fault condition.
causes: Sensor coated with carbon or fuel residue

P2276.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P2276.plain: O2 sensor at bank 2 sensor 3 reports a lean reading suspiciously stable for too long. Sensor 3 is typically downstream of the second catalyst on systems with three-stage aftertreatment.

P2277.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P2277.plain: O2 sensor at bank 2 sensor 3 reports a rich reading suspiciously stable for too long. Sensor 3 is typically downstream of the second catalyst on systems with three-stage aftertreatment; sensor coated with carbon or fuel residue is the typical cause.

P2278.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 3 / Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2278.plain: The PCM detects that the O2 sensor signals from bank 1 sensor 3 and bank 2 sensor 3 are swapped — typically a wiring crossover after sensor replacement.

P2279.title: Intake Air System Leak
P2279.plain: The ECU has detected a discrepancy between commanded throttle/intake conditions and the resulting MAP/MAF that points to unmetered air entering after the throttle body. On turbocharged engines this often means a cracked or disconnected boost pipe between turbo and intake; on naturally aspirated engines, a hole in the intake manifold or hose.

P227A.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit
P227A.plain: A general electrical fault on barometric pressure sensor C — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. The sensor measures atmospheric pressure for altitude compensation; sensor C is a redundant or secondary unit.

P227B.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P227B.plain: Barometric sensor C reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P227C.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit Low
P227C.plain: Barometric sensor C below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P227D.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit High
P227D.plain: Barometric sensor C above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P227E.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P227E.plain: Barometric sensor C signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P227F.title: Air Flow Restriction/Air Leak Between Air Filter and MAF (Bank 2)
P227F.plain: Restriction or leak detected in the intake plumbing between the air filter and the mass-air-flow sensor on bank 2 — typically a cracked intake boot or torn filter element.

P2280.title: Air Flow Restriction / Air Filter Restriction
P2280.plain: The ECU detects an excessive intake restriction. Either the air filter is heavily clogged or an obstruction in the intake duct is reducing airflow below the expected level.

P2281.title: Air Leak Between MAF and Throttle Body
P2281.plain: The ECU detects unmetered air entering between the mass airflow sensor and the throttle body. The actual airflow into the engine is greater than what the MAF measures, leading to lean conditions.

P2282.title: Air Leak Between Throttle Body and Intake Valves
P2282.plain: The ECU detects unmetered air entering downstream of the throttle body. Typical sources are leaking intake-manifold gaskets, vacuum hoses or PCV components.

P2283.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2283.plain: A general electrical fault on the injector control pressure (ICP) sensor — used on HEUI (Hydraulically actuated Electronically controlled Unit Injector) systems on heavy-duty diesel engines such as the Ford Powerstroke 6.0/7.3 and Caterpillar engines. ICP measures the high-pressure oil that actuates the injectors.

P2284.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2284.plain: The injector control pressure (ICP) sensor on HEUI diesel systems reports a value that does not match expected operating range or commanded pressure. Affects fuel injection timing and quantity.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2285.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2285.plain: The voltage of the injector control pressure sensor is below the calibrated minimum. The signal indicates either a short to ground or a sensor that has lost its supply.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2286.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P2286.plain: The voltage of the injector control pressure sensor is above the calibrated maximum. Likely a short to supply voltage or an open ground in the sensor circuit.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2287.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Intermittent
P2287.plain: The injector control pressure sensor signal is intermittently lost or out of range. Often caused by intermittent wiring faults or a failing sensor that drops out under vibration or temperature.

P2288.title: Injector Control Pressure Too High
P2288.plain: ICP is above the upper threshold during operation. Typically the injection pressure regulator (IPR) is stuck closed or the high-pressure oil pump runs above target.

P2289.title: Injector Control Pressure Too High - Engine Off
P2289.plain: ICP remains above threshold after engine shutdown — pressure does not bleed off as expected, indicating a stuck check valve or sensor offset error.

P228A.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A - Forced Engine Shutdown
P228A.plain: Fuel Pressure Regulator A - Forced Engine Shutdown: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

P228B.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B - Forced Engine Shutdown
P228B.plain: Fuel Pressure Regulator B - Forced Engine Shutdown: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

P228C.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low
P228C.plain: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

P228D.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too High
P228D.plain: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too High: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.
causes: Return path blocked or pump runaway

P228E.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too Low
P228E.plain: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too Low: the adaptive learning value has reached its lower limit, so the ECU can no longer compensate. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

P228F.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too High
P228F.plain: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too High: the adaptive learning value has reached its upper limit, so the ECU can no longer compensate. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

P2290.title: Injector Control Pressure Too Low
P2290.plain: ICP is below the lower threshold — typically IPR stuck open, leaking high-pressure oil rail, or weak HP oil pump.

P2291.title: Injector Control Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking
P2291.plain: During cranking, ICP does not build up enough to fire injectors. Typical no-start condition on HEUI engines from a stuck-open IPR or weak HP oil pump.
causes: HP oil rail does not pressurise

P2292.title: Injector Control Pressure Erratic
P2292.plain: ICP signal is unstable or jumps — connector or sensor issue, or air in the high-pressure oil rail. A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2293.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Performance
P2293.plain: The high-pressure fuel pressure regulator (volume control or pressure control valve on a direct-injection rail) is not maintaining commanded pressure. Often the rail-pressure sensor reading drifts away from the setpoint under load.

P2294.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Control Circuit
P2294.plain: Electrical fault on the control line to the high-pressure fuel pressure regulator solenoid. Without a working drive signal the rail cannot maintain pressure and the engine may not start or runs in limp-home.

P2295.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Control Circuit Low
P2295.plain: Drive voltage to the second fuel pressure regulator solenoid is below the lower limit. On common-rail diesels and direct-injection petrol engines this affects high-pressure fuel control directly.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2296.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Control Circuit High
P2296.plain: Drive voltage to the second fuel pressure regulator solenoid is above the upper limit — short to supply or open ground side. The driver protection trips, regulator falls back to default.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2297.title: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2297.plain: During engine deceleration with closed throttle (DFCO), the O2 sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 should swing fully lean as the manifold fills with fresh air. Code is set when the swing does not happen — usually a slow or coated sensor.

P2298.title: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2298.plain: During engine deceleration with closed throttle (DFCO), the O2 sensor on bank 2 sensor 1 should swing fully lean as the manifold fills with fresh air. Code is set when the swing does not happen — usually a slow or coated sensor.

P2299.title: Brake Pedal Position / Accelerator Pedal Position Correlation
P2299.plain: The ECU detects simultaneous brake and accelerator activation beyond a permitted threshold. Modern brake-throttle override safety logic forces idle in this state — usually triggered by a stuck brake light switch or a faulty pedal sensor.

P229A.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low
P229A.plain: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

P229B.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too High
P229B.plain: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too High: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.
causes: Return path blocked or pump runaway

P229C.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Learning Limits - Too Low
P229C.plain: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Learning Limits - Too Low: the adaptive learning value has reached its lower limit, so the ECU can no longer compensate. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

P229D.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Learning Limits - Too High
P229D.plain: The adaptive learning offset for fuel pressure regulator B has reached the upper limit. Long-term drift upward indicates progressive wear of the regulator or a return path that is becoming restricted.

P229E.title: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P229E.plain: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2): an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P229F.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 2
P229F.plain: The downstream NOx sensor on bank 1 (after the SCR catalyst) returns implausible NOx readings during operation. Either the sensor is degraded or upstream chemistry is abnormal.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P22A0.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A0.plain: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P22A1.title: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A1.plain: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P22A2.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A2.plain: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the signal is intermittent or erratic. Often a loose connector or chafed wiring; a wiggle test often locates it.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P22A3.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A3.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the control circuit is open. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P22A4.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A4.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P22A5.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A5.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P22A6.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A6.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2): an electrical fault is present in the circuit. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.

P22A7.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A7.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the signal is implausible or outside the valid range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P22A8.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A8.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the signal voltage is below the expected range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P22A9.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A9.plain: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the signal voltage is above the expected range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P22AA.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AA.plain: The feedback line that monitors the NOx sensor heater current draw on bank 1 sensor 2 jumps or drops out intermittently — connector loose or chafed wire near the exhaust heat zone.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P22AB.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AB.plain: The positive (sourcing) side of the O2 sensor pumping current control circuit on bank 1 sensor 2 is open. Wide-band O2 sensors regulate oxygen concentration in a reference chamber by pumping current; the positive line is open here.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P22AC.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AC.plain: O2 positive current line on bank 1 sensor 2 stuck low — short to ground. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P22AD.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AD.plain: O2 positive current line on bank 1 sensor 2 stuck high — short to B+. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P22AE.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AE.plain: The reference voltage line for the wide-band O2 sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 is open. The reference is used as the floating mid-point for the pumping cell.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P22AF.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AF.plain: O2 sensor reference voltage on bank 1 sensor 2 is in range but plausibility check fails — drift or instability.

P22B0.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B0.plain: O2 reference voltage on bank 1 sensor 2 below lower plausibility — short to ground. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P22B1.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B1.plain: O2 reference voltage on bank 1 sensor 2 above upper plausibility — short to B+. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P22B2.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B2.plain: The negative (sinking) side of the O2 sensor pumping current control circuit on bank 1 sensor 2 is open.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P22B3.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B3.plain: O2 negative current line on bank 1 sensor 2 stuck low — short to ground. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P22B4.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B4.plain: O2 negative current line on bank 1 sensor 2 stuck high — short to B+. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P22B5.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B5.plain: The pumping current trim line on bank 1 sensor 2 is open. The trim is the per-sensor calibration code that adjusts pumping current to compensate for production tolerances.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P22B6.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B6.plain: O2 trim line on bank 1 sensor 2 stuck low — short to ground. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P22B7.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B7.plain: O2 trim line on bank 1 sensor 2 stuck high — short to B+. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P22B8.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22B8.plain: The positive (sourcing) side of the O2 sensor pumping current control circuit on bank 2 sensor 2 is open. Wide-band O2 sensors regulate oxygen concentration in a reference chamber by pumping current; the positive line is open here.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P22B9.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22B9.plain: O2 positive current line on bank 2 sensor 2 stuck low — short to ground. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P22BA.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22BA.plain: O2 positive current line on bank 2 sensor 2 stuck high — short to B+. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P22BB.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22BB.plain: The reference voltage line for the wide-band O2 sensor on bank 2 sensor 2 is open. The reference is used as the floating mid-point for the pumping cell.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P22BC.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Performance (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22BC.plain: O2 sensor reference voltage on bank 2 sensor 2 is in range but plausibility check fails — drift or instability.

P22BD.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22BD.plain: O2 reference voltage on bank 2 sensor 2 below lower plausibility — short to ground. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P22BE.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 2)

Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

Component wear with age - mechanical play

P22C9.title: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Valve Stuck Closed

P22F1.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Heater Performance
P22F1.plain: The particulate matter (PM) sensor heater on diesel after-DPF systems does not reach or hold the calibrated operating temperature within the expected time. Without proper heating the PM sensor cannot be regenerated and read correctly.

P22F9.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response Low to High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P22F9.plain: NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 responds too slowly when NOx concentration rises (typically observed when SCR dosing is reduced or stopped). The sensor has aged or its protection cap is clogged.
causes: Sensor aged or protection cap clogged
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P22FA.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response High to Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P22FA.plain: NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 responds too slowly when NOx concentration falls (typically observed when SCR dosing increases). The sensor has aged or its protection cap is clogged.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P22FB.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Sensing Element (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P22FB.plain: The wide-band sensing element of the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 reports an internal performance fault — typically poisoning, condensate damage, or end of service life.
causes: Element poisoned or end of life
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P22FC.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response Low to High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22FC.plain: NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 responds too slowly when NOx concentration rises (typically observed when SCR dosing is reduced or stopped). The sensor has aged or its protection cap is clogged.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P22FD.title: NOx Sensor Performance Slow Response High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 2
P22FD.plain: The downstream NOx sensor on bank 1 (post-SCR) responds too slowly when NOx levels fall after a reductant injection event. The control unit measures the time between commanded reductant dose and the resulting NOx drop and finds it exceeds the diagnostic threshold, indicating an aged sensor element.
causes: NOx sensor element aged or thermally damaged
SCR efficiency reduced (catalyst aged or contaminated)

P22FE.title: NOx Sensor Sensing Element Bank 1 Sensor 2
P22FE.plain: NOx Sensor Sensing Element Bank 1 Sensor 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.
causes: Sensor element poisoned by silicone, sulphur or oil ash
Thermal shock from condensate (cold start with wet exhaust)
Sensor at end of service life

P22FF.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too Low
P22FF.plain: The temperature sensor at the SCR catalyst inlet reports a value below the threshold needed for efficient ammonia conversion. Below roughly 180-200 °C the SCR cannot reduce NOx and reductant injection is suspended; if this is detected continuously the ECU sets the fault.
causes: Temperature sensor drifts low or has shifted resistance
Short-trip operation - exhaust never reaches operating temperature
Exhaust heater or heat-management strategy not active

P2300.title: Ignition Coil A Primary Control Circuit Low
P2300.plain: The primary control circuit of ignition coil A reads a voltage below the expected level — usually a short to ground on the primary driver wire or a low-resistance fault in the coil primary winding. Coil A cannot build a normal charge, so the cylinder it fires misfires, especially under load. Causes: short to ground in the primary wiring, an internal coil primary fault, or a faulty ECU/igniter driver.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2301.title: Ignition Coil A Primary Control Circuit High
P2301.plain: The primary control circuit of ignition coil A reads a voltage above the expected level — typically an open primary circuit or a short to battery voltage on the primary control wire. The ECU sees no normal current flow, coil A does not fire, and the cylinder misfires. Causes: an open or disconnected primary wire, an internal open in the coil, or a faulty ECU driver.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2302.title: Ignition Coil A Secondary Circuit
P2302.plain: A fault is detected on the secondary (high-voltage) side of ignition coil A. The spark delivered to the plug is missing or too weak, causing a misfire on the cylinder served by coil A. Causes: a worn spark plug or wide gap, a cracked coil or boot, carbon tracking, or an open or leaking secondary winding.

P2303.title: Ignition Coil B Primary Control Circuit Low
P2303.plain: The ECU reads a low primary control voltage on ignition coil B. Misfire is typically observed on the cylinder this coil serves.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2304.title: Ignition Coil B Primary Control Circuit High
P2304.plain: Voltage on the primary control of ignition coil B exceeds the calibrated upper limit, indicating an electrical fault that prevents proper coil charging.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2305.title: Ignition Coil B Secondary Circuit
P2305.plain: The secondary side of ignition coil B is faulty. Spark energy at the corresponding spark plug is insufficient, producing misfires.

P2306.title: Ignition Coil C Primary Control Circuit Low
P2306.plain: The primary control of ignition coil C reads below the calibrated minimum. The cylinder served by this coil will misfire.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2307.title: Ignition Coil C Primary Control Circuit High
P2307.plain: The primary control voltage at ignition coil C exceeds the upper limit, suggesting a short to battery or an open primary winding.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2308.title: Ignition Coil C Secondary Circuit
P2308.plain: The secondary side of ignition coil C does not produce sufficient spark energy. Misfire is observed on the corresponding cylinder.

P2309.title: Ignition Coil D Primary Control Circuit Low
P2309.plain: Low primary control voltage on ignition coil D. The cylinder served by this coil will misfire if not corrected quickly.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P230A.title: Cylinder 1 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P230A.plain: The ECU continuously trims individual cylinders to equalise air-fuel ratio across the bank using ion-current or per-cylinder lambda feedback. For cylinder 1 the per-cylinder fuel correction has hit its software-side maximum or minimum without restoring balance, indicating the underlying mechanical or fuelling deviation is too large to compensate.
causes: Fuel injector for cylinder 1 has drifted in flow rate
Local intake or vacuum leak at cylinder 1
Partial misfire from ignition or fuel-side defect

P230B.title: Cylinder 2 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance Adjustment At Limit During Balance

P2310.plain: The ECU detects an excessive voltage on the primary control of ignition coil D, normally caused by a short to battery or an open primary winding.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2311.title: Ignition Coil D Secondary Circuit
P2311.plain: A fault is detected in the secondary side of ignition coil D. Insufficient spark energy results in cylinder misfire.

causes: Primary winding shorted to ground or harness chafed
Connector oxidised or loose at coil E

P2314.title: Ignition Coil E Secondary Circuit
P2314.plain: A fault is detected on the secondary (high-voltage) side of ignition coil E. The spark delivered to the plug is missing or too weak, causing a misfire on the cylinder served by coil E. Causes: a worn spark plug or wide gap, a cracked coil or boot, carbon tracking, or an open or leaking secondary winding.
causes: Spark plug worn, fouled or with excessive electrode gap

P2315.title: Ignition Coil F Primary Control Circuit Low
P2315.plain: The primary control circuit of ignition coil F reads a voltage below the expected level — usually a short to ground on the primary driver wire or a low-resistance fault in the coil primary winding. Coil F cannot build a normal charge, so the cylinder it fires misfires, especially under load. Causes: short to ground in the primary wiring, an internal coil primary fault, or a faulty ECU/igniter driver.
causes: Primary winding shorted to ground or harness chafed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2316.title: Ignition Coil F Primary Control Circuit High

The ECU sees no normal current flow, coil F does not fire, and the cylinder misfires. Causes: an open or disconnected primary wire, an internal open in the coil, or a faulty ECU driver.
causes: Open circuit in primary winding or harness for coil F
Control line shorted to battery or supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P231A.title: Cylinder 7 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P231A.plain: The ECU continuously trims individual cylinders to equalise air-fuel ratio across the bank using ion-current or per-cylinder lambda feedback. For cylinder 7 the per-cylinder fuel correction has hit its software-side maximum or minimum without restoring balance, indicating the underlying mechanical or fuelling deviation is too large to compensate.
causes: Fuel injector for cylinder 7 has drifted in flow rate

P2336.title: Cylinder 1 Above Knock Threshold
P2336.plain: The knock sensor channel for cylinder 1 has registered combustion noise above the calibrated knock threshold beyond what the spark retard map can correct. Often associated with low-octane fuel, EGR malfunction or carbon-induced hot spots.

P2337.title: Cylinder 2 Above Knock Threshold
P2337.plain: The knock sensor channel for cylinder 2 has registered combustion noise above the calibrated knock threshold beyond what the spark retard map can correct. Often associated with low-octane fuel, EGR malfunction or carbon-induced hot spots.

P2338.title: Cylinder 3 Above Knock Threshold
P2338.plain: The knock sensor channel for cylinder 3 has registered combustion noise above the calibrated knock threshold beyond what the spark retard map can correct. Often associated with low-octane fuel, EGR malfunction or carbon-induced hot spots.

P2339.title: Cylinder 4 Above Knock Threshold
P2339.plain: The knock sensor channel for cylinder 4 has registered combustion noise above the calibrated knock threshold beyond what the spark retard map can correct. Often associated with low-octane fuel, EGR malfunction or carbon-induced hot spots.

P233A.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator C Control Circuit Open
P233A.plain: The ECU detects an open circuit on the control line for the third (C) fuel pressure regulator. Either the regulator solenoid coil is internally open, the harness is broken, or the connector has lost contact - the ECU cannot drive the regulator and rail pressure cannot be controlled by this stage.
causes: Open circuit in harness or connector
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P233B.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator C Control Circuit Low
P233B.plain: Same as P233A but with the control line shorted to ground - the ECU measures a low voltage that does not match the commanded duty cycle.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P233C.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator C Control Circuit High
P233C.plain: Same as P233A but with the control line shorted to supply - the ECU measures a high voltage that does not match the commanded duty cycle.
causes: Control line shorted to battery or supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P233D.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit Open
P233D.plain: The supply line that powers the solenoid of fuel pressure regulator B is open. Without supply the regulator cannot operate and the ECU cannot maintain rail pressure on this stage; sets when the controller sees no current flow even with the solenoid commanded on.
causes: Supply line open or relay defective
Fuse for regulator B supply blown
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P233E.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit Low
P233E.plain: The supply line that powers the solenoid of fuel pressure regulator B is below the expected voltage with the regulator commanded active - typically a high-resistance feed, partial short to ground or weak relay contact.
causes: Supply feed has high contact resistance
Partial short to ground on supply line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P233F.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit High
P233F.plain: Same as P233D but with the supply line shorted to a higher potential than expected, so the ECU measures more voltage on the regulator B feed than the commanded level allows.
causes: Supply line shorted to a higher voltage rail
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2340.title: Cylinder 5 Above Knock Threshold
P2340.plain: The knock-sensor evaluation reports cylinder 5 above the knock threshold over a sustained window. The ECU retards ignition for that cylinder; persistent knock indicates poor fuel quality, carbon deposits or cooling issues.

P2341.title: Cylinder 6 Above Knock Threshold
P2341.plain: Same condition as P2340 but on cylinder 6 — sustained knock above the threshold with retarded ignition correction.

P2342.title: Cylinder 7 Above Knock Threshold
P2342.plain: Sustained knock above the threshold on cylinder 7 — usual causes are fuel quality, carbon deposits, or cooling issues at this cylinder.

P2343.title: Cylinder 8 Above Knock Threshold
P2343.plain: Sustained knock above the threshold on cylinder 8 — typical on V8 engines under load with poor fuel.

P2344.title: Cylinder 9 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold
P2344.plain: The knock or combustion-vibration sensor monitors the structure-borne noise of each cylinder. The signal level for cylinder 9 has stayed above the diagnostic threshold for an extended period, indicating either persistent knock or an electrical fault that biases the channel high.
causes: Persistent knocking on cylinder 9 (low-octane fuel, carbon deposits, hot spot)
Sensor or wiring biased high by short or moisture
Mechanical knock from bearings, piston pin or wrong torque

P2345.title: Cylinder 10 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold
P2345.plain: The knock or combustion-vibration sensor monitors the structure-borne noise of each cylinder. The signal level for cylinder 10 has stayed above the diagnostic threshold for an extended period, indicating either persistent knock or an electrical fault that biases the channel high.
causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

P2346.title: Cylinder 11 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold
