P2348.title: Cylinder 9 Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2348.plain: A general electrical fault on the cylinder 9 combustion pressure sensor — used on engines with closed-loop combustion control (e.g. some Volvo and BMW direct-injection diesels) to measure cylinder pressure directly via a sensor at the glow plug or injector position.
causes: Open circuit in sensor or wiring

P2349.title: Cylinder 9 Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2349.plain: Cylinder 9 pressure sensor reads in range but plausibility check fails. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Sensor signal implausible against engine model
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P234A.title: Cylinder 9 Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P234A.plain: Cylinder 9 pressure sensor below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P234B.title: Cylinder 9 Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P234B.plain: Cylinder 9 pressure sensor above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P234C.title: Cylinder 9 Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P234C.plain: Cylinder 9 pressure sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or wiring issue. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Intermittent contact at connector or terminal
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P234D.title: Cylinder 9 Pressure Too Low
P234D.plain: Cylinder 9 measured peak combustion pressure is below the calibrated minimum — typically low compression, weak injection, or stuck-open exhaust valve.
causes: Low compression on cylinder 9 (valves, rings, head gasket)

P234E.title: Cylinder 9 Pressure Too High
P234E.plain: Cylinder 9 measured peak combustion pressure is above the calibrated maximum — typically pre-ignition, knock, over-fuelling, or runaway combustion.

P234F.title: Cylinder 9 Pressure Variation Low
P234F.plain: Cylinder-to-cylinder pressure variation on cylinder 9 is below the calibrated minimum — pressure stays unusually constant cycle-to-cycle, often a sign that the closed-loop combustion controller has lost authority or the sensor signal is filtered.

P2350.title: Cylinder 9 Pressure Variation High
P2350.plain: Cylinder-to-cylinder pressure variation on cylinder 9 is above the calibrated maximum — combustion is unstable cycle-to-cycle, typical of partial misfire or injector seat erosion.

P2351.title: Cylinder 9 Combustion Performance
P2351.plain: The closed-loop combustion controller reports that combustion performance on cylinder 9 is below the calibrated quality metric. Computed from the cylinder pressure trace — IMEP (indicated mean effective pressure), CA50 (50% mass burnt angle) or peak pressure deviates from the model.
causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

P2366.title: Cylinder 12 Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2366.plain: A general electrical fault on the cylinder 12 combustion pressure sensor — used on engines with closed-loop combustion control (e.g. some Volvo and BMW direct-injection diesels) to measure cylinder pressure directly via a sensor at the glow plug or injector position.
causes: Open circuit in sensor or wiring

P2367.title: Cylinder 12 Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2367.plain: Cylinder 12 pressure sensor reads in range but plausibility check fails. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Sensor signal implausible against engine model
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2368.title: Cylinder 12 Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2368.plain: Cylinder 12 pressure sensor below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2369.title: Cylinder 12 Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P2369.plain: Cylinder 12 pressure sensor above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P236A.title: Cylinder 12 Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P236A.plain: Cylinder 12 pressure sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or wiring issue. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P236B.title: Cylinder 12 Pressure Too Low
P236B.plain: Cylinder 12 measured peak combustion pressure is below the calibrated minimum — typically low compression, weak injection, or stuck-open exhaust valve.

P236C.title: Cylinder 12 Pressure Too High
P236C.plain: Cylinder 12 measured peak combustion pressure is above the calibrated maximum — typically pre-ignition, knock, over-fuelling, or runaway combustion.

P236D.title: Cylinder 12 Pressure Variation Low
P236D.plain: Cylinder-to-cylinder pressure variation on cylinder 12 is below the calibrated minimum — pressure stays unusually constant cycle-to-cycle, often a sign that the closed-loop combustion controller has lost authority or the sensor signal is filtered.

P236E.title: Cylinder 12 Pressure Variation High
P236E.plain: Cylinder-to-cylinder pressure variation on cylinder 12 is above the calibrated maximum — combustion is unstable cycle-to-cycle, typical of partial misfire or injector seat erosion.

P236F.title: Cylinder 12 Combustion Performance
P236F.plain: The closed-loop combustion controller reports that combustion performance on cylinder 12 is below the calibrated quality metric. Computed from the cylinder pressure trace — IMEP (indicated mean effective pressure), CA50 (50% mass burnt angle) or peak pressure deviates from the model.
causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P2370.title: Fuel Volume Regulator B Control Circuit Open
P2370.plain: An open circuit is detected on the control line for the second fuel volume regulator (B) used on twin high-pressure-pump diesel systems. Without this regulator the high-pressure pump cannot meter fuel for its assigned cylinder bank, leading to rail-pressure faults and limp-home behaviour.
causes: Open in harness or connector to regulator B
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2371.title: Fuel Volume Regulator B Control Circuit Performance
P2371.plain: The ECU sees implausible feedback on the control loop for fuel volume regulator B - duty cycle does not match measured rail pressure response. The regulator either reacts too slowly, sticks, or has shifted from its calibration.
causes: Regulator stem sticking due to debris or wear
High-pressure pump wear changes regulator response

P2372.title: Fuel Volume Regulator B Control Circuit Low
P2372.plain: Same as P2370 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2373.title: Fuel Volume Regulator B Control Circuit High
P2373.plain: Same as P2370 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Control line shorted to battery or supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2374.title: Turbocharger Inlet Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P2374.plain: The pressure sensor at the inlet of the second turbocharger (B) - on twin-turbo or sequential-turbo systems - is reporting a circuit fault. The ECU cannot determine inlet pressure and falls back to a substitute value, which limits boost control accuracy on this stage.
causes: Open in sensor signal, supply or ground

P2375.title: Turbocharger Inlet Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range or Performance
P2375.plain: Same as P2374 but with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model under boost. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

P2376.title: Turbocharger Inlet Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P2376.plain: Same as P2374 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2377.title: Turbocharger Inlet Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P2377.plain: Same as P2374 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2378.title: Turbocharger Inlet Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P2378.plain: Same as P2374 but the signal is intermittent or has spikes that the ECU cannot reconcile - typically a wiring or connector fault.
causes: Intermittent contact at connector or terminal
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2379.title: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration Bank 2 Sensor 2
P2379.plain: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration Bank 2 Sensor 2: the control module has detected this fault condition. (Code P2379)
causes: Exhaust leak between catalyst and sensor

P237A.title: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1 Sensor 2
P237A.plain: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1 Sensor 2: the control module has detected this fault condition. (Code P237A)
causes: Sensing element or protective tube fouled with soot, oil or coolant
Sensor seal or thread leaks - bypass air dilutes sample

P237B.title: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 2 Sensor 2
P237B.plain: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 2 Sensor 2: the control module has detected this fault condition. (Code P237B)
causes: Sensing element or protective tube fouled
Sensor seal leaks - bypass air dilutes sample

P237C.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Open
P237C.plain: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Open: the control circuit is open. Likely a broken wire, disconnected connector, or failed actuator.
causes: Actuator solenoid or motor winding open
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P237D.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Low
P237D.plain: Same as P237C with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P237E.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit High
P237E.plain: Same as P237C with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P237F.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve A Control Performance
P237F.plain: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve A Control Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.
causes: Flap stuck due to soot or carbon deposits
Position sensor offset against actual flap angle

P2380.title: Wait to Start Lamp Control Circuit
P2380.plain: The ECU detects an electrical fault on the wait-to-start indicator output of the diesel preheat system. The driver may not get a correct preheat indication.

P2381.title: EGR Sensor D Circuit High
P2381.plain: EGR Sensor D Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2382.title: EGR Sensor D Circuit Low
P2382.plain: Same as P2381 but with the signal voltage below the plausible lower limit - typically the signal line shorted to ground or an internal sensor short.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2383.title: EGR Sensor D Circuit Range or Performance
P2383.plain: Same as P2381 but with the signal in plausible voltage range yet not matching the engine model - drift, partial blockage of the reference port, or a slow sensor.
causes: Reference port partially blocked by soot

P2384.title: EGR Sensor D Circuit Intermittent
P2384.plain: Same as P2381 but the signal is intermittent - typically a connector or harness fault. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: Intermittent contact at connector or terminal
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2385.title: EGR Sensor E Circuit
P2385.plain: A circuit fault is detected on the fifth exhaust-gas recirculation sensor (E). The ECU loses this EGR feedback channel and falls back to a substitute value; emissions and EGR rate accuracy on this stage are reduced until repair.
causes: Open in sensor signal, supply or ground

P2386.title: EGR Sensor E Circuit High
P2386.plain: EGR Sensor E Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2387.title: EGR Sensor E Circuit Low
P2387.plain: Same as P2382 on EGR sensor E. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2388.title: EGR Sensor E Circuit Range or Performance
P2388.plain: Same as P2383 on EGR sensor E. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P2389.title: EGR Sensor E Circuit Intermittent
P2389.plain: Same as P2384 on EGR sensor E. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P238A.title: Water in Fuel Sensor B Circuit
P238A.plain: A general circuit fault on the secondary water-in-fuel sensor B - typically used on diesel systems with two filter housings (pre-pump and post-pump). The ECU loses water-detection feedback on this stage; risk of water reaching the high-pressure pump and injectors.

P238B.title: Water in Fuel Sensor B Circuit Range or Performance
P238B.plain: Same as P238A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P238C.title: Water in Fuel Sensor B Circuit Low
P238C.plain: Same as P238A with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P238D.title: Water in Fuel Sensor B Circuit High
P238D.plain: Same as P238A with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P238E.title: Water in Fuel Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P238E.plain: Same as P238A with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P238F.title: Water in Fuel Condition Sensor B
P238F.plain: Sensor B reports water in the fuel filter housing - drain the water trap immediately. Continued operation may cause damage to the high-pressure pump and injectors.
causes: Water has collected in the filter trap

P2390.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Control Circuit Open
P2390.plain: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Control Circuit Open: the control circuit is open. Likely a broken wire, disconnected connector, or failed actuator.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2391.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Control Performance
P2391.plain: Same as P2390 with the actuator electrically intact yet not delivering the commanded position - sticky valve, broken linkage, or position offset.

P2392.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Control Circuit Low
P2392.plain: Same as P2390 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2393.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Control Circuit High
P2393.plain: Same as P2390 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2394.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Control Stuck Open
P2394.plain: Diesel intake air flow valve B is mechanically stuck open - the ECU cannot close it for anti-shudder shutdown or EGR mixing assistance.
causes: Valve stuck open due to soot or broken linkage
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2395.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Control Stuck Closed
P2395.plain: Same as P2394 with the valve stuck closed - intake airflow blocked even when the engine should run with full air.
causes: Valve stuck closed due to soot or broken linkage
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2396.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Position Sensor Circuit
P2396.plain: A general circuit fault on the position sensor of diesel intake air flow valve B.

P2397.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Position Sensor Range or Performance
P2397.plain: Same as P2396 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the actuator command.

P2398.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Position Sensor Circuit Low
P2398.plain: Same as P2396 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2399.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Position Sensor Circuit High
P2399.plain: Same as P2396 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P239A.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P239A.plain: Same as P2396 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P239B.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Control Motor Current Range or Performance
P239B.plain: The motor current of the actuator on diesel intake air flow B is outside the calibrated window - typically excessive (sticky valve), or too low (worn brushes).

P239C.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Control System High Air Flow Detected
P239C.plain: With diesel intake air flow valve B commanded closed the measured airflow is above the calibrated threshold - valve does not seat or position sensor offset.

P239D.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow B Control System Low Air Flow Detected
P239D.plain: Same as P239C with the airflow below the threshold when the valve is commanded open - valve does not open fully or the path is restricted.

P239E.title: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration Bank 1 Sensor 2
P239E.plain: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration Bank 1 Sensor 2: the control module has detected this fault condition. (Code P239E)

P239F.title: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration Bank 2 Sensor 2
P239F.plain: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration Bank 2 Sensor 2: the control module has detected this fault condition. (Code P239F)

P23A0.title: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1 Sensor 2
P23A0.plain: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1 Sensor 2: the control module has detected this fault condition. (Code P23A0)
causes: Sensing element or protective tube fouled

P23A1.title: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 2 Sensor 2
P23A1.plain: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 2 Sensor 2: the control module has detected this fault condition. (Code P23A1)
causes: Sensing element or protective tube fouled

P23A2.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve B Control Circuit Open
P23A2.plain: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve B Control Circuit Open: the control circuit is open. Likely a broken wire, disconnected connector, or failed actuator.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P23A3.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve B Control Circuit Low
P23A3.plain: Same as P237D on bypass valve B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P23A4.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve B Control Circuit High
P23A4.plain: Same as P237E on bypass valve B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P23A5.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve B Control Performance
P23A5.plain: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve B Control Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.
causes: Flap stuck due to soot or carbon

P23A6.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve B Stuck Open
P23A6.plain: Bypass valve B is stuck in the open position - exhaust bypasses the heat exchanger continuously, slowing engine warm-up.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P23A7.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve B Stuck Closed
P23A7.plain: Same as P23A6 with bypass valve B stuck closed - exhaust always passes through the heat exchanger.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P23A8.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Bypass Valve B Position Sensor Stop Performance
P23A8.plain: During calibration the position sensor of bypass valve B does not reach one of its mechanical end stops as expected.

P23A9.title: Communication Fault Forced Engine Shutdown
P23A9.plain: A safety-critical communication loss between control modules has triggered a forced engine shutdown. The ECU could not validate signals it needs to operate safely (e.g. throttle commands, brake state) and stopped the engine.
causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P23AA.title: Turbocharger Bypass Valve A Stuck
P23AA.plain: The turbocharger bypass valve A (compressor bypass for surge protection or wastegate-style boost relief) is mechanically stuck. Boost control is impaired - either no relief on overspeed or no boost build-up depending on which position the valve is stuck in.
causes: Valve stuck due to debris or actuator failure

P23AB.title: NOx Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23AB.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "NOx sensor processing, bank 1 sensor 3" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P23AC.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23AC.plain: A general circuit fault on the third NOx sensor of bank 1.

P23AD.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23AD.plain: Same as P23AC with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P23AE.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23AE.plain: Same as P23AC with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P23AF.title: NOx Sensor Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23AF.plain: Same as P23AC with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P23B0.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23B0.plain: Same as P23AC with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P23B1.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Open Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23B1.plain: The heater control circuit for the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 3 is open. Without the heater the sensor cannot reach operating temperature; readings stay invalid.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P23B2.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23B2.plain: Same as P23B1 with the heater control line shorted to ground. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Heater control line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P23B3.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23B3.plain: Same as P23B1 with the heater control line shorted to supply. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Heater control line shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P23B4.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23B4.plain: A general circuit fault on the heater sense feedback for the bank 1 sensor 3 NOx sensor - the line over which the ECU verifies that the heater is actually drawing current.

P23B5.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range or Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23B5.plain: Same as P23B4 with the sense voltage in plausible range yet not matching the heater model.

P23B6.title: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23B6.plain: The supply voltage to the bank 1 sensor 3 NOx sensor is outside the calibrated window.

P23B7.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Range or Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23B7.plain: Same as P23B1 with the heater control loop in plausible range yet not matching the heater model - aged heater or harness resistance.

P23B8.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23B8.plain: Same as P23B4 with the sense voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P23B9.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23B9.plain: Same as P23B4 with the sense voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P23BA.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Intermittent Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23BA.plain: Same as P23B4 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P23BB.title: NOx Sensor Heater Resistance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23BB.plain: The resistance of the NOx sensor heater on bank 1 sensor 3 is outside the calibrated band - aged element or contact resistance increased.

P23BC.title: NOx Sensor Calibration Memory Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23BC.plain: The NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 3 reports a calibration memory check-sum failure - factory calibration data corrupted or unreadable.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P23BD.title: NOx Sensor Performance Signal Biased or Stuck High Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23BD.plain: The NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 3 reports a value that stays at the upper end of its range despite changing engine conditions - sensor element biased or stuck high.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P23BE.title: NOx Sensor Performance Signal Biased or Stuck Low Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23BE.plain: Same as P23BD with the sensor stuck low.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P23BF.title: NOx Sensor Performance Slow Response Low to High Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23BF.plain: NOx Sensor Performance Slow Response Low to High Bank 1 Sensor 3: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.
causes: Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P23C0.title: NOx Sensor Performance Slow Response High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23C0.plain: NOx Sensor Performance Slow Response High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 3: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.
causes: Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P23C1.title: NOx Sensor Sensing Element Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23C1.plain: NOx Sensor Sensing Element Bank 1 Sensor 3: the control module has detected this fault condition.
causes: Sensor element poisoned by silicone or sulphur

P23C2.title: NOx Sensor Delayed Response High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 3
P23C2.plain: Same as P23C0 with a measurable delay before the sensor begins to track falling levels - the start of the response is delayed, not just the slope.

P23C3.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Position Sensor Circuit
P23C3.plain: A general circuit fault on the position sensor of the third engine coolant bypass valve C - typically used in advanced thermal management systems with multiple coolant loops.

P23C4.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Position Sensor Circuit Low
P23C4.plain: Same as P23C3 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P23C5.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Position Sensor Circuit High
P23C5.plain: Same as P23C3 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P23C6.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Control Circuit Driver Current or Temperature Too High
P23C6.plain: The driver stage of the coolant bypass valve C reports excessive current draw or thermal protection trip - typically a sticking valve drawing too much motor current.

P23C7.title: Fuel Heater Control Module Power Control Circuit Open
P23C7.plain: The control line that energises the fuel heater control module - used on diesel systems for cold-weather fuel preheating - is open.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P23C8.title: Fuel Heater Control Module Power Control Circuit Low

P23E1.title: EGR C Control Circuit Open
P23E1.plain: A general open-circuit fault on the third EGR valve C control - typically a third EGR loop in heavy-duty engines or specific Euro-7 systems.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P23E2.title: EGR C Control Circuit Performance
P23E2.plain: Same as P23E1 with the actuator electrically intact but not delivering the commanded position. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: EGR valve C sticking due to soot

P23E3.title: EGR C Control Circuit Low
P23E3.plain: Same as P23E1 with the control line shorted to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P23E4.plain: Same as P23E1 with the control line shorted to supply. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P23E5.title: EGR C Control Stuck Open
P23E5.plain: EGR valve C is stuck in the open position - exhaust gas continuously dilutes intake air, reducing power and risking misfires at idle.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P23E6.title: EGR C Control Stuck Closed
P23E6.plain: Same as P23E5 with valve C stuck closed - no EGR through this stage; NOx emissions rise. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P23E7.plain: Same as P049B on EGR loop C. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: EGR cooler C clogged with soot

P23E8.title: EGR C Flow Excessive Detected
P23E8.plain: Same as P049C on EGR loop C. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P23E9.title: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit Open Bank 2
P23E9.plain: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit Open Bank 2: the circuit is open. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P23F2.title: Cylinder 1 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23F2.plain: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 1 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.
causes: Injector B for cylinder 1 has drifted in flow rate

causes: Injector B for cylinder 2 has drifted in flow rate

causes: Injector B for cylinder 3 has drifted in flow rate

P23F5.title: Cylinder 4 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance

causes: Injector B for cylinder 12 has drifted in flow rate

P23FE.title: Bank 1 System B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FE.plain: The secondary fuel system B on bank 1 (e.g. port-injection rail in a dual-injection engine, or LPG/CNG rail in a bi-fuel system) does not maintain calibrated mixture - lambda response on bank 1 is biased by an offset on the B system.

P23FF.title: Bank 2 System B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FF.plain: The secondary fuel system B on bank 2 (e.g. port-injection rail in a dual-injection engine, or LPG/CNG rail in a bi-fuel system) does not maintain calibrated mixture - lambda response on bank 2 is biased by an offset on the B system.

P2400.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Open
P2400.plain: The control circuit to the EVAP leak-detection pump is open. Without that pump the ECU cannot pressurise the fuel-vapour system to test for leaks.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2401.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Low
P2401.plain: Drive voltage on the leak-detection pump line is below the lower limit. Often a short to ground in the harness.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2402.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit High
P2402.plain: Drive voltage on the leak-detection pump line is above the upper limit. Usually a short to supply or open ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2403.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Open
P2403.plain: The leak detection pump (LDP) - which actively pressurises the EVAP system to find leaks - has an open sense circuit. The ECU cannot read the pump status during the diagnostic cycle.
causes: Open in pump or sense wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2404.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2404.plain: The sense (reed-switch or current-feedback) signal from the leak-detection pump is electrically valid but does not match expectations during a leak test. Often a worn pump diaphragm or a sticking reed contact.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2405.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Low
P2405.plain: Same as P2403 with the sense voltage below the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2406.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit High
P2406.plain: Same as P2403 with the sense voltage above the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2407.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2407.plain: The leak detection pump returns a sense signal that is electrically valid but does not match the expected response during the pump's self-test or pressure cycle.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2408.title: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P2408.plain: On vehicles with a sensed fuel cap, the cap-status signal is electrically valid but does not change as expected when the cap is opened or closed.
causes: Cap seal aged, switch never seats
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2409.title: Fuel Cap Sensor or Switch Circuit Range or Performance
P2409.plain: The sensor or switch that detects whether the fuel cap is properly closed reports a value within plausible range yet not matching driver action.

P240A.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit Open
P240A.plain: The leak detection pump heater - keeps the pump diaphragm warm in cold weather - has an open control circuit.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P240B.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit Low
P240B.plain: Same as P240A with the control line shorted to ground. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P240C.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit High
P240C.plain: Same as P240A with the control line shorted to supply. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P240D.title: Alternative Fuel Low Pressure System Leak
P240D.plain: Alternative Fuel Low Pressure System Leak: a leak has been detected in this brake-hydraulic circuit, which reduces braking pressure. Safety-critical.

P240E.title: Alternative Fuel High Pressure System Leak
P240E.plain: Alternative Fuel High Pressure System Leak: a leak has been detected in this brake-hydraulic circuit, which reduces braking pressure. Safety-critical.
causes: Hose, fitting or cylinder valve leak

P240F.title: EGR Slow Response
P240F.plain: The EGR system reacts to commanded changes more slowly than calibrated - typically a partly clogged EGR cooler, sticky valve, or worn actuator.

P2410.title: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Stuck
P2410.plain: The fuel cap status switch is stuck in one position — the ECU never sees the expected transition between open and closed.

P2411.title: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Circuit
P2411.plain: A general electrical fault on the fuel cap sensor/switch circuit — open or short.

P2412.title: Fuel Cap Sensor or Switch Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P2412.plain: Same as P2409 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2413.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation System Performance
P2413.plain: The ECU monitors EGR flow indirectly through MAF, MAP or differential-pressure feedback and finds that actual EGR flow does not match the commanded value over a sustained period.

P2414.title: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2414.plain: Same as P237A but on the upstream sensor B1S1 (pre-catalyst). A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P2415.title: EVAP Switching Valve Circuit Open
P2415.plain: The ECU detects an open circuit on the EVAP switching valve drive line. The valve cannot be commanded between its purge and isolation positions.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2416.title: EVAP Switching Valve Performance
P2416.plain: The EVAP switching valve responds electrically but does not produce the expected pressure change. Often a stuck valve seat or a torn diaphragm.

P2417.title: EVAP Switching Valve Stuck Closed
P2417.plain: The EVAP switching valve cannot reach the open position. Purge flow is blocked and the EVAP system cannot vent the canister.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2418.title: EVAP Switching Valve Control Circuit Performance
P2418.plain: The evaporative switching valve — used on multi-path EVAP systems to route purge or pressure-test flow — does not respond as expected. Self-test fails because tank pressure does not change in the calibrated direction.

P2419.title: EVAP Switching Valve Stuck Open
P2419.plain: The EVAP switching valve cannot close. Tank pressure cannot be isolated for the leak detection test, and purge routing may bypass the canister.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P241A.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1 and Sensor 2
P241A.plain: The pre- and post-catalyst lambda signals on bank 1 are swapped - the upstream sensor responds like a downstream sensor and vice versa. Typically the harness was reversed during a sensor change.

P241B.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 2 Sensor 1 and Sensor 2
P241B.plain: The pre- and post-catalyst lambda signals on bank 2 are swapped - the upstream sensor responds like a downstream sensor and vice versa. Typically the harness was reversed during a sensor change.

P241C.title: Throttle Actuator Control System Ice Blockage Bank 2
P241C.plain: The throttle actuator on bank 2 cannot move because of ice formation - typical for very cold ambient temperature with humid intake. Engine de-ices on warm-up.

P241D.title: SCR Inducement Forced Engine Shutdown
P241D.plain: The SCR inducement strategy (mandatory regulatory measure to enforce AdBlue refilling and emissions compliance) has reached the final stage and shut down the engine. Refill AdBlue and clear inducement fault to restart.
causes: AdBlue tank empty or out of compliance

P241E.title: Reductant Heater Coolant Control Valve Stuck Closed
P241E.plain: The valve that routes engine coolant to heat the AdBlue lines is stuck closed - AdBlue lines do not warm up and may freeze in cold weather, blocking dosing.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P241F.title: EGR Cooler B Efficiency Below Threshold
P241F.plain: The temperature drop across EGR cooler B is below the calibrated threshold - cooler is fouled with soot, has internal scaling, or coolant flow is restricted. Recirculated gas reaches the intake hotter than designed, increasing NOx and combustion temperatures.
causes: Cooler fouled with soot or scaled

P2420.title: EVAP Switching Valve Stuck Closed
P2420.plain: The EVAP switching valve cannot open when commanded. Purge or test flow cannot reach the appropriate path and the leak monitor aborts.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2421.title: EVAP Vent Valve Stuck Open
P2421.plain: The evaporative emission system vent valve does not close on command. The ECU detects that the evap system cannot hold pressure or vacuum because the canister is permanently vented to atmosphere.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2422.title: EVAP Canister Vent Valve Stuck Closed
P2422.plain: The vent valve at the canister end of the EVAP system cannot open. Without ambient air entering the canister, fresh fuel cannot purge the stored vapors and refueling may trigger ORVR issues. Common with rusted or rodent-damaged vent valves.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2423.title: HC Adsorption Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P2423.plain: The ECU determines that the hydrocarbon adsorption catalyst on bank 1 no longer holds enough HC during cold start to meet emission targets. Often due to ageing or thermal damage.

P2424.title: HC Adsorption Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 2
P2424.plain: The hydrocarbon adsorption catalyst on bank 2 - which traps HC during cold-start until the main catalyst lights off - is degraded; HC slip during cold start is above the calibrated threshold.

P2425.title: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit Open
P2425.plain: The valve that admits coolant flow to the EGR cooler has an open control circuit - cooling cannot be enabled and EGR temperatures stay too high.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2426.title: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit Low
P2426.plain: Same as P2425 with the control line shorted to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2427.title: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit High
P2427.plain: Same as P2425 with the control line shorted to supply. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2428.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Too High Bank 1
P2428.plain: An EGT sensor on bank 1 reports a temperature above the safety threshold for prolonged operation - typical for blocked DPF, restricted exhaust, or excessive fuelling. Risk of catalyst, DPF or turbo damage.

P2429.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Too High Bank 2
P2429.plain: An EGT sensor on bank 2 reports a temperature above the safety threshold for prolonged operation - typical for blocked DPF, restricted exhaust, or excessive fuelling. Risk of catalyst, DPF or turbo damage.

P242A.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242A.plain: A general circuit fault is detected on the EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 3 (typically just downstream of the turbo or before the catalyst). The ECU loses thermal protection feedback for the catalyst and DPF.

P242B.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242B.plain: Same as P242A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P242C.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242C.plain: Same as P242A with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P242D.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242D.plain: Same as P242A with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P242E.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242E.plain: Same as P242A with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P242F.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Ash Accumulation Bank 1
P242F.plain: The diesel particulate filter on bank 1 reports backpressure attributable to ash (non-combustible residue from oil and fuel additives, not removable by regeneration). The filter has reached the end of its service life and needs cleaning or replacement.

P2430.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P2430.plain: A general circuit fault on the secondary air injection (AIR) system flow or pressure sensor on bank 1 - the sensor that verifies air pump flow during cold-start enrichment compensation.

P2431.title: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2431.plain: The ECU detects a general fault in the secondary air injection system air flow or pressure sensor circuit. The diagnostic cannot verify proper SAI operation.

P2432.title: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2432.plain: The signal of the SAI air flow or pressure sensor is implausible during operation. The reading does not change as expected when the air pump is commanded.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2433.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit High Bank 1
P2433.plain: Same as P2430 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2434.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 1
P2434.plain: Same as P2430 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2435.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 2
P2435.plain: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 2: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P2436.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 2
P2436.plain: Same as P2430 on bank 2 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P2437.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2
P2437.plain: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2438.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit High Bank 2
P2438.plain: Same as P2433 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2439.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 2
P2439.plain: Same as P2434 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P243A.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Ash Accumulation Bank 2
P243A.plain: The diesel particulate filter on bank 2 reports backpressure attributable to ash (non-combustible residue from oil and fuel additives, not removable by regeneration). The filter has reached the end of its service life and needs cleaning or replacement.

P243B.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 2
P243B.plain: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P243C.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Frequency Bank 2
P243C.plain: The DPF on bank 2 needs regeneration more often than calibrated. Possible causes are an oil-burning engine, fuel-injector leak, short-trip operation, or a sensor offset.

P243D.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Duration Bank 2
P243D.plain: Regenerations on bank 2 take longer than calibrated to complete - typically a low EGT during the cycle (cold weather, short trips) or a partially aged catalyst before the DPF.

P243E.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 2
P243E.plain: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P243F.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 2
P243F.plain: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P2440.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2440.plain: The switching/check valve in the secondary air injection plumbing on bank 1 is stuck in the open position. With the valve permanently open, exhaust gas can back-feed into the air pump and corrode it, while the downstream O2 sensor sees ambient air constantly.
causes: Switching valve stuck open by carbon or corrosion
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2441.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2441.plain: The switching valve on bank 1 will not open when commanded, so no secondary air reaches the exhaust during cold start. Catalyst light-off is delayed and emissions during the cold-start window rise.
causes: Switching valve stuck closed by carbon
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2442.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2)
P2442.plain: The switching/check valve in the secondary air injection plumbing on bank 2 is stuck in the open position. With the valve permanently open, exhaust gas can back-feed into the air pump and corrode it, while the downstream O2 sensor sees ambient air constantly.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2443.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 2)
P2443.plain: The switching valve on bank 2 will not open when commanded, so no secondary air reaches the exhaust during cold start. Catalyst light-off is delayed and emissions during the cold-start window rise.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2444.title: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck Off (Bank 1)
P2444.plain: The secondary-air pump does not run when commanded during cold start. Often a seized pump (after exhaust back-feed corroded the impeller), a blown fuse, or a failed relay.

P2445.title: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck On (Bank 1)
P2445.plain: The secondary-air pump continues to run after the cold-start window, when the ECU has commanded it off. Usually a stuck-closed relay welding the pump permanently to battery voltage.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2446.title: Secondary Air Injection Pump Stuck Off (Bank 2)
P2446.plain: Bank 2 secondary air pump does not deliver air when commanded. The catalyst light-off process is delayed and cold-start emissions rise.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2447.title: Secondary Air Injection Pump Stuck On (Bank 2)
P2447.plain: Bank 2 secondary air pump runs continuously. Either a stuck-on relay or a shorted control output keeps the pump powered when it should be off.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2448.title: AIR System High Air Flow Bank 1
P2448.plain: The secondary air injection system on bank 1 delivers more flow than calibrated when the pump is commanded on - typically a stuck-open switching valve allowing free flow.

P2449.title: AIR System High Air Flow Bank 2
P2449.plain: The secondary air injection system on bank 2 delivers more flow than calibrated when the pump is commanded on - typically a stuck-open switching valve allowing free flow.

P244A.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too Low
P244A.plain: The differential pressure across the DPF is below the calibrated minimum even at higher loads. Often a sign of a damaged or missing filter substrate, or a leak in the sensing line.

P244B.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Sensor Offset
P244B.plain: At engine off, the DPF differential pressure sensor does not return to zero within the allowed offset window. The static offset is too large to be ignored.

P244C.title: Exhaust Temperature Too Low For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 1
P244C.plain: During an attempted regeneration of the bank 1 DPF the EGT did not reach the temperature window needed for soot oxidation. Regeneration could not start or was held. Driving in higher load is needed.
causes: Engine load too low for regeneration

P244D.title: Exhaust Temperature Too High For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 1
P244D.plain: Same as P244C with the EGT too high - regeneration paused to protect filter substrate from melt damage.
causes: Engine load too high - filter overheating risk

P244E.title: Exhaust Temperature Too Low For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 2
P244E.plain: During an attempted regeneration of the bank 2 DPF the EGT did not reach the temperature window needed for soot oxidation. Regeneration could not start or was held. Driving in higher load is needed.
causes: Engine load too low for regeneration

P244F.title: Exhaust Temperature Too High For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 2
causes: Engine load too high - filter overheating risk

P2450.title: EVAP System Switching Valve Performance/Stuck
P2450.plain: The EVAP switching valve does not respond to commands as expected. The valve is mechanically stuck or unable to switch between purge and vent paths, blocking proper leak diagnosis.

P2451.title: EVAP System Switching Valve Stuck Closed
P2451.plain: The EVAP switching valve - which directs vapor flow between purge and leak-detection paths - is stuck in the closed position. The diagnostic cycle cannot complete.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2452.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2452.plain: A general electrical fault on the DPF differential-pressure sensor circuit. Without a valid pressure reading the ECU cannot estimate soot load and may inhibit regeneration.
causes: Sensor sample hoses clogged with soot

P2453.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2453.plain: The DPF differential-pressure sensor produces a value that is electrically valid but does not match expectations — for example a non-zero reading with engine off or no change between idle and load.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2454.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2454.plain: Voltage on the DPF differential-pressure sensor signal line is below the lower threshold. Typically a short to ground or an open in the supply line.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2455.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P2455.plain: Voltage on the DPF pressure sensor line exceeds the upper threshold. Usually a short to supply or an open ground on the sensor.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2456.title: DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P2456.plain: The DPF differential-pressure sensor delivers an intermittent signal — usually a marginal connector or a chafed wiring section that breaks contact during temperature or vibration.

P2457.title: EGR Cooler Performance
P2457.plain: The EGR cooler does not lower exhaust gas temperature as expected — typically internal coolant fouling, a partial blockage, or a cracked cooler that mixes coolant with exhaust gas.

P2458.title: DPF Regeneration Duration
P2458.plain: The DPF regeneration cycle takes longer than the calibrated maximum. The ECU sets this code when the soot load is not being burned off within the expected window — common after many short trips or with degraded post-injection.

P2459.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Regeneration Frequency
P2459.plain: Active DPF regenerations are being requested more often than the calibration window allows. Indicates that soot accumulates faster than the filter can burn it off — typically due to short-trip use, leaking injectors, or excessive engine oil consumption.
causes: High engine oil consumption (turbo seals, valve stems)

P245A.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Open Bank 1
P245A.plain: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 1 - routes EGR around the cooler during cold-start to keep cabin and engine warm-up fast - has an open control circuit.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P245B.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Range or Performance Bank 1
P245B.plain: Same as P245A with the actuator electrically intact yet not delivering the commanded position. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: Bypass valve sticking due to soot

P245C.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P245C.plain: Same as P245A with the control line shorted to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P245D.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit High Bank 1
P245D.plain: Same as P245A with the control line shorted to supply. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P245E.title: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P245E.plain: A general circuit fault on the secondary differential pressure sensor B across the DPF - measures backpressure for the regeneration strategy.

P245F.title: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range or Performance
P245F.plain: Same as P245E with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P2460.title: DPF Restriction — Forced Limited Power
P2460.plain: The DPF restriction has reached a level that forces the ECU to limit engine power. The driver must allow a forced regeneration or have the filter serviced before normal power is restored.

P2461.title: DPF Restriction — Forced Limited
P2461.plain: The DPF restriction has reached the limit defined for forced limited operation. Vehicle behaviour depends on the manufacturer — usually a hard torque cap with a service warning.

P2462.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Restriction - Soot Accumulation
P2462.plain: The DPF differential pressure sensor reports a backpressure rise consistent with excessive soot accumulation. The filter cannot regenerate fast enough, eventually causing limp mode.

P2463.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Restriction — Soot Accumulation
P2463.plain: The estimated soot mass in the DPF has crossed the upper limit and the ECU could not complete a regeneration to bring it back down. Very common on cars used on short trips. Continued driving in this state risks a runaway regeneration that destroys the filter.
causes: DPF heavily loaded after multiple aborted regenerations
Differential pressure sensor reading drifted high

P2464.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too High
P2464.plain: The differential pressure across the DPF exceeds the calibrated upper threshold during operation. Indicates severe blockage of the filter element.

P2465.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P2465.plain: The DPF differential pressure sensor signal is implausible compared to engine load and exhaust flow. Either the sensor or the pressure tubes leading to it are at fault.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2466.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2466.plain: A general circuit fault is detected on the EGT sensor at bank 2 sensor 3 (typically just downstream of the turbo or before the catalyst). The ECU loses thermal protection feedback for the catalyst and DPF.

P2467.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2467.plain: Same as P242B on bank 2 sensor 3.

P2468.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2468.plain: Same as P242C on bank 2 sensor 3. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P246A.plain: Same as P242E on bank 2 sensor 3. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P246B.title: Vehicle Conditions Incorrect for Particulate Filter Regeneration
P246B.plain: The driving pattern (short trips, low speed, frequent stops) does not provide the load and EGT needed for passive or active DPF regeneration. Filter loading rises until limit reached.

P246C.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 1
P246C.plain: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P246D.title: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A and B Correlation
P246D.plain: The two DPF differential pressure sensors A and B disagree by more than the diagnostic tolerance - one of them has drifted.

P246E.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 4
P246E.plain: A general circuit fault is detected on the EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 4 (typically just downstream of the turbo or before the catalyst). The ECU loses thermal protection feedback for the catalyst and DPF.

P246F.title: Reductant System Cold Start Performance
P246F.plain: At cold start the SCR system is unable to begin reductant dosing within the required time. Typical cause on diesel cars in winter — frozen AdBlue in the tank or lines, failed tank heater, or a slow-warming SCR catalyst.
causes: AdBlue frozen — tank or line heater not working
SCR catalyst slow to reach light-off

P2470.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2470.plain: The exhaust gas temperature sensor 3 on bank 1 (often after the DPF) shows intermittent dropouts. Erratic readings disturb DPF regeneration logic.

P2471.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2471.plain: EGT sensor 3 on bank 1 reports values that are not plausible for current operating conditions. Either drift or wiring resistance changes the signal away from the expected value.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2472.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2472.plain: The voltage from EGT sensor 3 on bank 1 is below the calibrated minimum. The signal indicates either a short to ground or a sensor returning impossibly low temperature.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2473.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2473.plain: The voltage of EGT sensor 3 on bank 1 is above the calibrated maximum. Often a sign of an open sensor circuit or a short to supply voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2474.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 2 Sensor 4
P2474.plain: Same as P242B on bank 2 sensor 4.

P2478.plain: The EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 reports a value outside its plausible operating range over time - typically a degraded element giving an offset that the substitute logic flags as implausible.

P2479.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Out of Range Bank 1 Sensor 2

P2480.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2480.plain: General electrical fault on EGT sensor 3 on bank 2. The ECU loses the temperature reference required for DPF regeneration management on bank 2.

P248A.title: Reductant Heater A Sense Circuit Low
P248A.plain: Reductant Heater A Sense Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) heater keeps the urea fluid from freezing; a fault can impair SCR dosing in cold conditions.
