P266C.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2
P266C.plain: The position sensor signal for actuator A on bank 2 is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P266D.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High Bank 2
P266D.plain: The position sensor signal for actuator A on bank 2 is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P266E.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 2
P266E.plain: The position sensor signal for actuator A on bank 2 jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P266F.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P266F.plain: The driver stage for the A/C refrigerant distribution valve A is in current limit or over-temperature. Sustained overload from a partially shorted load or excessive switching frequency.

P2670.title: Actuator Supply Voltage B Circuit Low
P2670.plain: The supply voltage to actuator group B (e.g. solenoids, valves driven by ECU) is below the calibrated threshold. The affected actuators may be slow or unable to switch.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2671.title: Actuator Supply Voltage B Circuit High
P2671.plain: The second actuator supply rail is above the expected voltage. Likely a charging system overvoltage or a short to a higher-voltage source.
causes: Wiring shorted to a higher-voltage circuit
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2672.title: Injection Pump Timing Offset
P2672.plain: The high-pressure injection pump timing is offset from the expected reference. On distributor pumps with a timing solenoid, the actuator does not match the commanded position.
causes: Worn timing actuator piston or seal
Stretched pump drive chain or belt

P2673.title: Injection Pump Timing Calibration Not Learned
P2673.plain: The injection pump timing learning routine did not complete successfully. Without learned values, injection timing runs from default tables and combustion is suboptimal.
causes: Learning routine aborted by other DTC or unstable conditions
Timing actuator drift outside learning window

P2674.title: Injection Pump Fuel Calibration Not Learned
P2674.plain: The injection pump fuel quantity calibration did not complete successfully. Without learned fuel calibration, AFR runs from default tables and emissions or smoke can rise.
causes: Learning routine aborted by other DTC or unstable conditions
Fuel quantity solenoid drift outside learning window

P2675.title: Air Cleaner Inlet Control Circuit / Open
P2675.plain: The controller cannot drive the air cleaner inlet control valve (warm-air or snorkel switching for cold-start emissions). Stuck in default position so cold-start fueling is sub-optimal.
causes: Open coil in inlet valve solenoid

P2676.title: Air Cleaner Inlet Control Circuit Low
P2676.plain: Voltage on the air cleaner inlet valve control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2677.title: Air Cleaner Inlet Control Circuit High
P2677.plain: Voltage on the air cleaner inlet valve control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2678.title: Coolant Degassing Valve Control Circuit / Open
P2678.plain: The controller cannot drive the coolant degassing valve. Air pockets in the cooling system can form and cause local overheating.

P2679.title: Coolant Degassing Valve Control Circuit Low
P2679.plain: Voltage on the coolant degassing valve control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P267A.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Bank 2
P267A.plain: The position sensor that confirms the B rocker arm switching state on bank 2 returns no usable signal.

P267B.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2
P267B.plain: The position sensor reading does not transition cleanly between the two valve lift modes for actuator B on bank 2.
causes: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn lock pin reduces travel between modes
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P267C.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2
P267C.plain: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 2 is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P267D.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High Bank 2
P267D.plain: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 2 is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P267E.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 2
P267E.plain: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 2 jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P267F.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P267F.plain: The internal temperature sensor of the control module shows intermittent jumps or dropouts. Module thermal protection may falsely activate or fail to activate when needed.
causes: Cracked solder joint at internal sensor
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2680.title: Coolant Degassing Valve Control Circuit High
P2680.plain: Voltage on the coolant degassing valve control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2681.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Control Circuit / Open
P2681.plain: The controller cannot drive the engine coolant bypass valve A. The valve usually routes coolant around the radiator during warm-up; without it warm-up takes longer and emissions during the warm-up phase rise.
causes: Open coil in bypass valve solenoid

P2682.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Low
P2682.plain: Voltage on the coolant bypass valve A control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2683.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Control Circuit High
P2683.plain: Voltage on the coolant bypass valve A control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2684.title: Actuator Supply Voltage C Circuit / Open
P2684.plain: The third actuator supply rail is open. All loads on this rail are powerless and report follow-on faults.
causes: Blown fuse on the supply rail
Broken supply wire from main relay

P2685.title: Actuator Supply Voltage C Circuit Low
P2685.plain: The third actuator supply rail is below the expected voltage. Battery weakness, blown fuse, or excessive current draw collapses the supply.
causes: Load on the rail shorted to ground
Battery condition causes voltage to drop
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2686.title: Actuator Supply Voltage C Circuit High
P2686.plain: The third actuator supply rail is above the expected voltage. Likely a charging system overvoltage or a short to a higher-voltage source.
causes: Wiring shorted to a higher-voltage circuit
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2687.title: Fuel Supply Heater Control Circuit / Open
P2687.plain: The controller cannot drive the diesel fuel filter or supply line heater. In cold weather diesel waxing can clog the filter.

P2688.title: Fuel Supply Heater Control Circuit Low
P2688.plain: Voltage on the fuel supply heater control line is below the expected window. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2689.title: Fuel Supply Heater Control Circuit High
P2689.plain: Voltage on the fuel supply heater control line is above the expected window. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P268A.title: Fuel Injector Calibration Not Learned/Programmed
P268A.plain: After injector replacement the engine controller did not receive the per-injector flow calibration codes (IMA, ISA, IMV). Cylinder balance and emissions are out of tolerance.
causes: Injector calibration codes not entered after replacement
Wrong codes entered for the wrong cylinder positions

P268B.title: High Pressure Fuel Pump Calibration Not Learned/Programmed
P268B.plain: After high-pressure pump replacement the engine controller did not receive the pump-specific calibration data. Rail pressure regulation runs from default values.
causes: Pump calibration codes not entered after replacement

P268C.title: Cylinder 1 Injector Data Incompatible
P268C.plain: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 1 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software. Calibration was applied for the wrong injector type or family.
causes: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P268D.title: Cylinder 2 Injector Data Incompatible
P268D.plain: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 2 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.
causes: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P268E.title: Cylinder 3 Injector Data Incompatible
P268E.plain: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 3 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.
causes: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P268F.title: Cylinder 4 Injector Data Incompatible
P268F.plain: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 4 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.
causes: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2690.title: Cylinder 5 Injector Data Incompatible
P2690.plain: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 5 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.
causes: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2691.title: Cylinder 6 Injector Data Incompatible
P2691.plain: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 6 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.
causes: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2692.title: Cylinder 7 Injector Data Incompatible
P2692.plain: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 7 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.
causes: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2693.title: Cylinder 8 Injector Data Incompatible
P2693.plain: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 8 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.
causes: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2694.title: Cylinder 9 Injector Data Incompatible
P2694.plain: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 9 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.
causes: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2695.title: Cylinder 10 Injector Data Incompatible
P2695.plain: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 10 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.
causes: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2696.title: Injector Data Incompatible
P2696.plain: Generic counterpart to the cylinder-specific incompatibility codes. The injector calibration data set as a whole does not match the controller software.
causes: Replacement injector set incompatible with software version
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2697.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Circuit / Open
P2697.plain: The 7th injector (HC dosing for DPF active regeneration) cannot be driven. Active regeneration cannot raise exhaust temperature, soot accumulates in the DPF.

P2698.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Performance
P2698.plain: The 7th injector responds to commands but does not deliver expected fuel during regeneration. Coking on the nozzle or worn pressure regulation reduces flow.
causes: Fuel pressure to the dosing line out of tolerance

P2699.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Circuit Low
P2699.plain: Voltage on the 7th injector control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P269A.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Circuit High
P269A.plain: Voltage on the 7th injector control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P269B.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Control Circuit / Open
P269B.plain: The control line for the aftertreatment glow plug (used on some diesels to ignite injected HC during DPF regeneration) is open. Active regeneration cannot start.
causes: Open coil in glow plug control relay

P269C.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Control Performance
P269C.plain: The aftertreatment glow plug control responds to commands but the resulting current draw is out of tolerance. Worn glow plug or high-resistance contact.
causes: Worn glow plug element raises resistance

P269D.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Control Circuit Low
P269D.plain: Voltage on the aftertreatment glow plug control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P269E.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Control Circuit High
P269E.plain: Voltage on the aftertreatment glow plug control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P269F.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Circuit / Open
P269F.plain: The aftertreatment glow plug element itself is open. No current flows even with the relay closed.
causes: Glow element burnt out from age or HC overload
Corroded terminal at the plug body

P26A0.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Performance
P26A0.plain: The aftertreatment glow plug heats but exhaust temperature does not rise as expected. Combustion of injected HC may not start.
causes: Aged glow plug heats slowly or unevenly
HC supply from 7th injector below required

P26A1.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Circuit Low
P26A1.plain: The aftertreatment glow plug current is below expected. Either the element is partially open or supply is undersized.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26A2.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Circuit High
P26A2.plain: The aftertreatment glow plug current is above expected. Internal short reduces resistance. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Internal short in the glow plug element
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26A3.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Range/Performance
P26A3.plain: The coolant bypass valve A responds to commands but the resulting coolant temperature behaviour is not as expected. Possibly stuck partially open or contaminated bore.
causes: Weak return spring fails to close fully
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P26A4.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit
P26A4.plain: The position sensor on the coolant bypass valve A returns no usable signal. Closed-loop control of bypass position is lost.

P26A5.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P26A5.plain: The bypass valve A position sensor reading does not correlate with commanded position. Sensor drift or worn linkage.
causes: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn linkage between actuator and valve
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P26A6.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Low
P26A6.plain: The bypass valve A position sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26A7.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit High
P26A7.plain: The bypass valve A position sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26A8.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P26A8.plain: The bypass valve A position sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P26A9.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Stop/Minimum Stop Performance
P26A9.plain: During self-calibration the bypass valve A position sensor never reached the minimum mechanical stop. The position reference cannot be zeroed.
causes: Sediment prevents valve from reaching minimum stop
Sensor not aligned with valve shaft

P26AA.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Maximum Stop Performance
P26AA.plain: During self-calibration the bypass valve A position sensor never reached the maximum mechanical stop.
causes: Sediment prevents valve from reaching maximum stop
Sensor not aligned with valve shaft

P26AB.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Stuck/Open
P26AB.plain: The coolant bypass valve A is stuck in the open position. Coolant always bypasses the radiator, leading to overheating under load.
causes: Valve seized open by sediment or wax

P26AC.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Control Circuit / Open
P26AC.plain: The controller cannot drive the second coolant bypass valve. The associated cooling sub-loop cannot be regulated.
causes: Open coil in bypass valve solenoid

P26AD.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Control Circuit Low
P26AD.plain: Voltage on the second coolant bypass valve control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26AE.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Control Circuit High
P26AE.plain: Voltage on the second coolant bypass valve control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26AF.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Stuck/Open
P26AF.plain: The second coolant bypass valve is stuck in the open position. Coolant always bypasses the second radiator path.

P26B0.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Range/Performance
P26B0.plain: The second coolant bypass valve responds to commands but the resulting coolant temperature behaviour is not as expected.
causes: Weak return spring fails to close fully
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P26B1.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Stuck Closed
P26B1.plain: The coolant bypass valve A is stuck closed. Coolant cannot bypass the radiator during warm-up so warm-up takes longer and emissions in the warm-up phase rise.
causes: Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26B2.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Stuck Closed
P26B2.plain: The second coolant bypass valve is stuck closed.
causes: Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26B3.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P26B3.plain: The first fuel shutoff valve is commanded on but does not open. Fuel cannot reach the engine via this path.
causes: Solenoid loses force from coil aging
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26B4.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Stuck On
P26B4.plain: The first fuel shutoff valve stays open when commanded closed. Fuel cannot be cut off via this path during a safety event.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26B5.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P26B5.plain: The second fuel shutoff valve is commanded on but does not open.
causes: Solenoid loses force from coil aging
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26B6.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit Stuck On
P26B6.plain: The second fuel shutoff valve stays open when commanded closed.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26B7.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Control Circuit / Open
P26B7.plain: The controller cannot drive the third coolant bypass valve.
causes: Open coil in bypass valve solenoid

P26B8.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Control Circuit Low
P26B8.plain: Voltage on the third coolant bypass valve control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26B9.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Control Circuit High
P26B9.plain: Voltage on the third coolant bypass valve control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26BA.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Stuck/Open
P26BA.plain: The third coolant bypass valve is stuck open.

P26BB.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Range/Performance
P26BB.plain: The third coolant bypass valve responds to commands but the resulting coolant temperature behaviour is not as expected.
causes: Weak return spring fails to close fully
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P26BC.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Stuck Closed
P26BC.plain: The third coolant bypass valve is stuck closed.
causes: Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26BD.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Control Circuit / Open
P26BD.plain: The controller cannot drive the fourth coolant bypass valve.
causes: Open coil in bypass valve solenoid

P26BE.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Control Circuit Low
P26BE.plain: Voltage on the fourth coolant bypass valve control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26BF.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Control Circuit High
P26BF.plain: Voltage on the fourth coolant bypass valve control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26C0.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Stuck/Open
P26C0.plain: The fourth coolant bypass valve is stuck open.

P26C1.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Range/Performance
P26C1.plain: The fourth coolant bypass valve responds to commands but the resulting coolant temperature behaviour is not as expected.
causes: Weak return spring fails to close fully
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P26C2.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Stuck Closed
P26C2.plain: The fourth coolant bypass valve is stuck closed.
causes: Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26C3.title: Internal Control Module Transmission Range Sensor Performance
P26C3.plain: The internal transmission range sensor inside the control module (used for redundancy on shift-by-wire systems) does not match the external sensor reading.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P26C4.title: Internal Control Module Clutch Pedal Performance
P26C4.plain: The internal clutch pedal interpretation logic in the control module does not match the external clutch switch state. Manual transmission start interlock or stop-start enable can misbehave.
causes: Signal corruption between switch and ECU

P26C5.title: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Circuit / Open
P26C5.plain: The controller cannot drive the exhaust flow control valve A (used for exhaust acoustics, EGR boost, or aftertreatment heating).

P26C6.title: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Circuit Low
P26C6.plain: Voltage on the exhaust flow control valve A control line is below the expected window. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26C7.title: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Circuit High
P26C7.plain: Voltage on the exhaust flow control valve A control line is above the expected window. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26C8.title: Chassis Control Module 1 Requested MIL Illumination
P26C8.plain: A chassis control module (typically active suspension, AWD coupling, or steering controller) has signalled an emissions-relevant fault and requested the engine controller to switch on the MIL.
causes: Active DTC stored in the chassis module
Communication loss interpreted as MIL request

P26C9.title: Chassis Control Module 2 Requested MIL Illumination
P26C9.plain: A second chassis control module has signalled an emissions-relevant fault and requested the engine controller to switch on the MIL.
causes: Active DTC stored in the chassis module
Communication loss interpreted as MIL request

P26CA.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Circuit / Open
P26CA.plain: The controller cannot drive the main electric coolant pump. Without flow the engine and aftertreatment will overheat under load.
causes: Broken control wire to the pump

P26CB.title: Engine Coolant Pump Performance/Stuck Off
P26CB.plain: The main electric coolant pump is commanded on but does not run.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26CC.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Circuit Low
P26CC.plain: Voltage on the engine coolant pump control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26CD.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Circuit High
P26CD.plain: Voltage on the engine coolant pump control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26CE.title: Engine Coolant Pump Overspeed/Air In System
P26CE.plain: The coolant pump speed feedback is higher than the commanded value with no resistance from coolant. Indicates air in the cooling loop or low coolant level so the pump spins free.
causes: Low coolant level due to leak or improper fill
Air pocket trapped in the cooling loop

P26CF.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module System Voltage
P26CF.plain: The integrated controller of the smart coolant pump reports a system voltage out of operating range.
causes: Weak battery sags voltage under pump load

P26D0.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module System Voltage Low
P26D0.plain: The smart coolant pump module reports the system voltage below operating range. Pump output is reduced or disabled to protect the module.
causes: Weak battery sags voltage under load

P26D1.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module System Voltage High
P26D1.plain: The smart coolant pump module reports the system voltage above operating range. Pump output is reduced or disabled to protect the module.
causes: Alternator regulator failed to limit output
Load dump transient after disconnecting a heavy load

P26D2.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module Over Temperature
P26D2.plain: The smart coolant pump controller has reached over-temperature. Sustained high duty or insufficient cooling air flow.
causes: Sustained high duty cycle from cooling demand
Cooling air channel blocked by debris

P26D3.title: Engine Coolant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit
P26D3.plain: The dedicated supply voltage line to the coolant pump module is faulty. Pump cannot operate without battery feed.

P26D4.title: Engine Coolant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P26D4.plain: The dedicated supply voltage to the coolant pump module is below operating range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Weak battery sags under pump current
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26D5.title: Engine Coolant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit High
P26D5.plain: The dedicated supply voltage to the coolant pump module is above operating range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Alternator regulator failed to limit output
Wiring shorted to a higher-voltage circuit
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26D6.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Control Circuit / Open
P26D6.plain: The mechanical clutch on a belt-driven coolant pump (used to disengage the pump for fast warm-up) cannot be driven. Pump always engaged so warm-up takes longer.

P26D7.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Performance/Stuck Off
P26D7.plain: The coolant pump clutch is commanded on but does not engage. Coolant flow is missing under load, leading to overheating.
causes: Worn friction surfaces enlarge air gap
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26D8.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Stuck On
P26D8.plain: The coolant pump clutch remains engaged when commanded off. Pump runs continuously, slowing warm-up and increasing parasitic load.
causes: Armature plate seized to the pulley face
Driver stuck on keeps clutch energised
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26D9.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Control Circuit Low
P26D9.plain: Voltage on the coolant pump clutch control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26DA.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Control Circuit High
P26DA.plain: Voltage on the coolant pump clutch control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26DB.title: Engine Sound Control A Circuit / Open
P26DB.plain: The active engine sound generator A (Active Sound Design or AVAS — Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System for EV/hybrid) cannot be driven. EV pedestrian warning sound or sport-mode engine sound is missing.
causes: Open output stage in the sound amplifier

P26DC.title: Engine Sound Control A Circuit Low
P26DC.plain: Voltage on the sound generator A control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26DD.title: Engine Sound Control A Circuit High
P26DD.plain: Voltage on the sound generator A control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26DE.title: Engine Sound Control A Circuit Performance
P26DE.plain: The sound generator A circuit responds to commands but the resulting acoustic feedback is not as expected. Speaker damage or feedback path noise.
causes: Speaker cone damaged or coil shorted

P26DF.title: Sensor Power Supply D Circuit / Open
P26DF.plain: The 5 V supply rail D for sensors is open. All sensors fed from this rail report invalid readings.
causes: Open wire on the supply rail
Open inside the ECU regulator output

P26E0.title: Sensor Power Supply D Circuit Low
P26E0.plain: The 5 V supply rail D is below the expected level. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Sensor on the rail shorted internally to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E1.title: Sensor Power Supply D Circuit High
P26E1.plain: The 5 V supply rail D is above the expected level. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Reference wire shorted to a B+ supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E2.title: Fuel Mode Indicator Lamp Control Circuit Low
P26E2.plain: Voltage on the fuel mode indicator lamp control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E3.title: Fuel Mode Indicator Lamp Control Circuit High
P26E3.plain: Voltage on the fuel mode indicator lamp control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E4.title: Starter Relay B Circuit
P26E4.plain: The control circuit for the secondary starter relay (used on twin-starter heavy diesels or stop-start systems with a dedicated stop-start starter) returns no usable signal.

P26E5.title: Starter Relay B Circuit Low
P26E5.plain: Voltage on the secondary starter relay control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E6.title: Starter Relay B Circuit High
P26E6.plain: Voltage on the secondary starter relay control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E7.title: Actuator Supply Voltage D Circuit / Open
P26E7.plain: The fourth actuator supply rail is open. All loads on this rail are powerless and report follow-on faults.
causes: Blown fuse on the supply rail
Broken supply wire from main relay

P26E8.title: Actuator Supply Voltage D Circuit Low
P26E8.plain: The fourth actuator supply rail is below the expected voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Load on the rail shorted to ground
Battery condition causes voltage to drop
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E9.title: Actuator Supply Voltage D Circuit High
P26E9.plain: The fourth actuator supply rail is above the expected voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Wiring shorted to a higher-voltage circuit
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26EA.title: Fuel Pump Control Module B
P26EA.plain: A general fault in the second fuel pump control module (smart pump controller, separate from the ECU). Internal self-test failed or communication with the ECU is degraded.
causes: Internal fault in the pump module

P26EB.title: Alternative Fuel Control Module System Voltage
P26EB.plain: The alternative fuel control module reports a system voltage out of operating range. CNG, LPG, or hydrogen fuelling can be disabled until voltage is in spec.
causes: Weak battery sags voltage under load

P26EC.title: Engine Sound Control B Circuit / Open
P26EC.plain: The second active sound generator (B) cannot be driven.
causes: Open output stage in the sound amplifier

P26ED.title: Engine Sound Control B Circuit Low
P26ED.plain: Voltage on the sound generator B control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26EE.title: Engine Sound Control B Circuit High
P26EE.plain: Voltage on the sound generator B control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26EF.title: Engine Sound Control B Circuit Performance
P26EF.plain: The sound generator B circuit responds but the resulting acoustic feedback is not as expected.
causes: Speaker cone damaged or coil shorted

P26F0.title: Starter Relay A Stuck On
P26F0.plain: The first starter relay stays closed when commanded off. Starter motor remains engaged after the engine is running, which can destroy the starter pinion or ring gear.
causes: Relay contacts welded shut by inrush current
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26F1.title: Starter Relay A Stuck Off
P26F1.plain: The first starter relay does not close when commanded on. Starter motor cannot crank, the engine will not start.
causes: Burned relay contacts no longer make contact
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26F2.title: Starter Relay B Stuck On
P26F2.plain: The second starter relay stays closed when commanded off. Starter motor B remains engaged after the engine is running, which can destroy the starter pinion or ring gear.
causes: Relay contacts welded shut by inrush current
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26F3.title: Starter Relay B Stuck Off
P26F3.plain: The second starter relay does not close when commanded on. The associated starter motor cannot crank.
causes: Burned relay contacts no longer make contact
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26F4.title: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit / Open
P26F4.plain: The controller cannot drive the third electric coolant pump. Cooling demand of the connected loop (often hybrid power electronics or battery cooling) is not satisfied.
causes: Broken control wire to the pump

P26F5.title: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit Low
P26F5.plain: Voltage on the third coolant pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.
causes: Internal short in pump motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26F6.title: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit High
P26F6.plain: Voltage on the third coolant pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor winding.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26F7.title: Coolant Pump C Supply Voltage Circuit
P26F7.plain: The dedicated supply voltage line to the third coolant pump module is faulty. Pump cannot operate without battery feed.

P26F8.title: Coolant Pump C Stuck/Stalled
P26F8.plain: The third coolant pump is commanded on but the rotor does not turn. Sediment, frozen coolant, or a foreign object jams the impeller.
causes: Impeller jammed by sediment or debris
Pump motor seized by bearing failure

P26F9.title: Coolant Pump C Control Module Overtemperature
P26F9.plain: The smart controller of the third coolant pump has reached over-temperature. Sustained high duty or insufficient cooling air flow around the pump electronics.
causes: Sustained high duty cycle from cooling demand
Cooling air channel around pump blocked by debris

P26FA.title: Coolant Pump C Overspeed/Air in System
P26FA.plain: The third coolant pump speed feedback is higher than commanded with no resistance from coolant. Indicates air in the cooling loop or low coolant level so the pump spins free.
causes: Low coolant level due to leak or improper fill
Air pocket trapped in the cooling loop

P26FB.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Stuck Closed Bank 1
P26FB.plain: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 1 is stuck in the closed position. EGR gas always passes through the cooler, which slows engine warm-up and can degrade cold-start emissions.
causes: Valve flap seized closed by soot
Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26FC.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Stuck Closed Bank 2
P26FC.plain: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 2 is stuck in the closed position. EGR gas always passes through the cooler, slowing engine warm-up and degrading cold-start emissions.
causes: Valve flap seized closed by soot
Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26FD.title: A/C Compressor Internal Control Module Performance
P26FD.plain: The internal control module of an electrically driven A/C compressor (typical on hybrid and BEV vehicles) reports an internal performance fault. Compressor capacity may be reduced or shut down.
causes: Internal fault in compressor inverter electronics
Software error in compressor control logic
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P26FE.title: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Performance
P26FE.plain: The exhaust flow control valve A responds to commands but the resulting flow or back-pressure does not match expectations. Worn flap or carbon coking on the bore.

P26FF.title: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 2
P26FF.plain: During controller auto-configuration the expected throttle input on bank 2 was not detected. Configuration cannot complete and the second throttle path cannot be used.
causes: Broken signal wire from throttle B2
Hardware variant mismatch — sensor not installed

P2700.title: Transmission Friction Element A Apply Time Range/Performance
P2700.plain: The transmission control module measured an apply time for friction element A (clutch or band) outside the calibrated window. Indicates worn clutch material, low line pressure, or a degrading shift solenoid.

P2701.title: Transmission Friction Element B Apply Time Range/Performance
P2701.plain: The time required to apply friction element B (a clutch or band inside the automatic transmission) is outside the expected window. Either too long (worn clutch, low pressure) or too short (sticky valve, mis-calibration).
causes: Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

P2702.title: Transmission Friction Element C Apply Time Range/Performance
P2702.plain: The time required to apply friction element C is outside the expected window. Worn clutch, low pressure, or sticky valve.
causes: Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

P2703.title: Transmission Friction Element D Apply Time Range/Performance
P2703.plain: The time required to apply friction element D is outside the expected window.
causes: Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

P2704.title: Transmission Friction Element E Apply Time Range/Performance
P2704.plain: The time required to apply friction element E is outside the expected window.
causes: Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

P2705.title: Transmission Friction Element F Apply Time Range/Performance
P2705.plain: The time required to apply friction element F is outside the expected window.
causes: Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

P2706.title: Shift Solenoid F
P2706.plain: A general fault in shift solenoid F (the sixth gear-selection solenoid in 6-speed and higher transmissions). Detected through electrical resistance, hydraulic response, or downstream gear engagement check.
causes: Worn valve body bore around the solenoid

P2707.title: Shift Solenoid F Performance/Stuck Off
P2707.plain: Shift solenoid F is commanded on but does not produce the expected hydraulic response. Spool stuck closed or hydraulic apply circuit blocked.
causes: Solenoid spool stuck in closed position
Apply circuit blocked by debris in valve body
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2708.title: Shift Solenoid F Stuck On
P2708.plain: Shift solenoid F stays in the activated state when commanded off. Affected gear stays applied so the transmission cannot shift correctly.
causes: Solenoid spool stuck in open position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2709.title: Shift Solenoid F Electrical
P2709.plain: Electrical fault in shift solenoid F — open or shorted coil, or short to ground/battery in the harness.
causes: Short to ground or battery in the harness

P270A.title: Transmission Friction Element A Temperature Too High
P270A.plain: Friction element A inside the automatic transmission has reached over-temperature. Excessive slip during shifts or trailer towing burns the clutch.
causes: Excessive slip due to worn clutch or low pressure
Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

P270B.title: Transmission Friction Element B Temperature Too High
P270B.plain: Friction element B inside the automatic transmission has reached over-temperature.
causes: Excessive slip due to worn clutch or low pressure
Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

P270C.title: Transmission Friction Element C Temperature Too High
P270C.plain: Friction element C inside the automatic transmission has reached over-temperature.
causes: Excessive slip due to worn clutch or low pressure
Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

P270D.title: Transmission Friction Element D Temperature Too High
P270D.plain: Friction element D inside the automatic transmission has reached over-temperature.
causes: Excessive slip due to worn clutch or low pressure
Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

P270E.title: Transmission Friction Element E Temperature Too High
P270E.plain: Friction element E inside the automatic transmission has reached over-temperature.
causes: Excessive slip due to worn clutch or low pressure
Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

P270F.title: Transmission Friction Element F Temperature Too High
P270F.plain: Friction element F inside the automatic transmission has reached over-temperature.
causes: Excessive slip due to worn clutch or low pressure
Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

P2710.title: Shift Solenoid F Intermittent
P2710.plain: Shift solenoid F shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic faults that come and go. Loose connector or marginal coil.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2711.title: Unexpected Mechanical Gear Disengagement
P2711.plain: The transmission disengaged mechanically without a corresponding command. The vehicle can free-wheel, which is a safety concern. Often a hydraulic or hardware fault inside the gearbox.
causes: Clutch piston seal failure releases gear

P2712.title: Hydraulic Power Unit Leakage
P2712.plain: The transmission hydraulic power unit (pump + accumulator) has detected a pressure drop that suggests internal leakage. Pressure cannot be held during shifts.
causes: Worn or hardened seals in the valve body
Worn hydraulic pump cannot maintain pressure

P2713.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D
P2713.plain: A general fault in pressure control solenoid D. Detected via electrical resistance, response to commanded duty cycle, or downstream pressure measurement.
causes: Worn valve body bore around the solenoid

P2714.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Performance/Stuck Off
P2714.plain: Pressure control solenoid D is commanded on but does not produce the expected pressure. Spool stuck closed or hydraulic feed restricted.
causes: Solenoid spool stuck in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2715.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Stuck On
P2715.plain: Pressure control solenoid D stays in the activated state when commanded off. Affected hydraulic circuit stays pressurised.
causes: Solenoid spool stuck in open position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2716.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Electrical
P2716.plain: The TCM detects an electrical fault on transmission pressure control solenoid D. Hydraulic pressure cannot be modulated as expected, causing harsh or slipping shifts.

P2717.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Intermittent
P2717.plain: Pressure control solenoid D shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic faults. Loose connector or marginal coil.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2718.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Control Circuit / Open
P2718.plain: The control line to pressure control solenoid D is open. The solenoid cannot be driven.

P2719.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Control Circuit Range/Performance
P2719.plain: The current through pressure control solenoid D does not match the commanded value within tolerance. Coil resistance drift or high-resistance contact.
causes: Coil resistance changed by thermal stress
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P271A.title: Park Pawl Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P271A.plain: The position sensor that confirms the park pawl A engagement state reads below the lower diagnostic threshold. Without confirmed park engagement the shift-by-wire controller cannot release the brake hold.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P271B.title: Park Pawl Position Sensor A Circuit High
P271B.plain: The position sensor for park pawl A reads above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P271C.title: Park Pawl Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P271C.plain: The redundant park pawl position sensor B reads below the lower diagnostic threshold. Redundancy for the park-engagement check is lost.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P271D.title: Park Pawl Position Sensor B Circuit High
P271D.plain: The redundant park pawl position sensor B reads above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P271E.title: Transmission Performance
P271E.plain: A general transmission performance fault. The transmission controller has detected behaviour outside acceptable bounds (slip, shift quality, ratio error) without a more specific cause.

P271F.title: Electronic Gear Shift - Position Not Learned
P271F.plain: The shift-by-wire controller did not complete the position learning routine for the gear selector. Without learned end stops the controller cannot map selector positions to gear requests.
causes: Learning routine aborted by other DTC or low voltage

P2720.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Control Circuit Low
P2720.plain: Voltage on the pressure control solenoid D control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2721.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Control Circuit High
P2721.plain: Voltage on the pressure control solenoid D control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2722.title: Pressure Control Solenoid E
P2722.plain: A general fault in pressure control solenoid E.
causes: Worn valve body bore around the solenoid

P2723.title: Pressure Control Solenoid E Stuck Off
P2723.plain: The TCM detects that pressure control solenoid E is stuck in the de-energised position. The corresponding clutch or band cannot be applied, leading to gear slip or loss of certain gears.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2724.title: Pressure Control Solenoid E Stuck On
P2724.plain: Pressure control solenoid E stays in the activated state when commanded off.
causes: Solenoid spool stuck in open position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2725.title: Pressure Control Solenoid E Electrical
P2725.plain: Electrical fault in pressure control solenoid E — open or shorted coil, or short to ground/battery in the harness.
causes: Short to ground or battery in the harness

P2726.title: Pressure Control Solenoid E Intermittent
P2726.plain: Pressure control solenoid E shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic faults.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2727.title: Pressure Control Solenoid E Control Circuit / Open
P2727.plain: The control line to pressure control solenoid E is open. The solenoid cannot be driven.

P2728.title: Pressure Control Solenoid E Control Circuit Range/Performance
P2728.plain: The current through pressure control solenoid E does not match the commanded value within tolerance.
causes: Coil resistance changed by thermal stress
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2729.title: Pressure Control Solenoid E Control Circuit Low
P2729.plain: Voltage on the pressure control solenoid E control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P272A.title: Transmission Range Select Motor Control Circuit
P272A.plain: A general fault in the transmission range select motor control circuit. The motor that physically moves the gear range selector (P-R-N-D) does not respond correctly.

P272B.title: Transmission Range Select Motor Control Circuit Current Too High
P272B.plain: The current through the range select motor exceeds the limit. Mechanism is binding or shorted.

P272C.title: Park Pawl Motor Control Circuit
P272C.plain: A general fault in the park pawl motor control circuit. The motor that engages or releases the park pawl does not respond correctly.

P272D.title: Park Pawl Motor Control Circuit Current Too High
P272D.plain: The current through the park pawl motor exceeds the limit. Park pawl mechanism binding or motor shorted.
causes: Park pawl mechanism binding from wear or corrosion

P2730.title: Pressure Control Solenoid E Control Circuit High
P2730.plain: Voltage on the pressure control solenoid E control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2731.title: Pressure Control Solenoid F
P2731.plain: A general fault in pressure control solenoid F.
causes: Worn valve body bore around the solenoid

P2732.title: Pressure Control Solenoid F Performance/Stuck Off
P2732.plain: Pressure control solenoid F is commanded on but does not produce the expected pressure.
causes: Solenoid spool stuck in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2733.title: Pressure Control Solenoid F Stuck On
P2733.plain: Pressure control solenoid F stays in the activated state when commanded off.
causes: Solenoid spool stuck in open position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2734.title: Pressure Control Solenoid F Electrical
P2734.plain: Electrical fault in pressure control solenoid F.
causes: Short to ground or battery in the harness

P2735.title: Pressure Control Solenoid F Intermittent
P2735.plain: Pressure control solenoid F shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic faults.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2736.title: Pressure Control Solenoid F Control Circuit / Open
P2736.plain: The control line to pressure control solenoid F is open.

P2737.title: Pressure Control Solenoid F Control Circuit Range/Performance
P2737.plain: The current through pressure control solenoid F does not match the commanded value within tolerance.
causes: Coil resistance changed by thermal stress
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2738.title: Pressure Control Solenoid F Control Circuit Low
P2738.plain: Voltage on the pressure control solenoid F control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2739.title: Pressure Control Solenoid F Control Circuit High
P2739.plain: Voltage on the pressure control solenoid F control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P273A.title: Transmission Friction Element G Apply Time Range/Performance
P273A.plain: The time required to apply friction element G is outside the expected window.
causes: Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

P273B.title: Transmission Friction Element H Apply Time Range/Performance
P273B.plain: The time required to apply friction element H is outside the expected window.
causes: Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

P273C.title: Gear Shift Control Module A Supply Voltage Low
P273C.plain: The shift-by-wire gear shift control module A reports a supply voltage below the operating range.
causes: Weak battery sags voltage under load

P273D.title: Gear Shift Control Module A Supply Voltage High
P273D.plain: The gear shift control module A reports a supply voltage above the operating range.
causes: Alternator regulator failed to limit output
Load dump transient after disconnecting a heavy load

P273E.title: Gear Shift Control Module A Over Temperature
P273E.plain: The gear shift control module A has reached over-temperature. Excessive switching activity, sustained high motor load, or insufficient cooling.
causes: Cooling air channel blocked by debris

P273F.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Over Temperature Condition
P273F.plain: The second transmission fluid temperature sensor reports an over-temperature condition. Transmission fluid is too hot in the area monitored by sensor B.
causes: Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

P2740.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Circuit
P2740.plain: The second transmission fluid temperature sensor returns no usable signal.
causes: Open sensor element or broken sensor wire

P2741.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2741.plain: The second transmission fluid temperature sensor reading is implausible against engine load and ambient temperature. Drift or stuck signal.
causes: Sensor not seated properly in the fluid path
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2742.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
P2742.plain: The second transmission fluid temperature sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2743.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
P2743.plain: The second transmission fluid temperature sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2744.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P2744.plain: The second transmission fluid temperature sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Loose connector or chafed wire.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2745.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit
P2745.plain: The intermediate shaft speed sensor B (used for closed-loop ratio control on planetary or DCT gearboxes) returns no usable signal. The controller cannot verify ratio change.
causes: Open sensor element or broken signal wire

P2746.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2746.plain: The intermediate shaft speed sensor B reading is implausible against expected speed from gear ratio and input shaft speed.
causes: Damaged tone wheel teeth produce missing pulses
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2747.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit No Signal
P2747.plain: The intermediate shaft speed sensor B produces no pulses while the shaft is known to be turning.
causes: Tone wheel sheared or rotating loose

P2748.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P2748.plain: The intermediate shaft speed sensor B signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2749.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit
P2749.plain: The third intermediate shaft speed sensor returns no usable signal. Used on transmissions with multiple intermediate planetary stages.
causes: Open sensor element or broken signal wire

P274A.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor C Circuit
P274A.plain: The third transmission fluid temperature sensor returns no usable signal.
causes: Open sensor element or broken sensor wire

P274B.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P274B.plain: The third transmission fluid temperature sensor reading is implausible. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Sensor not seated properly in the fluid path
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P274C.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor C Circuit Low

P28BE.plain: Ion current from cylinder 12 is below the expected window. Spark plug fouled, signal wire shorted to ground, or sensing path interrupted.
causes: Spark plug fouled with carbon or oil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P28BF.title: Cylinder 12 Ion Current Sense Circuit High
P28BF.plain: Ion current from cylinder 12 is above the expected window. Cross-coupled signal, biased reference, or sensor fault.
causes: Inductive cross-coupling from ignition coil primary
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P28C0.title: Ion Sense Module Supply Voltage Circuit

P28C1.title: Ion Sense Module Supply Voltage Low
P28C1.plain: Supply voltage on the ion sense module is below the expected window. Wiring shorted to ground, blown fuse, or upstream regulator fault.

P28C2.title: Ion Sense Module Supply Voltage High
P28C2.plain: Supply voltage on the ion sense module is above the expected window. Charging system overvoltage or upstream regulator fault.

P28C3.title: EVAP System High Load Purge Line B Performance

P28C4.title: Clutch A Phase U-V-W Circuit Low

P28C5.title: Clutch A Phase U-V-W Circuit High
P28C5.plain: The output stage for the clutch A BLDC motor reports a high phase voltage on at least one of the U/V/W phases. Short to B+ or interrupted load.

P28C6.title: Clutch A Phase U-V-W Circuit/Open
P28C6.plain: The output stage for the clutch A BLDC motor cannot drive current through at least one of the U/V/W phases. Open wire or open winding.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P28C7.title: Clutch A Phase U-V-W Performance
P28C7.plain: The phase currents of the clutch A BLDC motor do not match the commanded commutation pattern within tolerance. Sensor or driver synchronisation off.

P28C8.title: Clutch A Pump Motor Performance
P28C8.plain: The clutch A hydraulic pump motor does not produce the expected flow for the commanded speed. Worn pump, leakage, or aged motor characteristic.

P28C9.title: Clutch A Motor Overspeed
P28C9.plain: The clutch A actuator motor exceeds the calibrated maximum speed. Load on the motor unexpectedly low or rotor position offset.

P28CA.title: Clutch A Motor Underspeed
P28CA.plain: The clutch A actuator motor falls below the calibrated minimum speed for the commanded duty. High mechanical load or supply voltage low.

P28CB.title: Clutch A Motor Position Sensor Circuit/Open

causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P28CC.title: Clutch A Motor Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance

P28CD.title: Clutch A Pressure Sensor Circuit/Open

P28DE.title: Clutch B Pressure Sensor Circuit High

causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P28DF.title: Clutch B Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P28DF.plain: The clutch B pressure signal does not match plausibility checks against actuator commands. Sensor drift or installation offset.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P28E0.plain: The output stage for the shift motor reports a low phase voltage on at least one of the U/V/W phases. Short to ground or interrupted half-bridge.

P28E5.title: Shift Motor Performance

causes: Increased friction in gear actuator mechanism

P28E6.title: Shift Motor Overspeed
P28E6.plain: The shift motor exceeds the calibrated maximum speed. Mechanical load lost or rotor position offset.

P28E7.title: Shift Motor Position Sensor Circuit/Open

causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P28EB.title: Shift Motor Position Not Learned

causes: Adaptation lost after battery disconnect or TCM reset
Shift motor replaced without learn procedure

P28EC.title: Shift Motor Position Sensor Exceeded Learning Limit
P28EC.plain: The required adaptation offset for the shift motor position sensor exceeds the calibrated learning window. Sensor or mechanism out of nominal range.

P28ED.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Overspeed
P28ED.plain: The auxiliary transmission fluid pump B exceeds the calibrated maximum speed for the commanded duty. Mechanical load on the pump unexpectedly low.

P28EE.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Underspeed
P28EE.plain: The auxiliary transmission fluid pump B falls below the calibrated minimum speed for the commanded duty. Mechanical resistance high or supply voltage low.

P28EF.title: Engine Disconnect Clutch Actuator Performance/Stuck Off
P28EF.plain: The engine disconnect clutch actuator is commanded to engage but does not produce the expected motion. Actuator stuck in disengaged position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P28F0.title: Engine Disconnect Clutch Actuator Stuck On
P28F0.plain: The engine disconnect clutch actuator stays in the engaged state when release is commanded. Pure electric driving is not available.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P28F1.title: Engine Disconnect Clutch Pressure Sensor Circuit
P28F1.plain: The hybrid control module detects a generic fault on the engine disconnect clutch pressure sensor circuit. Engagement pressure cannot be monitored reliably.

P28F2.title: Engine Disconnect Clutch Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
