causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P28F5.title: Engine Disconnect Clutch Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P28F5.plain: The engine disconnect clutch pressure sensor signal drops out or jumps intermittently. Loose connector or noisy ground reference.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P28F6.title: Engine Disconnect Clutch Actuator Circuit Intermittent
P28F6.plain: The control circuit of the engine disconnect clutch actuator drops out intermittently. Loose connector or vibration-sensitive wiring.
causes: Harness chafing intermittently shorts the wire
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P28F7.title: Exhaust Pressure Too High Bank 1
P28F7.plain: The exhaust pressure measured on bank 1 exceeds the calibrated maximum. Common causes are clogged DPF, restricted exhaust path, or stuck exhaust brake/back-pressure valve.
causes: DPF clogged with soot or ash

P28F8.title: Exhaust Pressure Too High Bank 2
P28F8.plain: The exhaust pressure measured on bank 2 exceeds the calibrated maximum. Common causes are clogged DPF, restricted exhaust path, or stuck exhaust brake/back-pressure valve.
causes: DPF clogged with soot or ash

P28F9.title: Exhaust Pressure Too Low Bank 1
P28F9.plain: The exhaust pressure measured on bank 1 falls below the calibrated minimum. Common causes are leaks upstream of the sensor, missing DPF substrate, or sensor calibration drift.

P28FA.title: Exhaust Pressure Too Low Bank 2
P28FA.plain: The exhaust pressure measured on bank 2 falls below the calibrated minimum. Common causes are leaks upstream of the sensor, missing DPF substrate, or sensor calibration drift.

P2A00.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2A00.plain: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1: the signal is implausible or outside the valid range.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A01.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 2
P2A01.plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 1 does not show the expected slow steady-state behaviour after the catalyst. Either the sensor is degraded or the catalyst itself behaves abnormally.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A02.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2A02.plain: The optional third oxygen sensor on bank 1 (typically downstream of a second catalyst) returns implausible values during long-term monitoring.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A03.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2A03.plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 2 reacts too slowly or shows insufficient signal swing during closed-loop fuel control.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A04.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 2
P2A04.plain: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 2 shows abnormal behaviour during long-term plausibility evaluation. Often a sign of an aged sensor or weakened catalyst.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A05.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2A05.plain: The third oxygen sensor on bank 2 (after a second catalyst stage on some vehicles) returns implausible values. Often related to sensor aging or mechanical exhaust leak upstream.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A06.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 4
P2A06.plain: The fourth oxygen sensor on bank 1, where present, returns implausible values during long-term plausibility evaluation. Used on multi-stage aftertreatment systems.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A07.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 4
P2A07.plain: The fourth oxygen sensor on bank 2 returns values outside the expected long-term performance window during plausibility checks.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A08.title: O2 Sensor Negative Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2A08.plain: The ECM detects a negative voltage on the signal line of oxygen sensor 3 on bank 1. This is unusual for narrow-band sensors and often indicates a short to a negative reference, ground offset, or a wide-band sensor wired incorrectly.
causes: Signal wire shorted to negative reference
Ground offset between sensor and ECM

P2A09.title: O2 Sensor Negative Voltage Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2A09.plain: The ECM detects a negative voltage on the signal line of oxygen sensor 1 on bank 2. This is unusual for narrow-band sensors and often indicates a short to a negative reference, ground offset, or a wide-band sensor wired incorrectly.
causes: Signal wire shorted to negative reference
Ground offset between sensor and ECM

P2A0A.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P2A0A.plain: The ECM detects a generic fault on the secondary manifold absolute pressure sensor (MAP B). Air load estimation cannot be cross-checked.

P2A0B.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2A0B.plain: The MAP B signal does not correlate with TPS, MAF, or RPM as expected. Vacuum leak, restricted port, or sensor drift.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A0C.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P2A0C.plain: Voltage on the MAP B signal line is below the expected window. Wire shorted to ground or sensor short.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2A0D.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P2A0D.plain: Voltage on the MAP B signal line is above the expected window. Wire shorted to B+ or sensor open. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2A0E.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2A0E.plain: The MAP B signal drops out or jumps intermittently. Loose connector or noisy ground reference. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2A0F.title: Fuel Supply Heater Performance
P2A0F.plain: The fuel supply heater does not raise fuel temperature within the calibrated time window. Common in diesel and biofuel installations to prevent paraffin or fat crystallisation in cold weather.

P2A10.title: O2 Sensor Negative Voltage Bank 2 Sensor 2

causes: Signal wire shorted to negative reference
Ground offset between sensor and ECM

P2A33.title: AFCM Power Relay Control Circuit Low

causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2A34.title: AFCM Power Relay Control Circuit High

P2A35.title: AFCM Power Relay Sense Circuit
P2A35.plain: The AFCM detects a generic fault on the sense feedback line of its power relay. Relay state cannot be confirmed reliably.

P2A36.title: AFCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low
P2A36.plain: The sense feedback voltage from the AFCM power relay is below the expected window. Indicates the relay output stays low when the relay is commanded on.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2A37.title: AFCM Power Relay Sense Circuit High
P2A37.plain: The sense feedback voltage from the AFCM power relay is above the expected window. Indicates relay output is energised when the relay should be off, or wire shorted to B+.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2B8D.title: Intake Air O2 Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P2B8D.plain: Voltage on the intake air O2 sensor heater control line on bank 1 is below the expected window. Wire shorted to ground or heater element shorted.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2B8E.title: Intake Air O2 Sensor Heater Control Circuit High Bank 1
P2B8E.plain: Voltage on the intake air O2 sensor heater control line on bank 1 is above the expected window. Wire shorted to B+ or heater element open.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2B8F.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Temperature Sensor Circuit
P2B8F.plain: The ECM detects a circuit fault on the turbocharger/supercharger b temperature sensor. Reading cannot be used reliably for control.

P2B90.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P2B90.plain: The ECM detects a circuit low fault on the turbocharger/supercharger b temperature sensor. Reading cannot be used reliably for control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2B91.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P2B91.plain: The ECM detects a circuit high fault on the turbocharger/supercharger b temperature sensor. Reading cannot be used reliably for control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2B92.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
P2B92.plain: The ECM detects a range/performance fault on the turbocharger/supercharger b temperature sensor. Reading cannot be used reliably for control.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2B93.title: Wastegate Position Sensor A Exceeded Learning Limit
P2B93.plain: The required adaptation offset for the wastegate position sensor A exceeds the calibrated learning window. Sensor or mechanism out of nominal range.

P2B94.title: Wastegate Position Sensor B Exceeded Learning Limit
P2B94.plain: The required adaptation offset for the wastegate position sensor B exceeds the calibrated learning window. Sensor or mechanism out of nominal range.

P2B95.title: Cold Start Injection Pulse Performance
P2B95.plain: During cold start, the ECM detects that the overall injection pulse performance does not match the calibrated cold-start strategy. Combustion stability is reduced during warm-up.
causes: Injectors aged - flow drift across cylinders
Fuel rail pressure drifts during pulse

P2B96.title: Injection Pulse Performance
P2B96.plain: The ECM detects that the overall injection pulse performance does not match the calibrated values. Combustion result deviates from expected fuelling behaviour.
causes: Injectors aged - flow drift across cylinders
Fuel rail pressure drifts during pulse

P2B97.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P2B97.plain: The required adaptation offset for the exhaust pressure control valve A position exceeds the calibrated learning window. Mechanical wear or sensor drift beyond compensation.

P2B98.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Supply Low
P2B98.plain: The supply voltage to the exhaust pressure control valve A actuator is below the expected window. Fuse blown, supply wire shorted, or upstream regulator fault.

P2B99.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P2B99.plain: The output driver for the exhaust pressure control valve A reports current or junction temperature above its protection threshold. Stalled actuator or short-circuit fault.

P2B9A.title: Reductant Quality Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2B9A.plain: The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) quality sensor signal drops out or jumps intermittently. Loose connector, dilution noise, or ground reference offset.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2B9B.title: Vehicle Conditions Incorrect for Particulate Matter Sensor Regeneration
P2B9B.plain: The ECM detects that the vehicle is not operating in conditions suitable for the periodic PM sensor regeneration cycle. The sensor element cannot be cleaned and soot-mass measurement is paused.
causes: Driving cycle too short for regen conditions

P2B9C.title: Coolant Pump A Stuck/Stalled
P2B9C.plain: Coolant pump A reports a stuck/stalled condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

P2B9D.title: Coolant Pump A Supply Voltage Circuit
P2B9D.plain: Coolant pump A reports a supply voltage circuit condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

P2B9E.title: Coolant Pump A Control Module Overtemperature
P2B9E.plain: Coolant pump A reports a control module overtemperature condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.
causes: Ambient or under-bonnet temperature too high

P2B9F.title: Coolant Pump B Underspeed
P2B9F.plain: Coolant pump B reports a underspeed condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

P2BA0.title: Coolant Pump C Underspeed
P2BA0.plain: Coolant pump C reports a underspeed condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

P2BA1.title: Coolant Pump D Underspeed
P2BA1.plain: Coolant pump D reports a underspeed condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

P2BA2.title: Engine Coolant Pump Stuck/Stalled
P2BA2.plain: The engine coolant pump is mechanically stuck or has stalled. Coolant circulation through the engine is severely reduced or absent.

P2BA3.title: Starter/Generator Mechanical Performance
P2BA3.plain: The hybrid control module detects that the integrated starter/generator does not deliver the expected mechanical torque or speed for the commanded operation. Belt slippage, bearing wear, or coupling fault.

P2BA4.title: Catalyst Feedgas Performance
P2BA4.plain: The ECM detects that the exhaust gas composition reaching the catalyst (feedgas) deviates from the calibrated profile. Pre-cat O2 measurement and air-fuel control are inconsistent with engine operation.
causes: Long-term fuel trim drifted out of nominal range

P2BA5.title: Particulate Filter Feedgas Performance
P2BA5.plain: The ECM detects that the exhaust gas composition reaching the particulate filter (feedgas) deviates from the calibrated profile. Soot input rate cannot be modelled correctly, affecting regen scheduling.

P2BA6.title: NOx Exceedance - SCR NOx Catalyst Performance
P2BA6.plain: NOx emissions are above the legal threshold and the ECU isolates the cause to the SCR NOx catalyst. Conversion efficiency is degraded — aged substrate, sulphur poisoning, or thermal damage.
causes: SCR catalyst substrate aged or contaminated
Thermal damage from prior over-temperature event

P2BA7.title: NOx Exceedence - Empty Reagent Tank
P2BA7.plain: NOx emissions are above the legal threshold and the ECU isolates the cause to an empty reductant tank. SCR cannot dose AdBlue/DEF.

P2BA8.title: NOx Exceedence - Interruption of Reagent Dosing Activity
P2BA8.plain: NOx emissions are above the legal threshold and the ECU isolates the cause to interruption of reductant dosing. The injection valve, pump, or supply line is impaired.

P2BA9.title: NOx Exceedence — Insufficient Reagent
P2BA9.plain: The SCR system has detected that NOx emissions exceed the legal limit and the cause is traced to insufficient AdBlue/DEF dosing. Modern emission regulations require this fault to be reported separately so that operator-induced misuse (running an empty tank, diluting the fluid) is recorded.

P2BAA.title: NOx Sensor Range/Performance (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P2BAA.plain: The upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 returns values that are not plausible for the current operating point. NOx sensors are slow to warm up, sensitive to soot and water, and are a frequent failure on diesel SCR systems.
causes: Sensor contaminated with soot or condensate
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2BAB.title: NOx Exceedence — Reagent System Performance
P2BAB.plain: The SCR system has detected that NOx emissions exceed the legal limit and the cause is traced to a performance fault in the reagent dosing system — for example a slow dosing pump, a clogged injector, or a frozen line that is not yet caught by another DTC.

P2BAC.title: NOx Exceedence - Insufficient Reagent Quality
P2BAC.plain: The diesel exhaust aftertreatment system detects elevated NOx levels combined with abnormal reagent (AdBlue/DEF) consumption, indicating that the reagent quality is insufficient or contaminated. Many regions trigger driver inducement (limited restarts).

P2BAD.title: NOx Exceedence - Insufficient Reagent Consumption
P2BAD.plain: The aftertreatment system detects elevated NOx emissions while reagent (AdBlue/DEF) consumption is below the expected level. Causes include clogged dosing injector, incorrect dosing rate or tampering.

P2BAE.title: NOx Exceedence - EGR System
P2BAE.plain: NOx emissions are above the legal threshold and the ECU isolates the cause to the EGR system. EGR flow is too low or absent under operating conditions where NOx reduction is required.

P2BAF.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2BAF.plain: The heater sense feedback of NOx sensor 1 on bank 1 reports values that do not match expected operation. The sensor warm-up cycle does not behave as the diagnostic expects.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2BB0.title: Alternative Fuel Consumption Too Low
P2BB0.plain: The AFCM detects that alternative fuel consumption falls below the expected value for the active operating mode. Indicates injector clogging, leaks before injectors, or incorrect tank-fill correction.

P2BB1.title: Alternative Fuel Consumption Too High
P2BB1.plain: The AFCM detects that alternative fuel consumption exceeds the expected value for the active operating mode. Indicates injector leakage, fuel pressure too high, or unmetered fuel loss.

P2BB2.title: Alternative Fuel Tank Empty
P2BB2.plain: The AFCM detects that the alternative fuel tank is empty. Bi-fuel vehicles may switch to gasoline operation; mono-fuel vehicles cannot continue without refuel.

P2BB3.title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Performance
P2BB3.plain: The ECM detects that the secondary fuel pump control circuit (typically used for high-load enrichment) does not respond as expected. Pump output, relay, or driver fault.

P2BB4.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 4 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2BB5.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 5 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
